# PROJECT VISUALIZER — MASTER BUILD PLAN

> **Software digital twin:** a live, explorable model of a codebase. Developers can see its architecture, watch it run, understand its errors in plain language, and simulate changes before making them.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Plan version | 1.0 (2026-09-24) |
| Owners | Swapnil Gite (product) · Abhishek Awari (system design) |
| Scope | Full enterprise product, Phases 0–6. The MVP comes out of Phase 1 (see **MVP CHECKPOINT**) |
| Written for | Any AI model, including very small ones (TinyLlama, Qwen2.5-3B), executing **one task at a time** |
| Architecture status | Server-side parts follow the current architecture (sheet 1 + backend design). Items tagged **[ARCH-DEPENDENT]** will be updated when the new client-server design arrives |
| Contents | Part A (how to use) · Part B (reference cards R1–R16) · Phases 0–6 · Part H (when the new architecture arrives) · Part I (extending this file) · Part J (module index) |

## PART A — HOW TO USE THIS FILE

### A1. For the human who relays tasks

1. **Order of work:** Phase 0 → Phase 1 → … → Phase 6. Inside a phase, follow that phase's **Wave table**. Inside a module, do tasks **in number order**.
2. **Parallel work:** all modules listed in the same wave can be given to different models **at the same time**. They never touch the same files (see R3).
3. **What to paste to a model for one task (keep it small):**
   1. The **Model Prompt Header** (A2), unchanged.
   2. The reference cards listed in the task's **Refs:** line (only those).
   3. The **module header** of the module the task belongs to.
   4. The **task** itself.
4. **After the model answers:**
   1. Apply the files it produced, on a branch named `task/<TASK-ID>` (for example `task/P1-CORE-004`).
   2. Run the task's **Verify** command yourself. Do not trust the model's claim.
   3. If Verify passes: commit with message `<TASK-ID>: <task title>`, create the status file (R2.5), merge to `main`.
   4. If Verify fails: give the same task + the error output back to the model once. If it fails again, give it to a stronger model.
5. **BLOCKED answers:** a model replies `BLOCKED: …` when something it needs is missing. Do not force it. Check that all earlier tasks and the modules in **Starts after** are merged, then retry.
6. **[ARCH-DEPENDENT] tasks:** you can build them now; they may be revised when the new architecture arrives (see Part H).
7. **Never** let a model "fix" a file that belongs to another module. If a bug is in another module's file, add a note in `docs/status/bugs/<TASK-ID>-bug.md` and fix it as a new task inside the owning module.

### A2. Model Prompt Header (paste above every task, unchanged)

```text
You are implementing ONE task of the Project Visualizer build plan.
RULES:
1. Do exactly what the task says. Nothing more, nothing less.
2. Only create or edit the files listed in the task's "Files:" line. Never touch any other file.
3. Use the exact names, paths, function signatures, JSON field names and texts given. Do not rename, reorder, or "improve" them.
4. If a file, function, or type the task relies on does not exist, or any step is unclear, STOP and reply only: BLOCKED: <reason>.
5. Do not add libraries or packages unless the task explicitly says so.
6. If the task has a Test, write the test first, then the code, then run the Verify command.
7. Keep code simple: no clever tricks, no extra features, no unused code, no TODO comments.
8. Reply with: (a) the complete content of every file you created or changed,
   (b) the output of the Verify command, (c) one final line: DONE <TASK-ID>  or  FAILED <TASK-ID>: <reason>.
```

### A3. How a module and a task look

```text
### MODULE P1-CORE — Core types and utilities
- Type: CODE | DEPS | DOCS            (DEPS = may edit shared manifest files, see R3.4)
- Lane: ENGINE | DESKTOP | SERVER | AI | AGENT | VSCODE | INFRA | CONTRACTS | DOCS | BUSINESS | WEB
- Owns: `engine/modules/core/**`      (the ONLY paths this module's tasks may create/edit)
- Starts after: P1-EBOOT              (modules that must be fully merged first)
- Goal: one paragraph

#### P1-CORE-004 — Node id helpers
**Files:** `path/a.hpp` (create) · `path/a.cpp` (create) · `path/a_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R6, R7
**Why:** what this task is for, in plain words.
**Steps:** numbered, exact instructions.
**Test:** exact test cases (input → expected output).
**Verify:** exact command → expected result.
```

- `(create)` = the file must not exist yet. `(edit)` = the file exists (made by an earlier task of the **same module**) and must be changed only as described.
- A task implicitly depends on the **previous task of the same module**. Extra dependencies are written as **Needs:**.
- `[MVP]` tag = the task is needed for the MVP checkpoint. `[POST-MVP]` = after the checkpoint. `[ARCH-DEPENDENT]` = may change with the new architecture.

## PART B — REFERENCE CARDS (R1–R16)

Each card is short so it can be pasted into a small model's context together with one task.

### R1. Product summary (card)

- **What:** A desktop software that turns any codebase (folder, Git repo, code snippet) into an interactive 2D/3D "digital twin".
- **Zoom = abstraction, not camera:** Project → Packages (folders) → Modules (files) → Classes → Functions/Methods → Statements. "Zooming in" means moving **down this stack**.
- **Layers on top of the static structure:**
  1. *Runtime overlay* — watch requests/data move between modules live; see where it stalls, loops, or breaks.
  2. *AI layer* — explains errors and code in plain language, answers questions, analyzes impact of changes.
  3. *Prediction & simulation* — "what if" changes in a sandbox, health forecasting, recommendations with confidence.
- **Principles:** one phase = one mission · one owner per capability (and per file) · no overlap · the MVP emerges from the build.
- **Languages:** Python first, then JS/TS, Java, Go, C/C++, Rust, C#, then any language via plugins.

### R2. Workflow card: branches, commits, status, verification

1. **Branch per task:** `task/<TASK-ID>` created from latest `main`.
2. **Commit message:** `<TASK-ID>: <task title>` (example: `P1-CORE-004: Node id helpers`).
3. **Merge:** fast-forward or squash into `main` only after Verify passes.
4. **Never** commit: `node_modules/`, build outputs, `.env` files, secrets, API keys.
5. **Status file:** after merge, create `docs/status/done/<TASK-ID>.md` containing exactly 3 lines:
   ```text
   task: <TASK-ID>
   date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
   verify: passed
   ```
   Every task has its own status file, so parallel models never collide.
6. **Bug notes** go to `docs/status/bugs/<TASK-ID>-bug.md` (one file per note).
7. All paths in this plan are **relative to the repository root** `project-visualizer/` unless stated otherwise.
8. All commands are run from the repository root in **Git Bash** (Windows) or bash (Linux/macOS), unless the Verify line starts with `cd <dir> &&`.

### R3. Ownership and NO-OVERLAP rules (card)

1. **One owner per path.** Every file in the repository belongs to exactly one module (its **Owns** list). Only tasks of that module may create or edit it.
2. **Tasks only touch their Files line.** Reading other files is allowed; writing is not.
3. **Auto-discovery instead of shared lists.** New code registers itself by *existing in a known folder*; nobody edits a central list:
   - Engine C++ modules: any folder `engine/modules/<name>/` with a `CMakeLists.txt` is added automatically; any `src/register.cpp` is called automatically (R8).
   - Engine third-party libraries: any `engine/third_party/<name>/CMakeLists.txt` is added automatically.
   - Desktop main-process IPC handlers: any `desktop/src/main/handlers/*.ts` is loaded automatically (R10).
   - Desktop renderer features: any `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/<name>/register.ts(x)` is loaded automatically (R10).
   - Desktop graph renderers: any `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/<name>/index.ts` is loaded automatically.
   - Desktop AI providers: any `desktop/src/main/ai-providers/<name>/index.ts` is loaded automatically.
   - Python AI routers: any `ai/pv_ai/features/<name>/router.py` is loaded automatically (R11).
   - Server gateway routes: any `server/services/<svc>/gateway-route.json` is loaded automatically (R13).
   - Docker compose: any `infra/compose/compose.<name>.yml` is included automatically by `infra/compose/up.sh`.
   - Prometheus targets: any `infra/observability/prometheus/targets/<svc>.json` is loaded automatically.
   - Database migrations: any `server/db/migrations/<NNNN>_<module>_<name>.sql` is applied in filename order. Every migration filename is fixed in this plan.
4. **Shared manifest exception (the ONLY allowed shared files):** these files may be edited by more than one module, but **only by modules of Type DEPS**, and DEPS modules of the same manifest never run in parallel (they are in different phases):
   - `desktop/package.json`, `desktop/pnpm-lock.yaml`
   - `ai/pyproject.toml`, `ai/uv.lock`
5. **Generated files are never committed** (build outputs, caches). They are ignored by `.gitignore` (made in P0-REPO).
6. **Status and bug note files** (R2.5, R2.6) are exempt: each task writes its own uniquely named file.
7. **If two tasks ever seem to need the same file, the plan is wrong.** Stop and report it; do not improvise.

### R6. Naming conventions (card)

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| C++ namespace | `pv::<module>` | `pv::core`, `pv::graph` |
| C++ types | PascalCase | `NodeKind`, `LevelView` |
| C++ functions/variables | snake_case | `make_node_id`, `file_path` |
| C++ private members | snake_case + trailing `_` | `nodes_` |
| C++ enum values | PascalCase | `NodeKind::Function` |
| C++ files | snake_case `.hpp` / `.cpp`; tests `<name>_test.cpp` | `ids.hpp`, `ids_test.cpp` |
| GoogleTest suite names | PascalCase `<Module><Topic>` | `CoreIds`, `GraphStore` |
| TypeScript types/components | PascalCase | `GraphNode`, `InspectorPanel` |
| TypeScript functions/variables | camelCase | `getLevelView` |
| TypeScript files | kebab-case `.ts`/`.tsx`; tests `<name>.test.ts(x)` next to the file | `level-view.ts` |
| Python | modules/functions snake_case, classes PascalCase, tests `test_<name>.py` | `explain_node.py` |
| JSON fields (all contracts, RPC, HTTP, events) | **snake_case** | `project_id`, `node_id` |
| RPC method names | `<namespace>.<verb_or_noun>` snake_case | `graph.level_view` |
| Desktop IPC channels | `pv:<area>.<action>` camelCase action | `pv:ai.explainNode` |
| Env variables | `PV_<AREA>_<NAME>` uppercase | `PV_ENGINE_PATH` |
| Paths inside graph data | relative to project root, forward slashes `/`, no leading `./` | `src/app/main.py` |

### R7. Domain model (card) — the heart of the system

**NodeKind** (string form in JSON in brackets):
`Project ("project")`, `Package ("package")`, `Module ("module")`, `Class ("class")`, `Function ("function")`, `Method ("method")`, `Variable ("variable")`, `Statement ("statement")`, `External ("external")`.

**Level** (abstraction level, integer): Project=0 · Package=1 · External=1 · Module=2 · Class=3 · Function=4 · Method=4 · Variable=5 · Statement=5.

**EdgeKind:** `Imports ("imports")`, `Calls ("calls")`, `Inherits ("inherits")`, `References ("references")`.
Containment is **not** an edge: it is expressed by `parent_id`.

**Health:** `Unknown ("unknown")` < `Ok ("ok")` < `Warning ("warning")` < `Stalled ("stalled")` < `Error ("error")` (severity order, used for propagation: parent = worst child).

**Node JSON:**
```json
{
  "id": "function:src/app/main.py#run",
  "kind": "function",
  "name": "run",
  "qualified_name": "app.main.run",
  "file_path": "src/app/main.py",
  "language": "python",
  "span": {"start_line": 3, "start_col": 0, "end_line": 9, "end_col": 12},
  "level": 4,
  "parent_id": "module:src/app/main.py",
  "metrics": {"loc": 7, "complexity": 2, "fan_in": 1, "fan_out": 3},
  "health": "unknown"
}
```
- `span`: lines are **1-based**, columns **0-based**. All zero = unknown (project/package/external nodes).
- `file_path` is `""` for project, package and external nodes.
- `qualified_name` = language-level full name (Python: dotted module path + "." + in-file qualname).

**Edge JSON:**
```json
{"id": "calls|function:src/a.py#f|function:src/b.py#g", "kind": "calls",
 "source_id": "function:src/a.py#f", "target_id": "function:src/b.py#g",
 "weight": 2, "resolved": true}
```
- `weight` = how many times this relation occurs (two calls from f to g → weight 2).
- Aggregated edges in level views use id `agg|<kind>|<source_id>|<target_id>`.

**Node ID format (exact):**

| Kind | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| project | `project:` | `project:` |
| package | `package:<dir>` | `package:src/app` |
| module | `module:<file>` | `module:src/app/main.py` |
| class, function, method, variable | `<kind>:<file>#<in-file qualname>` | `method:src/app/main.py#App.start` |
| statement | `statement:<file>#<in-file qualname>@<line>` | `statement:src/app/main.py#run@5` |
| external | `external:<top-level name>` | `external:numpy` |

- *In-file qualname* = names of enclosing classes/functions joined by `.` (example `Outer.Inner.method`).
- If the same in-file qualname appears twice in one file, the 2nd gets suffix `~2`, the 3rd `~3`, … (example `helper~2`).
- **Package nodes:** every directory (relative to root) that contains at least one supported source file, directly or in any sub-directory, becomes a package node. The root directory itself is the project node (not a package).
- **Parents:** package → parent package or `project:`; module → its directory's package or `project:`; top-level class/function → module; method → class; nested def → enclosing def; external → `project:`.

### R8. Engine architecture (card)

**Layers (a module may only depend on modules in lower layers):**

| Layer | Modules |
|---|---|
| 0 | `core` (types, ids, paths, errors, JSON, logging, text utils) |
| 1 | `graph` (store, level views, span index) · `fs` (file discovery) · `fswatch` (native file change events, P4) · `rpc` (JSON-RPC framing, method table, CLI table) · `parse` (tree-sitter wrapper, adapter interface, raw extraction types, registry, project index) |
| 2 | `lang_*` (language adapters) · `builder` (raw extraction → graph) |
| 3 | `session` (projects, background loading, Registry struct) |
| 4 | feature modules: `graphapi`, `impact`, `context`, `search`, `analysis`, `deps`, `runtime`, `modtrace`, `health`, `errmap`, `rtsync`, `incremental`, `fixsync`, `change`, `grounding`, `mcp`, `plugins`, `ipc`, `cache`, `layout`, `gdiff`, `metrics`, `sim` |
| 5 | `app` (executable `pv-engine`) |

**Module folder:** `engine/modules/<m>/CMakeLists.txt` contains exactly one call: `pv_add_module(NAME <m> DEPS <targets...>)`. Library target = `pv_<m>`. Sources = all `src/*.cpp` (auto). Public headers in `include/pv/<m>/`. Tests = all `tests/*_test.cpp` (auto) → executable `pv_<m>_tests`. Test fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`, reachable in test code through the macro `PV_TEST_FIXTURES` (a string literal path).

**Registration:** a module that exposes RPC methods, CLI commands or language adapters has `src/register.cpp` defining exactly:
```cpp
#include "pv/session/registry.hpp"
void pv_register_<m>(pv::session::Registry& reg) { /* add methods / adapters / cli commands */ }
```
(global namespace, `<m>` = module folder name). The build generates a file calling every such function (alphabetical order). Nobody edits a central list.

**Registry struct** (defined in `session`):
```cpp
namespace pv::session {
struct Registry {
  pv::rpc::MethodTable& methods;     // add("graph.node", handler)
  pv::rpc::CliTable& cli;            // add("analyze", command)
  ProjectManager& projects;          // open/get projects
  pv::parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters;  // add(std::make_unique<PythonAdapter>())
  pv::rpc::Notifier& notifier;       // notify("project.progress", params)
  std::function<void()> request_shutdown;  // ends the stdio loop after the current response
};
}
```

**Errors:** throw `pv::core::PvError(code, message)`. The RPC layer turns it into a JSON-RPC error. Codes are in R9.

**Threading:** the RPC loop handles one request at a time on the main thread (in `serve` mode, P4-EIPC, every connection has its own reader thread but all requests pass one dispatch lock, so handlers still run one at a time). Long work (project loading) runs on a background `std::thread`. Every `Project` has a `std::shared_mutex`; readers take `std::shared_lock`, the loader takes `std::unique_lock` only when swapping in the finished graph.

**Build commands (from `engine/`):** configure `cmake --preset dev` · build `cmake --build --preset dev` · all tests `ctest --preset dev` · some tests `ctest --preset dev -R <SuiteName>`. On Linux/macOS use preset `dev-unix` instead of `dev`.

### R9. Engine RPC protocol + full method registry (card)

**Transport:** the desktop app starts `pv-engine` as a child process. Messages go over stdin/stdout using LSP-style framing:
```text
Content-Length: <number of bytes of the JSON body>\r\n
\r\n
<JSON body, UTF-8>
```
Logs go to **stderr only** (never stdout).

**Local server mode (new architecture, Phase 4, P4-EIPC):** `pv-engine serve` accepts several local clients at once with the same framing and messages:
- the **desktop app** over a **named pipe** `\\.\pipe\pv-engine-<user>-<desktop pid>` (Windows) or a **Unix socket** `<tmp>/pv-engine-<user>-<desktop pid>.sock` (macOS/Linux) — only the same OS user can connect;
- the **VS Code extension** and other local tools over **TCP `127.0.0.1:7700`** (7701–7709 if busy). The first request on TCP must be `engine.hello {token, client}`; the token and the chosen port are in `~/.project-visualizer/engine.json` `{pid, version, pipe, tcp_port, token}` (readable only by the user, deleted when the engine exits).
- Notifications go to **every** connected client. stdio stays for the CLI, tests and as the desktop's fallback.

**Messages:** JSON-RPC 2.0. Request `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"graph.node","params":{...}}` → response `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"result":{...}}` or `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32002,"message":"node not found: x"}}`. Notification (engine → app, no id): `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"project.progress","params":{...}}`.

**Error codes:** `-32700` parse error · `-32600` invalid request · `-32601` method not found · `-32602` invalid params · `-32603` internal error · `-32001` project not found · `-32002` node not found · `-32003` project not ready · `-32004` I/O error · `-32005` unsupported · `-32006` cancelled · `-32007` conflict.

**Method registry (all phases).** Schema files live in `contracts/rpc/<namespace>/<method>.params.schema.json` and `.result.schema.json`.

| Method | Params (JSON) | Result (JSON) | Handler module | Schema module |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine.ping` | `{}` | `{version, protocol}` (protocol = 1) | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| `engine.shutdown` | `{}` | `{ok:true}` then process exits | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| `engine.hello` | `{token?, client: 'desktop'\|'vscode'\|'tool'}` | `{version, client_id}` | P4-EIPC | P4-CRPC |
| `engine.info` | `{}` | `{version, pid, pipe, tcp_port, clients:[{client_id, client, transport}]}` | P4-EIPC | P4-CRPC |
| `editor.reveal` / notif `editor.reveal` | `{file_path, line, column?}` | `{delivered}` (sent to the other clients) | P4-EIPC | P4-CRPC |
| `editor.open` / notif `editor.open` | `{file_path, line}` | `{delivered}` (sent to `vscode` clients) | P4-EIPC | P4-CRPC |
| `lang.list` | `{}` | `{languages:[{id, extensions[]}]}` | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| `project.open` | `{root_path, exclude_globs?[]}` | `{project_id}` | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| `project.status` | `{project_id}` | `{project_id, root_path, state, files_total, files_done, error_message}` | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| `project.close` | `{project_id}` | `{ok:true}` | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| notif `project.progress` | `{project_id, state, files_total, files_done}` | — | P1-SESS | P1-CRPC |
| `graph.node` | `{project_id, node_id}` | `Node` | P1-GAPI | P1-CRPC |
| `graph.children` | `{project_id, node_id}` | `{nodes:Node[]}` | P1-GAPI | P1-CRPC |
| `graph.level_view` | `{project_id, parent_id?}` | `{parent:Node, nodes:Node[], edges:Edge[]}` | P1-GAPI | P1-CRPC |

### R10. Desktop architecture (card)

**Processes:** Electron *main* (Node.js: windows, engine child process, files, network, secrets) · *preload* (safe bridge) · *renderer* (React UI, no Node access, `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`).

**Bridge `window.pv`** (defined once in P1-DPRE, never changed). Every call returns an **envelope**; the renderer's `api/bridge.ts` (P1-DAPI) unwraps it and throws `ApiError` on failure:
```ts
export type Envelope<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: { code: string | number; message: string } };
export interface PvBridge {
  rpc(method: string, params?: unknown): Promise<Envelope<unknown>>;          // → engine
  invoke(channel: string, payload?: unknown): Promise<Envelope<unknown>>;     // → main handler; channel must start with "pv:"
  onNotification(cb: (method: string, params: unknown) => void): () => void;  // engine notifications; returns unsubscribe
  on(channel: string, cb: (payload: unknown) => void): () => void;            // main → renderer events; channel starts with "pv:"
}
```

**Main handlers:** each file `desktop/src/main/handlers/<name>.ts` has `export default function register(ctx: MainContext): void`. `MainContext` (P1-DMAIN, `desktop/src/main/core/context.ts`):
```ts
export interface MainContext {
  handle(channel: string, fn: (payload: unknown) => unknown | Promise<unknown>): void; // wraps ipcMain.handle
  send(channel: string, payload: unknown): void;       // to the renderer window
  engine: EngineService;                                 // request(method, params), onNotification(cb), status
  settings: SettingsStore;                               // get(key, fallback), set(key, value)
  secrets: SecretStore;                                  // set(name, value), get(name), has(name), delete(name)
  getWindow(): Electron.BrowserWindow | null;
  log: (level: 'info' | 'warn' | 'error', msg: string, extra?: unknown) => void;
}
```

**Renderer feature registry** (P1-DSHELL, `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/registry.ts`): each `features/<name>/register.ts(x)` has `export default function register(app: AppRegistry): void`. `AppRegistry` methods: `addPanel(PanelDef)` (areas `left`, `center`, `right`, `bottom`), `addCommand(CommandDef)`, `addNodeAction(NodeActionDef)`, `addSettingsSection(SettingsSectionDef)`, `addStatusItem(StatusItemDef)`, `addScreen(ScreenDef)`, `addToolbarItem(ToolbarItemDef)`, `addWelcomeAction(WelcomeActionDef)`, `addGlobal(GlobalDef)` (always-mounted components such as dialogs and watchers). Features may **import and call** exported functions/stores of other features (e.g. `revealNode`, `useImpactStore`) but never edit their files.

**Core store** (Zustand, `core/store.ts`, P1-DSHELL): `screen`, `projectId`, `projectRoot`, `projectState`, `currentParentId`, `selectedNodeId`, `hoveredNodeId`, `viewMode ('2d'|'3d')`, `focusNodeId`, `overlays: Record<string, Overlay>`, `graphVersion` (number; call `bumpGraphVersion()` when graph data changes), `settingsOpen`, `activePanel` per area + actions (`openedProject`, `closedProject`, `setParent`, `select`, `hover`, `setFocus`, `setViewMode`, `setOverlay`, `bumpGraphVersion`, `setSettingsOpen`, `showPanel`).

**Overlays** (render-agnostic highlighting used by impact, runtime, health, simulation, forecast…):
```ts
export interface NodeStyle { color?: string; borderColor?: string; badge?: string; pulse?: boolean; opacity?: number; }
export interface EdgeStyle { color?: string; width?: number; animated?: boolean; opacity?: number; }
export interface Overlay { priority: number; nodes: Record<string, NodeStyle>; edges: Record<string, EdgeStyle>; dimOthers?: boolean; }
```
Higher `priority` wins. A feature sets its overlay with `setOverlay('<feature-id>', overlay)` and removes it with `setOverlay('<feature-id>', null)`.

**Renderers:** `renderers/<name>/index.ts` exports `export const renderer: RendererEntry = { mode: '2d' | '3d', create: () => GraphRenderer }`. `GraphRenderer` interface is defined in `view/renderer-types.ts` (P1-DVIEW). Several renderers may exist per mode (P1-DVIEW-008): the setting `view.renderer2d` / `view.renderer3d` names one by its `id` (default = folder name), else the entry with `preferred: true` wins, else the first. An entry with `layout: 'engine'` receives positions from `layout.compute` in `ViewGraph.positions`. New architecture: `rf2d` (React Flow + D3, P4-DRF2D) and `r3f` (React Three Fiber, P4-DR3F) are preferred; `cy2d` and `fg3d` stay as the "Classic" choice.

**Engine connection (new architecture):** the main process starts `pv-engine serve --pipe <name> --tcp 7700 --parent-pid <pid>` and talks over the named pipe / Unix socket (P1-DENG-008); if that fails it falls back to stdio. The renderer never sees the difference.

**Commands (from `desktop/`):** install `pnpm install` · dev `pnpm dev` · tests `pnpm test` (all) or `pnpm vitest run <path-or-pattern>` · types `pnpm typecheck` · lint `pnpm lint` · build `pnpm build`.

**Renderer tests** start with the line `// @vitest-environment jsdom`. Main-process tests run in the default Node environment.

### R11. AI architecture (card)

- **MVP (Phase 1):** desktop main process calls the LLM **directly** with the user's own API key (Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible URL, e.g. local Ollama). The key is encrypted with Electron `safeStorage`.
- **Phase 4+:** optional *cloud mode*: desktop → server `ai-gateway` (HTTPS) → Python AI service → LLM provider. Direct mode stays: it is the only AI path with no account and no server (founder decision D1, 2026-09-26).
- **Streaming (new architecture):** cloud answers can stream back as Server-Sent Events: `event: delta` with `{"text": "…"}` chunks, then one `event: done` whose data is the normal JSON response (citations cleaned), or `event: error` with `{"error":{code,message}}` (schema `contracts/http/ai/stream_event.schema.json`).
- **Provider fallback:** the Python LLM gateway calls `PV_AI_PROVIDER`; on provider errors, rate limits or timeouts it retries once with `PV_AI_FALLBACK_PROVIDER` (for example Anthropic ↔ OpenAI) when configured.
- **Vector store:** Qdrant by default (local dev and on-prem); a Pinecone adapter is used when `PV_AI_VECTOR_STORE=pinecone` (hosted cloud only).
- **Grounding rule:** the LLM only receives facts built by the engine (`context.for_node`, `grounding.*`). Prompts require citations in the form `[[node:<node_id>]]`. Citations are validated against real node ids; invalid ones are removed before showing.
- **Prompt templates:** Markdown files with `{{variable}}` placeholders in `contracts/prompts/v1/` (P1-PROMPT) and `contracts/prompts/v2/` (P4-PROMPT). A template starts with a `SYSTEM:` section and a `USER:` section separated by a line `---`.
- **Python AI service:** package `pv_ai`, FastAPI app `pv_ai.app:app`, port `8200`, routers auto-loaded from `pv_ai/features/*/router.py`, settings from env vars `PV_AI_*`.

### R12. Runtime event and agent protocol (card)

**Event JSON (v1):**
```json
{"v":1, "event_id":"uuid4", "trace_id":"32 hex", "span_id":"16 hex", "parent_span_id":"16 hex or null",
 "kind":"call|http_in|http_out|db_query|message|error|stall|log",
 "name":"app.users.get_user", "file_path":"C:/code/app/users.py", "line":42,
 "start_ns":1790000000000000000, "duration_ns":1200000, "status":"ok|error",
 "error":{"type":"ValueError","message":"bad id","stack":"Traceback ..."} or null,
 "attrs":{"http.method":"GET","http.route":"/users/{id}","http.status_code":200,"db.system":"postgresql","db.statement":"SELECT ..."},
 "service":"my-app", "pid":1234, "thread":"MainThread"}
```
**Batch upload:** `POST http://127.0.0.1:47100/v1/events`, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, body `{"source":{"agent":"python","version":"0.1.0","service":"my-app","project_root":"C:/code/app"},"events":[...]}` → `{"accepted": n}`. The desktop app (P3-DHUB) receives it and forwards to the engine with `runtime.ingest`.
**OTLP:** the same hub accepts OTLP/HTTP JSON traces at `POST /v1/traces` (any OpenTelemetry-instrumented language) and converts spans to events.
**Ports:** runtime hub `47100` · engine TCP `7700` for the VS Code extension and local tools (token, P4-EIPC) · VS Code bridge WebSocket `47101` (fallback when the engine port is not available). All bind to `127.0.0.1` only.

**Team runtime upload (new architecture, opt-in per project, P3-DRTUP):** every **5 s** the desktop sends aggregates — never raw events — to the runtime aggregation service: `POST /api/runtime/metrics` (JWT) with `{cloud_project_id, window_end_ms, window_ms, nodes:[{node_id, calls, errors, error_rate, p95_ms, state}], errors:[{type, node_id, count}]}` (values taken from `health.get` and `errors.list`). Arguments, SQL text, stack traces and file contents are never uploaded.

### R13. Server architecture (card) [ARCH-DEPENDENT]

**New client-server architecture (applied 2026-09-26, Part H):** the desktop does all parsing, graph, impact, health and runtime work; the server only keeps identity, teams, billing, the AI proxy, optional sync and team runtime dashboards. Source code never leaves the user's machine. Services are separate processes grouped on four instances (sizing for 200 users from `docs/architecture/incoming/scaling-summary.md`):

| Group (instance) | Service | Folder | Port | Module |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. API gateway + auth & teams (2 vCPU / 4 GB) | Nginx (TLS, load balancer, public port 443) | `infra/nginx/` | 80/443 | P2-SGW |
| A | gateway (rate limit, auth check, routing) | `server/services/gateway` | 8080 | P2-SGW |
| A | realtime (WebSocket: team sync + notifications) | `server/services/realtime` | 8106 | P3-SRT |
| A | auth (JWT, sessions, OAuth) | `server/services/auth` | 8101 | P2-SAUTH |
| A | projects (teams & permissions: orgs, members, projects) | `server/services/projects` | 8102 | P2-SPROJ |
| A | billing (Stripe) | `server/services/billing` | 8107 | P6-SBILL |
| A | licensing (plans, entitlements) | `server/services/licensing` | 8108 | P6-SLIC |
| A | sso (OIDC) | `server/services/sso` | 8111 | P6-SSSO |
| A | audit | `server/services/audit` | 8110 | P6-SAUDIT |
| A | feedback (in-app feedback) | `server/services/feedback` | 8113 | P6-SFEED |
| B. AI gateway + sync (4 vCPU / 8 GB) | ai-gateway (AI queue, quotas, cache, SSE stream relay) | `server/services/ai-gateway` | 8104 | P4-SAIGW |
| B | ml-gateway | `server/services/ml-gateway` | 8109 | P5-SMLGW |
| B | sync (snapshots, diff & merge, share & export) | `server/services/sync` | 8103 | P2-SSYNC |
| C. Python AI (4 vCPU / 16 GB, no GPU) | Python AI/ML service (LLM gateway, embeddings, ML models) | `ai/` | 8200 | P4-AI*, P5-ML* |
| D. Runtime aggregation (2 vCPU / 4 GB + TimescaleDB) | runtime-agg (aggregator, time series, alert engine) | `server/services/runtime-agg` | 8105 | P3-SRTAGG |

**Removed by the new architecture:** collector (P3-SCOLL → P3-SRTAGG), ingest and parse-worker (P3-SING, P3-SPW → Git import runs on the desktop, P3-DCIMP). Their modules are marked SUPERSEDED and were never built.

**Stores (dev ports):** PostgreSQL 5432 (users, teams, projects, billing, audit) · TimescaleDB **5433** (runtime metrics) · Redis 6379 (sessions, queues, AI cache, notifications pub/sub) · MongoDB 27017 (shared graph snapshots) · MinIO 9000 (console 9001; S3 API: exports, reports, shared snapshots) · Qdrant 6333 · Prometheus 9090 · Grafana **3001** (3000 is often busy) · Jaeger UI 16686 / OTLP HTTP 4318 · Elasticsearch 9200 · Kibana 5601.

**Desktop ↔ server:** HTTPS through the gateway for auth, sync, AI requests and runtime upload; AI answers may stream back as SSE; team notifications arrive over WSS (`/api/realtime/ws`, Redis channels `pv:notify:<cloud_project_id>`).

**Common env vars:** `PV_ENV` (dev|test|prod) · `PV_LOG_LEVEL` · `PV_PG_URL` · `PV_TSDB_URL` (runtime-agg only) · `PV_REDIS_URL` · `PV_MONGO_URL` · `PV_S3_ENDPOINT` · `PV_S3_ACCESS_KEY` · `PV_S3_SECRET_KEY` · `PV_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH` · `PV_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` (auth only) · `PV_OTLP_URL`.

**Packages:** every library (`server/libs/<lib>`) and service (`server/services/<svc>`) is an **independent pnpm project** with its own `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` (no workspace). Services depend on libraries with the `link:` protocol, e.g. `"@pv/common": "link:../../libs/common"`. Libraries use structural (duck-typed) parameter types instead of importing Fastify types, so two copies of a dependency never clash.

**Service skeleton (every service):** `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` (extends `../../tsconfig.base.json`), `.env.example`, `src/index.ts` (start), `src/app.ts` (`buildApp(deps)` returns a Fastify instance — tests use `app.inject` with in-memory fakes), `src/config.ts` (zod-validated env), `src/routes/*.ts`, `gateway-route.json`, `Dockerfile`, tests `src/**/*.test.ts` (Vitest). Health endpoints `GET /healthz` → `{"ok":true}` and `GET /metrics` (Prometheus text). Build = one bundled file `dist/index.js` made by esbuild (see `server/docs/service-template.md`, P2-SBASE).

**Gateway route file** `server/services/<svc>/gateway-route.json`: `{"prefix":"/api/auth","upstream_env":"PV_AUTH_URL","auth_required":false,"rate_limit_per_min":120}`.

**Queues (BullMQ on Redis):** `pv-ai` (ai-gateway) · `pv-ml` (ml-gateway). (`pv-parse` and `pv-runtime` belonged to the removed parse-worker and collector; the names stay reserved in `@pv/queue`.)

### R14. Testing and verification (card)

| Lane | Framework | Test location | Run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engine | GoogleTest + CTest | `engine/modules/<m>/tests/*_test.cpp` | `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R <Suite>` |
| Desktop | Vitest (+ Testing Library, jsdom) | next to source: `*.test.ts(x)` | `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run <path>` |
| Server | Vitest + `fastify.inject` | `server/services/<svc>/src/**/*.test.ts`, `server/libs/<lib>/src/**/*.test.ts` | `cd server/services/<svc> && pnpm test` (libraries: `cd server/libs/<lib> && pnpm test`) |
| AI (Python) | pytest | `ai/tests/<feature>/test_*.py` | `cd ai && uv run pytest tests/<feature> -q` |
| Agents (Python) | pytest | `agents/python/tests/test_*.py` | `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q` |
| Agents (Node) | Vitest | `agents/node/src/**/*.test.ts` | `cd agents/node && pnpm test` |
| VS Code ext | Vitest (pure logic) | `vscode-extension/src/**/*.test.ts` | `cd vscode-extension && pnpm test` |
| Contracts | ajv (schema + examples) | `contracts/rpc/<ns>/examples/*.json` | `cd contracts && pnpm validate` |
| Docs tasks | human check | — | open the file; confirm every heading listed in the task exists |

**Test rules:** tests must be deterministic (no network, no real LLM, no clock-dependent sleeps > 100 ms). Use fakes given in the task.

### R15. Errors and logging (card)

- **Engine:** throw `pv::core::PvError(code, message)`; log with `pv::core::log_info/log_warn/log_error(message)` → stderr, format `[pv-engine] <LEVEL> <message>`.
- **Desktop main:** use `ctx.log(level, msg, extra)`; never `console.log` in committed code except inside the logger.
- **Renderer:** show user-facing errors with `notify.error(title, detail)` from `core/notify.ts` (P1-DSHELL); never crash the whole UI (feature panels are wrapped in an error boundary).
- **Server:** Fastify logger (pino) JSON logs; errors return `{"error":{"code":"<string>","message":"<text>"}}` with a correct HTTP status.
- **Python:** `logging` module, JSON formatter from `pv_ai.core.logging`; errors return the same JSON error shape as the server.
- **Never log:** API keys, passwords, tokens, full source code of user files.

### R16. Glossary (card)

- **Digital twin:** the live model (graph + runtime + AI) of a codebase.
- **Level view:** the children of one node plus the aggregated edges between them. It is what the canvas shows.
- **Drill down / up:** move one level deeper / higher in the abstraction stack.
- **Overlay:** extra colors/badges/animations on top of the graph (impact, runtime, health, simulation).
- **Context pack / grounding pack:** facts from the engine given to the LLM so it cannot invent things.
- **Hotspot:** a node with unusually high complexity, size, or coupling.
- **Module crossing:** a runtime call that goes from one module (file) into another.
- **Sandbox:** a copy-on-write copy of the graph where "what-if" changes are applied without touching the real project.
- **DEPS module:** a module that is allowed to edit shared manifest files (R3.4).
- **Wave:** a group of modules that can be built at the same time.

### MODULE P0-REPO — Repository skeleton

#### P0-ENV-003 — Environment check script
**Files:** `scripts/env/check_env.sh` (create)
**Refs:** R5
**Why:** one command proves a machine has every required tool at the right version.
**Steps:**
1. Create the file with exactly this content:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks that all Project Visualizer development tools are installed.
# Usage: bash scripts/env/check_env.sh
FAIL=0

ver_ge() { # usage: ver_ge <have> <need>  -> returns 0 if have >= need
  [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$2" "$1" | sort -V | head -n1)" = "$2" ]
}

check() { # usage: check <name> <min_version> <command...>
  local name="$1" need="$2"; shift 2
  local out
  if ! out=$("$@" 2>&1); then
    echo "FAIL  $name: not found"; FAIL=1; return
  fi
  local have
  have=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' | head -n1)
  if ver_ge "$have" "$need"; then
    echo "PASS  $name $have (need >= $need)"
  else
    echo "FAIL  $name $have (need >= $need)"; FAIL=1
  fi
}

check git 2.40 git --version
check node 22.0 node --version
check pnpm 10.0 pnpm --version
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then PY=python3; else PY=python; fi
check python 3.12 $PY --version
check uv 0.4 uv --version
check cmake 3.28 cmake --version

if command -v cl >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -d "/c/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft Visual Studio/2022/BuildTools/VC" ] || [ -d "/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/2022" ]; then
  echo "PASS  C++ compiler (MSVC 2022 found)"
elif command -v g++ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  check g++ 12.0 g++ --version
elif command -v clang++ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  check clang++ 16.0 clang++ --version
else
  echo "FAIL  C++ compiler: none found"; FAIL=1
fi

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "PASS  docker (needed from Phase 2)"
else
  echo "WARN  docker not found (needed from Phase 2)"
fi

if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then echo "ALL REQUIRED TOOLS OK"; else echo "SOME TOOLS MISSING"; exit 1; fi
```
**Verify:** `bash scripts/env/check_env.sh; echo "exit=$?"` → last lines show `ALL REQUIRED TOOLS OK` and `exit=0` on a ready machine.

#### P0-TOOLS-003 — Plan overlap linter
**Files:** `scripts/plan/plan_lint.py` (create)
**Refs:** R3
**Why:** machine-check that no two modules own the same file and no task writes outside its module.
**Steps:**
1. Create the file with exactly this content:
```python
"""Checks the build plan for ownership overlaps. Usage: python scripts/plan/plan_lint.py docs/plan/PROJECT_VISUALIZER_BUILD_PLAN.md"""
import re
import sys

MANIFESTS = {"desktop/package.json", "desktop/pnpm-lock.yaml", "ai/pyproject.toml", "ai/uv.lock"}


def glob_to_re(g):
    out, i = "", 0
    while i < len(g):
        if g[i:i + 3] == "**/":
            out += "(?:.*/)?"; i += 3
        elif g[i:i + 2] == "**":
            out += ".*"; i += 2
        elif g[i] == "*":
            out += "[^/]*"; i += 1
        else:
            out += re.escape(g[i]); i += 1
    return re.compile("^" + out + "$")


def main(path):
    lines = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    modules, order, tasks, errors = {}, [], {}, []
    cur, fence = None, None
    for n, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        st = line.lstrip()
        if fence is None and (st.startswith("```") or st.startswith("~~~")):
            fence = st[:3]; continue
        if fence is not None:
            if st.startswith(fence): fence = None
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^### MODULE (P\d-[A-Z0-9]+) — (.+)$", line)
        if m:
            cur = {"id": m.group(1), "type": None, "owns": [], "tasks": []}
            if cur["id"] in modules: errors.append(f"duplicate module {cur['id']}")
            modules[cur["id"]] = cur; order.append(cur["id"]); continue
        if cur and line.startswith("- **Type:**"):
            cur["type"] = line.split("**Type:**")[1].strip().split()[0]
        if cur and line.startswith("- **Owns:**"):
            cur["owns"] = re.findall(r"`([^`]+)`", line)
        t = re.match(r"^#### (P\d-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}) — ", line)
        if t:
            tid = t.group(1)
            if tid in tasks: errors.append(f"duplicate task {tid}")
            if not cur or not tid.startswith(cur["id"] + "-"): errors.append(f"task {tid} outside its module")
            tasks[tid] = {"module": cur["id"] if cur else None, "files": []}
            cur["tasks"].append(tid); continue
        if cur and cur["tasks"] and line.startswith("**Files:**"):
            tasks[cur["tasks"][-1]]["files"] += re.findall(r"`([^`]+)` \((create|edit)\)", line)
    own = {mid: [glob_to_re(g) for g in md["owns"]] for mid, md in modules.items()}
    created = {}
    for mid in order:
        for tid in modules[mid]["tasks"]:
            for p, mode in tasks[tid]["files"]:
                owners = [o for o, rs in own.items() if any(r.match(p) for r in rs)]
                if mid not in owners: errors.append(f"{tid}: {p} is not owned by {mid}")
                if len(owners) > 1 and not (p in MANIFESTS and all(modules[o]["type"] == "DEPS" for o in owners)):
                    errors.append(f"{tid}: {p} owned by several modules {owners}")
                if mode == "create":
                    if p in created: errors.append(f"{tid}: {p} already created by {created[p]}")
                    created[p] = tid
                elif p not in created:
                    errors.append(f"{tid}: edits {p} before it is created")
    print(f"modules={len(modules)} tasks={len(tasks)} files={len(created)} errors={len(errors)}")
    for e in errors: print("ERROR", e)
    return 1 if errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))
```
**Verify:** `python scripts/plan/plan_lint.py docs/plan/PROJECT_VISUALIZER_BUILD_PLAN.md` → last line of the summary shows `errors=0`.

#### P0-TOOLS-004 — Next-tasks helper
**Files:** `scripts/plan/next_tasks.py` (create)
**Refs:** R2
**Why:** the human needs a quick list of tasks that can start now (all earlier work merged).
**Steps:**
1. Create the file with exactly this content:
```python
"""Lists the next task of every module whose prerequisites are done.
Usage: python scripts/plan/next_tasks.py docs/plan/PROJECT_VISUALIZER_BUILD_PLAN.md"""
import os
import re
import sys


def main(path):
    done = {f[:-3] for f in os.listdir("docs/status/done") if f.endswith(".md")}
    lines = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    modules, order, cur, fence = {}, [], None, None
    for line in lines:
        st = line.lstrip()
        if fence is None and (st.startswith("```") or st.startswith("~~~")):
            fence = st[:3]; continue
        if fence is not None:
            if st.startswith(fence): fence = None
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^### MODULE (P\d-[A-Z0-9]+) — (.+)$", line)
        if m:
            cur = {"id": m.group(1), "title": m.group(2), "after": [], "tasks": []}
            modules[cur["id"]] = cur; order.append(cur["id"]); continue
        if cur and line.startswith("- **Starts after:**"):
            cur["after"] = re.findall(r"(P\d-[A-Z0-9]+)", line)
        t = re.match(r"^#### (P\d-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}) — (.+)$", line)
        if t and cur:
            cur["tasks"].append((t.group(1), t.group(2)))
    def complete(mid):
        return all(tid in done for tid, _ in modules[mid]["tasks"])
    for mid in order:
        md = modules[mid]
        if complete(mid) or not all(complete(a) for a in md["after"] if a in modules):
            continue
        for tid, title in md["tasks"]:
            if tid not in done:
                print(f"{tid} — {title}   [{md['title']}]")
                break


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1])
```
**Verify:** `python scripts/plan/next_tasks.py docs/plan/PROJECT_VISUALIZER_BUILD_PLAN.md` → prints at least one line (for example a P0-ENV task).

### MODULE P0-NFR — Non-functional requirements
- **Type:** DOCS
- **Lane:** DOCS
- **Owns:** `docs/nfr/**`

- **Goal:** measurable targets for speed, scale, security, reliability, maintainability and usability.

#### P0-NFR-001 — Performance targets
**Files:** `docs/nfr/performance.md` (create)
**Refs:** R1
**Why:** numbers make "fast enough" testable.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# Performance targets`; table ID · Target · Measure. Rows:
   PERF-01 Engine start to `engine.ping` answer < 1 s · timer in desktop |
   PERF-02 Open a 1,000-file Python project to `ready` < 10 s; 10,000 files < 60 s · `project.status` timestamps |
   PERF-03 `graph.level_view` with ≤ 500 nodes < 200 ms · engine test timer |
   PERF-04 2D render of ≤ 500 nodes < 500 ms; pan/zoom ≥ 30 fps with ≤ 2,000 visible nodes · browser performance panel |
   PERF-05 `impact.analyze` depth 5 on 100k edges < 300 ms · engine test |
   PERF-06 Explain first result < 20 s (network + LLM) · desktop timer |
   PERF-07 Runtime event to visible overlay < 1 s · end-to-end test (Phase 3) |
   PERF-08 Engine memory < 2 GB for 1 M lines of code · task manager |
   PERF-09 Server API P95 < 2 s at 200 concurrent users (from the scaling design) · load test (Phase 2+) |
   PERF-10 Graph data render in browser < 500 ms (from the scaling design) · same as PERF-04.
**Verify:** `grep -c "^| PERF-" docs/nfr/performance.md` → `10`.

#### P0-NFR-002 — Scalability expectations
**Files:** `docs/nfr/scalability.md` (create)
**Refs:** R13
**Why:** know what size of codebase and user count the design must handle.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# Scalability`; `## Desktop`: supports projects up to 5 M lines by loading one level view at a time; no full-graph rendering.
2. `## Server (from the current design) [ARCH-DEPENDENT]`: capacity targets for 200 concurrent users: ~50 parsing jobs/min, ~20 AI queries/min, P95 < 2 s. Scaling thresholds: 500 users → third parsing instance + Kubernetes; 1,000 → split Redis (sessions/queues/cache); 2,000 → consider self-hosted smaller LLM; 5,000 → full microservices with independent pipelines.
3. `## Compute sizing (current design)`: API gateway 2 vCPU/4 GB ×2; parsing 4 vCPU/8 GB ×2; AI service 8 vCPU/16 GB ×2; graph service 4 vCPU/8 GB ×2; runtime 2 vCPU/4 GB ×2; PostgreSQL primary + 1 replica 50 GB; MongoDB single node + replica 100 GB; Redis 2 vCPU/4 GB cluster mode off.
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/nfr/scalability.md` → `3`.

#### P0-NFR-003 — Security and privacy requirements
**Files:** `docs/nfr/security-privacy.md` (create)
**Refs:** R11, R15
**Why:** enterprise buyers ask about this first.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# Security and privacy`; table ID · Requirement:
   SEC-01 Source code never leaves the machine unless the user explicitly shares a snapshot. |
   SEC-02 AI requests contain only the engine-built context pack, never whole repositories. |
   SEC-03 API keys and tokens are encrypted at rest (OS keychain via Electron safeStorage). |
   SEC-04 Renderer runs with contextIsolation, sandbox, no Node integration. |
   SEC-05 Local ports (47100, 47101) bind to 127.0.0.1 and require a token. |
   SEC-06 Server traffic uses TLS; passwords hashed with Argon2id; JWT access tokens expire in 15 minutes. |
   SEC-07 Every server input is validated with zod; SQL uses parameters only. |
   SEC-08 Audit log for team/admin actions (Phase 6). |
   SEC-09 Dependencies scanned in CI; secrets scanning on push. |
   SEC-10 Telemetry is opt-in and never includes code or file names.
**Verify:** `grep -c "^| SEC-" docs/nfr/security-privacy.md` → `10`.

### MODULE P0-ADR — Architecture decision records and versions
- **Type:** DOCS
- **Lane:** DOCS
- **Owns:** `docs/decisions/**`
- **Starts after:** P0-GUIDE
- **Goal:** record every major decision with its reason, so nobody re-argues it later.

#### P0-ADR-001 — ADR template and index
**Files:** `docs/decisions/README.md` (create) · `docs/decisions/template.md` (create)
**Refs:** R2
**Why:** all ADRs share one format.
**Steps:**
1. `template.md`: title `# ADR-NNNN: <title>`; sections `## Status` (Proposed | Accepted | Superseded by ADR-XXXX), `## Date`, `## Context`, `## Decision`, `## Consequences`, `## Alternatives considered`.
2. `README.md`: title `# Decisions`; one paragraph: "One file per decision: `ADR-NNNN-<kebab-title>.md`. Never edit an accepted ADR; write a new one that supersedes it."; section `## Index` with a table Number · Title · Status (rows added by P0-ADR-012).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/template.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-002 — ADR-0001 Local-first desktop client with optional cloud services
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0001-desktop-client-server.md` (create)
**Refs:** R4, R13
**Why:** the product is installed software, not a website.
**Steps:**
1. Use the template. Status Accepted. Context: users want privacy and speed; analysing code locally avoids uploading it; enterprises prefer on-prem. Decision: a desktop app (Electron UI + C++ engine) does all parsing and visualization locally; cloud services (auth, teams, sync, AI gateway, collector, billing) are optional and follow the server architecture [ARCH-DEPENDENT]. Consequences: installers per OS; offline use possible; server load much lower. Alternatives: pure web app (rejected: code upload, privacy, server cost).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0001-desktop-client-server.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-003 — ADR-0002 C++20 core engine
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0002-cpp-engine.md` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** record why the heavy work is in C++.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Context: large codebases, real-time updates, graph queries must be fast and memory-efficient. Decision: `pv-engine`, a C++20 executable with tree-sitter parsing and an in-memory graph, talking JSON-RPC over stdio. Consequences: fast; harder to write; strict tests and small tasks needed; separate process isolates crashes. Alternatives: Rust (rejected: team knowledge), Node.js (rejected: speed/memory), linking C++ into Electron as N-API addon (rejected: crash takes down UI, complex builds).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0002-cpp-engine.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-004 — ADR-0003 Electron + React + TypeScript desktop UI
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0003-electron-react.md` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** record the UI technology choice.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Context: need cross-platform desktop, rich 2D/3D graphics, fast iteration. Decision: Electron + React + TypeScript, Cytoscape for 2D, three.js (3d-force-graph) for 3D, Zustand for state, electron-vite for builds. Consequences: large installer (~100 MB), huge ecosystem, same UI skills as web. Alternatives: Qt/C++ (rejected: slow UI development, weaker 3D/graph libraries), Tauri (rejected for now: less mature ecosystem for this team).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0003-electron-react.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-005 — ADR-0004 Python for AI and ML
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0004-python-ai.md` (create)
**Refs:** R11
**Why:** record the AI/ML language choice.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Context: ML libraries, LLM SDKs and embeddings are best in Python. Decision: Python 3.12 FastAPI service `pv_ai`; MVP uses direct LLM calls from desktop instead. Consequences: separate service to deploy; easy ML. Alternatives: do everything in Node (rejected: weaker ML ecosystem).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0004-python-ai.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-006 — ADR-0005 Node.js/TypeScript cloud services
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0005-node-server.md` (create)
**Refs:** R13
**Why:** record the server language and framework.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted [ARCH-DEPENDENT]. Context: the current design uses Bull queues (Node) and a JS client. Decision: Node.js + TypeScript + Fastify services in a pnpm workspace; BullMQ for queues. Consequences: one language for desktop and server; shared types possible. Alternatives: Go (rejected: second language to learn), Python (kept only for AI/ML).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0005-node-server.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-007 — ADR-0006 tree-sitter for parsing all languages
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0006-tree-sitter.md` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** record how "any language" support is possible.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Context: must support many languages with one approach. Decision: tree-sitter grammars + query files (`tags.scm` style captures) per language; language-specific resolvers only where needed; later dynamic grammar plugins. Consequences: 100+ grammars available; error-tolerant parsing; no type information (resolution is best-effort). Alternatives: language servers (LSP) (rejected as base: slow, heavy; may be added later for precision), writing parsers (rejected).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0006-tree-sitter.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-008 — ADR-0007 JSON-RPC over stdio between desktop and engine
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0007-json-rpc-stdio.md` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** record the process communication contract.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Context: UI and engine are separate processes. Decision: JSON-RPC 2.0 with LSP-style Content-Length framing on stdin/stdout; logs on stderr; schemas in `contracts/rpc`. Consequences: simple, debuggable, language-neutral; JSON cost acceptable for level-view sized payloads. Alternatives: gRPC (rejected: build complexity), shared memory (rejected: complexity).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0007-json-rpc-stdio.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-009 — ADR-0008 Monorepo with strict file ownership
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0008-monorepo-ownership.md` (create)
**Refs:** R3
**Why:** record the no-overlap rule so parallel AI models never collide.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Context: many models may work in parallel. Decision: one repo; every path owned by one module; auto-discovery folders instead of shared registries; only DEPS modules edit shared manifests. Consequences: zero merge conflicts by design; slightly more files. Alternatives: polyrepo (rejected: coordination overhead).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0008-monorepo-ownership.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-010 — ADR-0009 Right store for each data type
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0009-data-stores.md` (create)
**Refs:** R13
**Why:** record the storage choices from the current design.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted [ARCH-DEPENDENT]. Decision table: PostgreSQL = users, orgs, projects, permissions, metadata (relational, ACID) | MongoDB = graph snapshot JSON blobs | S3/MinIO = raw code snapshots and reports | Qdrant = AI embeddings (the design allows Pinecone/Weaviate; Qdrant chosen for simple local dev; interface abstracted) | Redis = sessions, BullMQ queues, cache | desktop local = in-memory graph + SQLite for metrics history (Phase 5).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0009-data-stores.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-011 — ADR-0010 LLM providers and grounding
**Files:** `docs/decisions/ADR-0010-llm-grounding.md` (create)
**Refs:** R11
**Why:** record how AI stays correct and affordable.
**Steps:**
1. Status Accepted. Decision: provider abstraction (Anthropic + any OpenAI-compatible endpoint incl. local Ollama); default model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` for cost, configurable; the engine builds all facts; citations `[[node:<id>]]` validated; no self-hosted GPUs until 2,000 users (scaling design). Alternatives: fine-tuned model (rejected for now: cost).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/decisions/ADR-0010-llm-grounding.md` → `6`.

#### P0-ADR-012 — Versions record and decision index
**Files:** `docs/decisions/versions.md` (create) · `docs/decisions/decision-log.md` (create)
**Refs:** R5
**Why:** the exact tool versions used must be written down; plus one index of all decisions.
**Steps:**
1. `versions.md`: title `# Versions`; table Tool · Required · Installed on dev machine. Fill "Required" from R5; fill "Installed" by running `git --version`, `node --version`, `pnpm --version`, `python --version`, `uv --version`, `cmake --version`.
2. `decision-log.md`: title `# Decision log`; table Number · Title · Status · File, with rows ADR-0001 … ADR-0010 (all Accepted).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^| ADR-" docs/decisions/decision-log.md` → `10`.

#### P0-ARCH-001 — Record the current server architecture
**Files:** `docs/architecture/current-server-design.md` (create)
**Refs:** R13
**Why:** keep a faithful copy of the design by Abhishek (Sheet 1, backend design, scaling for 200 users) so later changes are traceable.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# Current server design (v1)`; sections:
   - `## Layers`: Client (web browser React/Next.js, VS Code extension) → Nginx load balancer → API gateway (rate limiting, auth, routing) + WebSocket server → services: Auth (JWT/OAuth2 + Redis session store), Ingestion (folder/Git/snippet/context handlers → Redis ingestion queue), Parsing & Analysis (language parsers → AST generation → semantic analysis → layered graph builder), Graph & Rendering (render-agnostic core, abstraction navigation, shared rendering core, 2D Canvas/SVG, 3D Three.js, health hooks, component interaction), AI (Q&A, impact, what-if, simulation visualization, decision recommendation, prediction engine, health forecasting, AI queue), Runtime & Monitoring (runtime ingestion agent, module tracing, execution visualization, health & error detection, error explanation).
   - `## Storage`: Redis cache (graph/AST/sessions), CDN (static assets), PostgreSQL (users/projects/metadata), MongoDB (AST/graph JSON blobs), S3 (code snapshots/reports), Vector DB (Pinecone/Weaviate).
   - `## Messaging`: Redis Pub/Sub + Bull queue for job orchestration.
   - `## Observability`: ELK, Prometheus + Grafana, Jaeger.
   - `## Scaling decisions`: async everything heavy; cache aggressively; render on the client; managed external AI; right DB per data type; ≥ 2 instances per critical service; rate limit at the gateway.
   - `## What changes in the desktop direction`: parsing and graph building move into the desktop C++ engine; the server keeps auth, teams, sync, AI gateway, runtime aggregation, billing; a parse-worker reuses the engine for cloud/team imports.
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/architecture/current-server-design.md` → `6`.

### MODULE P0-CI — Continuous integration workflows
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** INFRA
- **Owns:** `.github/workflows/ci-*.yml`
- **Starts after:** P0-STD · P0-QA
- **Goal:** GitHub Actions workflows for every lane, each triggered only by its own folder so it never fails before that folder exists.

#### P0-CI-001 — Engine CI
**Files:** `.github/workflows/ci-engine.yml` (create)
**Refs:** R8, R14
**Why:** build and test the C++ engine on Windows and Linux on every change.
**Steps:**
1. Create with exactly:
```yaml
name: ci-engine
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['engine/**']
  pull_request:
    paths: ['engine/**']
jobs:
  build-test:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            preset: dev
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            preset: dev-unix
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Ninja (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y ninja-build
      - name: Configure
        working-directory: engine
        run: cmake --preset ${{ matrix.preset }}
      - name: Build
        working-directory: engine
        run: cmake --build --preset ${{ matrix.preset }}
      - name: Test
        working-directory: engine

#### P0-CON-001 — Contracts README
**Files:** `contracts/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R6, R7, R9
**Why:** explain the schema conventions once.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# Contracts`; sections:
   - `## Rules`: JSON Schema draft 2020-12; every schema has `"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"` and `"$id": "https://pv.local/schemas/<path relative to contracts/>"`; field names snake_case; `"additionalProperties": false` on every object unless stated.
   - `## Layout`: `common/` shared types; `rpc/<namespace>/<method>.params.schema.json` and `.result.schema.json`; `events/`; `http/<service>/`; `prompts/v1|v2/`.
   - `## Examples`: each schema folder may have `examples/<schema-base>.<n>.json`; `<schema-base>` is the schema file name without `.schema.json` (example: `examples/node.1.json` is validated against `node.schema.json` in the parent folder).
   - `## References`: use relative `$ref`, e.g. `"$ref": "../../common/node.schema.json"`.
   - `## Commands`: `pnpm install`, `pnpm validate`.
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " contracts/README.md` → `5`.

#### P0-CON-002 — Contracts package
**Files:** `contracts/package.json` (create) · `contracts/pnpm-lock.yaml` (create)
**Refs:** R5
**Why:** the validator needs Ajv.
**Steps:**
1. Create `contracts/package.json`:
```json

```
2. Run `cd contracts && pnpm add -D ajv@8 ajv-formats@3`. This updates `package.json` and creates `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

#### P0-CON-003 — Schema validator script
**Files:** `contracts/tools/validate.mjs` (create)
**Refs:** R14
**Why:** one command checks every schema compiles and every example matches its schema.
**Steps:**
1. Create with exactly this content:
```js
// Validates all JSON Schemas and examples under contracts/. Usage: pnpm validate
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, dirname, basename, relative } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import Ajv2020 from 'ajv/dist/2020.js';
import addFormats from 'ajv-formats';

const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const skip = new Set(['node_modules', 'tools', 'prompts']);

function walk(dir, out = []) {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
    if (skip.has(name)) continue;
    const p = join(dir, name);
    if (statSync(p).isDirectory()) walk(p, out);
    else if (name.endsWith('.json') && name !== 'package.json') out.push(p);
  }
  return out;
}

const ajv = new Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: true });
addFormats(ajv);
const files = walk(root);
const schemaFiles = files.filter((f) => f.endsWith('.schema.json'));
const exampleFiles = files.filter((f) => basename(dirname(f)) === 'examples');
let failed = 0;

for (const f of schemaFiles) {
  const schema = JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));
  const expectedId = 'https://pv.local/schemas/' + relative(root, f).split('\\').join('/');
  if (schema.$id !== expectedId) {
    console.error(`BAD $id in ${f}: expected ${expectedId}`);
    failed++;
  }
  ajv.addSchema(schema);
}
for (const f of schemaFiles) {
  const id = JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')).$id;
  try {
    ajv.getSchema(id);
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`SCHEMA ERROR ${f}: ${e.message}`);
    failed++;
  }
}
for (const f of exampleFiles) {
  const base = basename(f).replace(/\.\d+\.json$/, '');
  const schemaPath = join(dirname(dirname(f)), base + '.schema.json');
  const id = 'https://pv.local/schemas/' + relative(root, schemaPath).split('\\').join('/');
  const validate = ajv.getSchema(id);
  if (!validate) {
    console.error(`NO SCHEMA for example ${f} (looked for ${schemaPath})`);
    failed++;
    continue;
  }
  if (!validate(JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')))) {
    console.error(`INVALID ${f}: ${ajv.errorsText(validate.errors)}`);
    failed++;
  }
}
console.log(`schemas=${schemaFiles.length} examples=${exampleFiles.length} failed=${failed}`);
process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
```
**Verify:** `cd contracts && pnpm validate` → prints `schemas=0 examples=0 failed=0` (no schemas yet) and exits 0.

# PHASE 1 — CORE TWIN VISUALIZATION (PROJECT IMPORT AND MAPPING) → MVP

**Mission:** import a Python project, build the layered graph in the C++ engine, show it as an interactive 2D map in the desktop app, drill through abstraction levels, explain any node with AI, and show what breaks if a node changes. The **MVP CHECKPOINT** (module P1-MVP) happens in the middle of this phase; the rest of the phase adds search, insights, 3D, Git import, notebooks, packaging, documentation and user testing.

### Phase 1 wave table

| Wave | Modules (parallel inside a wave) |
|---|---|
| 1 | P1-EBOOT · P1-CRPC · P1-PROMPT · P1-DDEPS |
| 2 | P1-EDEPS · P1-DENG · P1-DPRE |
| 3 | P1-CORE · P1-DMAIN · P1-DSHELL |
| 4 | P1-GRAPH · P1-FS · P1-RPC · P1-PARSE · P1-DAPI · P1-DAI |
| 5 | P1-PY · P1-BUILDR · P1-DVIEW · P1-DIMPORT · P1-DSET |
| 6 | P1-SESS · P1-D2D · P1-DNAV · P1-DINSP · P1-DIMPACT · P1-DEXPL |
| 7 | P1-EAPP · P1-GAPI · P1-IMPACT · P1-CTX |
| 8 | P1-MVP  ← **MVP CHECKPOINT** |
| 9 | P1-SRCH · P1-ANLYS · P1-CLI · P1-EPERF · P1-PYNB · P1-DGIT · P1-DINPUT · P1-DSRCH · P1-DINSI · P1-D3D · P1-DEXPLORE |
| 10 | P1-DE2E · P1-REL · P1-UDOC |
| 11 | P1-UT |
| 12 | P1-SIGN |

**Special task-level dependencies (written as `Needs:` in the tasks):**
- `P1-PY-017` (Python adapter registration) needs P1-SESS merged. P1-PY starts in wave 5; only that last task waits for wave 6.
- `P1-BUILDR-003` and later builder tasks need `P1-PY-015` merged (they test with the real Python adapter). P1-BUILDR-001/002 can run earlier.

#### P1-EBOOT-001 — Root CMakeLists.txt
**Files:** `engine/CMakeLists.txt` (create)
**Refs:** R8, R3
**Why:** the entry point of the engine build; it discovers third-party libs, modules and the app.
**Steps:**
1. Create the file with exactly:
```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
project(pv_engine VERSION 0.1.0 LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(PV_ENGINE_ROOT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
set(PV_ENGINE_VERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION})

option(PV_BUILD_TESTS "Build unit tests" ON)

include(FetchContent)
if(PV_BUILD_TESTS)
  enable_testing()
  include(GoogleTest)
endif()
include(${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/cmake/PvModule.cmake)
include(${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/cmake/GenerateRegistry.cmake)

if(MSVC)
  add_compile_options(/utf-8 /EHsc /permissive- /Zc:__cplusplus)
endif()

# Third-party libraries: every engine/third_party/<name>/CMakeLists.txt (alphabetical)
file(GLOB PV_TP_CMAKES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/third_party/*/CMakeLists.txt)
list(SORT PV_TP_CMAKES)
foreach(cm ${PV_TP_CMAKES})
  get_filename_component(dir ${cm} DIRECTORY)
  add_subdirectory(${dir})
endforeach()

# Engine modules: every engine/modules/<name>/CMakeLists.txt (alphabetical)
file(GLOB PV_MODULE_CMAKES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/modules/*/CMakeLists.txt)
list(SORT PV_MODULE_CMAKES)
foreach(cm ${PV_MODULE_CMAKES})
  get_filename_component(dir ${cm} DIRECTORY)
  add_subdirectory(${dir})
endforeach()

# The pv-engine executable (created by P1-EAPP)
if(EXISTS ${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/app/CMakeLists.txt)
  add_subdirectory(${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/app)
endif()
```

#### P1-EBOOT-003 — Module helper pv_add_module
**Files:** `engine/cmake/PvModule.cmake` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** every module is declared with one line; sources and tests are found automatically.
**Steps:**
1. Create the file with exactly:
```cmake
# pv_add_module(NAME <name> [DEPS <targets>...] [TEST_DEPS <targets>...])
# Creates static library pv_<name> from src/*.cpp, public include dir include/,
# and test executable pv_<name>_tests from tests/*_test.cpp (if any).
function(pv_add_module)
  cmake_parse_arguments(PVM "" "NAME" "DEPS;TEST_DEPS" ${ARGN})
  if(NOT PVM_NAME)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "pv_add_module: NAME is required")
  endif()
  set(target pv_${PVM_NAME})
  file(GLOB_RECURSE srcs CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp)
  if(NOT srcs)
    set(empty_src ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}_empty.cpp)
    file(WRITE ${empty_src} "// generated: this module has no sources yet\n")
    set(srcs ${empty_src})
  endif()
  add_library(${target} STATIC ${srcs})
  target_include_directories(${target} PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)
  target_compile_features(${target} PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
  target_compile_definitions(${target} PUBLIC PV_ENGINE_VERSION="${PV_ENGINE_VERSION}")
  if(PVM_DEPS)
    target_link_libraries(${target} PUBLIC ${PVM_DEPS})
  endif()
  if(MSVC)
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE /W4)
  else()
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  endif()
  set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY PV_MODULE_TARGETS ${target})
  if(PV_BUILD_TESTS)
    file(GLOB tests CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*_test.cpp)
    if(tests)
      add_executable(${target}_tests ${tests})
      target_link_libraries(${target}_tests PRIVATE ${target} ${PVM_TEST_DEPS} GTest::gtest_main)
      target_compile_definitions(${target}_tests PRIVATE
        PV_TEST_FIXTURES="${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/fixtures"
        PV_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR="${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}")
      gtest_discover_tests(${target}_tests DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST)
    endif()
  endif()
endfunction()
```
2. Meaning for later tasks: in test code, `PV_TEST_FIXTURES` is the module's own `tests/fixtures` folder, and `PV_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR` is the `engine/` folder (tests may **read** fixtures of other modules through it, never write them).
**Verify:** checked in P1-EBOOT-005.

#### P1-EBOOT-004 — Registration generator
**Files:** `engine/cmake/GenerateRegistry.cmake` (create) · `engine/cmake/registry_gen.cpp.in` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** the app calls every module's `pv_register_<m>()` without anyone editing a central list.
**Steps:**
1. Create `GenerateRegistry.cmake` with exactly:
```cmake
# pv_generate_registry(<output .cpp path>)
# Finds every engine/modules/<m>/src/register.cpp and generates a .cpp file that
# declares and calls pv_register_<m>(reg) for each module, in alphabetical order.
function(pv_generate_registry out_file)
  file(GLOB reg_files CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/modules/*/src/register.cpp)
  list(SORT reg_files)
  set(PV_REGISTER_DECLS "")
  set(PV_REGISTER_CALLS "")
  foreach(f ${reg_files})
    get_filename_component(src_dir ${f} DIRECTORY)
    get_filename_component(mod_dir ${src_dir} DIRECTORY)
    get_filename_component(mod ${mod_dir} NAME)
    string(APPEND PV_REGISTER_DECLS "void pv_register_${mod}(pv::session::Registry& reg);\n")
    string(APPEND PV_REGISTER_CALLS "    pv_register_${mod}(reg);\n")
  endforeach()
  configure_file(${PV_ENGINE_ROOT}/cmake/registry_gen.cpp.in ${out_file} @ONLY)
endfunction()
```
2. Create `registry_gen.cpp.in` with exactly:
```cpp
// GENERATED FILE - do not edit. Produced by engine/cmake/GenerateRegistry.cmake.
#include "pv/session/registry.hpp"

@PV_REGISTER_DECLS@
namespace pv::app {
void register_all_modules(pv::session::Registry& reg) {
    (void)reg;
@PV_REGISTER_CALLS@}
}  // namespace pv::app
```

#### P1-CORE-006 — Path normalization
**Files:** `engine/modules/core/include/pv/core/paths.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/core/src/paths.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/core/tests/paths_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R6, R7
**Why:** every path inside the graph must have one canonical form (`/` separators, no `./`).
**Steps:**
1. `paths.hpp`: `#pragma once`, include `<optional>` and `<string>`, namespace `pv::core`, declare `std::string normalize_path(const std::string& path);`
2. Implement in `paths.cpp`:
   1. Replace every `\` with `/`.
   2. Split on `/` into segments. Remember whether the path started with `/` (absolute POSIX) and whether the first segment looks like a drive (`X:` — a letter then `:`).
   3. Build a result list: skip empty segments and `.` segments; for `..`: if the result list is non-empty and its last item is not `..` and is not a drive segment, pop the last item; otherwise push `..` (only when the path is relative).
   4. Join with `/`. Prefix `/` if the input was absolute POSIX. If the only segment is a drive (e.g. `C:`), return `C:/`.
   5. The empty string and `.` both normalize to `""`.
3. Tests suite `CorePaths`:
   `normalize_path("src\\app\\main.py") == "src/app/main.py"` · `normalize_path("./src//app/./x.py") == "src/app/x.py"` · `normalize_path("src/app/../lib/y.py") == "src/lib/y.py"` · `normalize_path("../a/b") == "../a/b"` · `normalize_path("/home/u/p/") == "/home/u/p"` · `normalize_path("C:\\code\\proj\\") == "C:/code/proj"` · `normalize_path("C:\\") == "C:/"` · `normalize_path("") == ""` · `normalize_path(".") == ""`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R CorePaths` → all pass.

#### P1-CORE-007 — Path parts and join
**Files:** `engine/modules/core/include/pv/core/paths.hpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/core/src/paths.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/core/tests/paths_test.cpp` (edit)
**Refs:** R6
**Why:** parents, file names and extensions are needed to build package/module nodes.
**Steps:**
1. Declare and implement (inputs are already normalized):
```cpp
std::string path_parent(const std::string& path);     // "src/app/main.py" -> "src/app"; "main.py" -> ""
std::string path_file_name(const std::string& path);  // "src/app/main.py" -> "main.py"
std::string path_stem(const std::string& path);       // "src/app/main.py" -> "main"; "a.tar.gz" -> "a.tar"; ".env" -> ".env"
std::string path_extension(const std::string& path);  // lowercase with dot: "X/Main.PY" -> ".py"; "Makefile" -> ""; ".env" -> ""
std::string path_join(const std::string& a, const std::string& b); // normalize_path(a + "/" + b); if a is "" returns normalize_path(b)
```
2. A file name that starts with `.` and has no other `.` has no extension (stem = whole name).
3. Tests (suite `CorePaths`): all examples in the comments above, plus `path_join("", "x.py") == "x.py"`, `path_join("C:/code", "src/a.py") == "C:/code/src/a.py"`, `path_parent("C:/code") == "C:"`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R CorePaths` → all pass.

#### P1-CORE-008 — Relative path computation
**Files:** `engine/modules/core/include/pv/core/paths.hpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/core/src/paths.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/core/tests/paths_test.cpp` (edit)
**Refs:** R7, R12
**Why:** runtime events carry absolute paths; the graph uses paths relative to the project root.
**Steps:**
1. Declare `std::optional<std::string> path_relative_to(const std::string& root, const std::string& path);`
2. Implement: normalize both. Comparison is **case-insensitive on Windows** (`#ifdef _WIN32`, compare with ASCII lower-case) and case-sensitive elsewhere. If `path` equals `root` return `""`. If `path` starts with `root + "/"` return the remainder (keeping the original case of `path`). If root is a drive root like `C:/`, a path `C:/x/y` returns `x/y`. Otherwise return `std::nullopt`.
3. Tests (suite `CorePaths`): `path_relative_to("C:/code/proj", "C:/code/proj/src/a.py") == "src/a.py"`; `path_relative_to("/home/u/p", "/home/u/p") == ""`; `path_relative_to("/home/u/p", "/home/u/px/a.py")` has no value; `path_relative_to("/home/u/p", "/home/u/other/a.py")` has no value; `path_relative_to("C:\\code\\proj", "C:\\code\\proj\\x.py") == "x.py"`. Add one test inside `#ifdef _WIN32`: `path_relative_to("C:/Code/Proj", "c:/code/proj/A.py") == "A.py"`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R CorePaths` → all pass.

**Files:** `engine/modules/core/include/pv/core/ids.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/core/src/ids.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/core/tests/ids_test.cpp` (create)

#### P1-CORE-012 — JSON for Node
**Files:** `engine/modules/core/include/pv/core/json.hpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/core/src/json.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/core/tests/json_test.cpp` (edit)
**Refs:** R7

**Steps:**
