### MODULE P1-GRAPH — In-memory graph store and level views
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/graph/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-CORE
- **Goal:** store nodes and edges with fast lookups (children, in/out edges, per file, by line) and build the aggregated **level view** that the canvas shows.

#### P1-GRAPH-001 — Graph class skeleton and node storage
**Files:** `engine/modules/graph/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/graph/include/pv/graph/graph.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/graph/src/graph.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/graph/tests/sample_graph.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/graph/tests/graph_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R8
**Why:** the core data structure of the twin.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME graph DEPS pv_core)`
2. `graph.hpp` — declare the **complete** class now (later tasks implement the rest):
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <cstddef>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>
#include "pv/core/types.hpp"

namespace pv::graph {

class Graph {
public:
    bool add_node(const core::Node& node);   // false (and no change) if the id already exists
    void add_edge(const core::Edge& edge);   // existing id: weight += edge.weight; else insert
    const core::Node* find_node(const std::string& id) const;  // nullptr if missing
    core::Node* find_node_mut(const std::string& id);
    const core::Edge* find_edge(const std::string& id) const;
    const core::Node& node(const std::string& id) const;       // throws PvError(err::NodeNotFound)
    std::vector<const core::Node*> children(const std::string& id) const;   // insertion order
    std::vector<const core::Edge*> out_edges(const std::string& id) const;  // insertion order
    std::vector<const core::Edge*> in_edges(const std::string& id) const;   // insertion order
    std::vector<const core::Node*> nodes_in_file(const std::string& file_path) const;
    std::vector<const core::Node*> all_nodes() const;  // sorted by id
    std::vector<const core::Edge*> all_edges() const;  // sorted by id
    std::size_t node_count() const;
    std::size_t edge_count() const;
    std::vector<std::string> ancestors(const std::string& id) const;  // root first, ends with id
    std::string ancestor_at_level(const std::string& id, int level) const;
    bool is_descendant(const std::string& id, const std::string& ancestor_id) const;
    std::vector<std::string> descendants(const std::string& id) const;
    std::size_t remove_file(const std::string& file_path);
    const core::Node* innermost_at(const std::string& file_path, int line) const;
    void clear();

private:
    std::unordered_map<std::string, core::Node> nodes_;
    std::unordered_map<std::string, core::Edge> edges_;
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> children_;  // parent id -> child ids
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> out_;       // node id -> edge ids
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> in_;        // node id -> edge ids
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> by_file_;   // file path -> node ids
};

}  // namespace pv::graph
```
3. In `graph.cpp` implement only: `add_node` (insert into `nodes_`; if `parent_id` is not empty append id to `children_[parent_id]`; if `file_path` not empty append id to `by_file_[file_path]`), `find_node`, `find_node_mut`, `node` (throws `core::PvError(core::err::NodeNotFound, "node not found: " + id)`), `node_count`, `clear` (clears all maps). Every other method gets a temporary body that only throws `core::PvError(core::err::Unsupported, "not implemented")`. Later tasks of this module replace these bodies one by one.
4. `tests/sample_graph.hpp` — a helper used by all graph tests:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include "pv/core/ids.hpp"
#include "pv/graph/graph.hpp"

namespace pv::graph::testing {

inline core::Node make_node(core::NodeKind kind, const std::string& id, const std::string& parent,
                            const std::string& file, int start_line, int end_line) {
    core::Node n;
    n.id = id;
    n.kind = kind;
    n.name = id.substr(id.find_last_of(":#.") + 1);
    n.qualified_name = n.name;
    n.file_path = file;
    n.parent_id = parent;
    n.level = core::level_of(kind);
    n.span = core::Span{start_line, 0, end_line, 0};
    return n;
}

inline core::Edge make_edge(core::EdgeKind kind, const std::string& src, const std::string& dst, int weight = 1) {
    core::Edge e;
    e.kind = kind;
    e.source_id = src;
    e.target_id = dst;
    e.weight = weight;
    e.id = core::make_edge_id(kind, src, dst);
    return e;
}

// project:
// ├── package:app
// │   └── module:app/a.py            (lines 1-20)
// │       ├── function:app/a.py#f    (lines 2-5)
// │       └── class:app/a.py#C       (lines 7-20)
// │           └── method:app/a.py#C.m (lines 8-12)
// ├── module:main.py                 (lines 1-10)
// │   └── function:main.py#main      (lines 1-10)
// └── external:os
// edges: calls main->f (1), calls main->C.m (2), imports main.py->app/a.py (1),
//        imports app/a.py->os (1), calls f->C.m (1)
inline Graph sample_graph() {
    using core::NodeKind;
    using core::EdgeKind;
    Graph g;
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Project, "project:", "", "", 0, 0));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Package, "package:app", "project:", "", 0, 0));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Module, "module:app/a.py", "package:app", "app/a.py", 1, 20));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Function, "function:app/a.py#f", "module:app/a.py", "app/a.py", 2, 5));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Class, "class:app/a.py#C", "module:app/a.py", "app/a.py", 7, 20));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Method, "method:app/a.py#C.m", "class:app/a.py#C", "app/a.py", 8, 12));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Module, "module:main.py", "project:", "main.py", 1, 10));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::Function, "function:main.py#main", "module:main.py", "main.py", 1, 10));
    g.add_node(make_node(NodeKind::External, "external:os", "project:", "", 0, 0));
    g.add_edge(make_edge(EdgeKind::Calls, "function:main.py#main", "function:app/a.py#f", 1));
    g.add_edge(make_edge(EdgeKind::Calls, "function:main.py#main", "method:app/a.py#C.m", 2));
    g.add_edge(make_edge(EdgeKind::Imports, "module:main.py", "module:app/a.py", 1));
    g.add_edge(make_edge(EdgeKind::Imports, "module:app/a.py", "external:os", 1));
    g.add_edge(make_edge(EdgeKind::Calls, "function:app/a.py#f", "method:app/a.py#C.m", 1));
    return g;
}

}  // namespace pv::graph::testing
```
5. `graph_test.cpp`: suite `GraphStore`. In this task do **not** call `sample_graph()` yet (it uses `add_edge`, which is implemented in the next task); build 3 nodes with `testing::make_node` instead. **Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R GraphStore` → all pass.

#### P1-GRAPH-005 — Ancestors and descendants
**Files:** `engine/modules/graph/src/graph.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/graph/tests/graph_test.cpp` (edit)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** breadcrumbs, level mapping and impact analysis walk the containment tree.
**Steps:**
1. `ancestors(id)`: throws `NodeNotFound` if missing; walk `parent_id` up until empty or a parent is missing; return list with root first and `id` last.
2. `ancestor_at_level(id, level)`: walk from `id` upward; return the first node id whose `level <= level`; return `""` if none (or id missing).
3. `is_descendant(id, ancestor_id)`: true if `id == ancestor_id` or `ancestor_id` appears in `ancestors(id)`; false if id missing.
4. `descendants(id)`: depth-first pre-order over `children()`, **not** including `id`.
5. Tests: `ancestors("method:app/a.py#C.m") == {"project:","package:app","module:app/a.py","class:app/a.py#C","method:app/a.py#C.m"}`; `ancestor_at_level("method:app/a.py#C.m", 2) == "module:app/a.py"`; `ancestor_at_level("function:main.py#main", 1) == "project:"`; `is_descendant("function:app/a.py#f","package:app")` true; `is_descendant("function:main.py#main","package:app")` false; `descendants("module:app/a.py") == {"function:app/a.py#f","class:app/a.py#C","method:app/a.py#C.m"}`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R GraphStore` → all pass.

#### P1-GRAPH-006 — Remove a file's nodes
**Files:** `engine/modules/graph/src/graph.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/graph/tests/graph_test.cpp` (edit)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** re-parsing a changed file (Phase 4) replaces its nodes.
**Steps:**
1. `remove_file(file_path)`: collect ids from `by_file_[file_path]`; for each existing node: remove every edge in its `out_` and `in_` lists from `edges_` and from the opposite node's list; remove the id from its parent's `children_` list; erase `children_[id]`, `out_[id]`, `in_[id]`; erase the node. Finally erase `by_file_[file_path]`. Return the number of nodes removed.
2. Tests: on the sample graph `remove_file("app/a.py") == 4`; then `node_count() == 5`; `edge_count() == 0` (all 5 sample edges touch a node of `app/a.py`); `children("package:app")` is empty; `out_edges("function:main.py#main")` is empty; removing an unknown file returns 0.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R GraphStore` → all pass.

#### P1-GRAPH-008 — Level view builder
**Files:** `engine/modules/graph/include/pv/graph/level_view.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/graph/src/level_view.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/graph/tests/level_view_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R16
**Why:** the canvas shows the children of one node plus aggregated edges between them.
**Steps:**
1. `level_view.hpp`:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include "pv/core/types.hpp"
#include "pv/graph/graph.hpp"

namespace pv::graph {
struct LevelView {
    core::Node parent;
    std::vector<core::Node> nodes;
    std::vector<core::Edge> edges;
};
LevelView build_level_view(const Graph& graph, const std::string& parent_id);
}  // namespace pv::graph
```
2. Algorithm in `level_view.cpp`:
   1. `parent = graph.node(parent_id)` (throws if missing). `nodes` = copies of `children(parent_id)`.
   2. Build a map `display_of` from every node id in each child's subtree (the child itself + `descendants(child)`) to that child's id.
   3. For each (id → display D) in the map, for each out-edge E of id: look up `display_of[E.target_id]`; if not found (target outside this view) skip; if it equals D (inside the same displayed node) skip; else add to an aggregate keyed by `(E.kind, D, display_target)`: weight += E.weight.
   4. Each aggregate becomes an `Edge` with `id = core::make_agg_edge_id(kind, D, target)`, `resolved = true`.
   5. Sort `nodes` by (level, then name, then id) and `edges` by id.
3. Tests suite `GraphLevelView` on the sample graph:
   - view of `project:` → 3 nodes (`package:app`, `module:main.py`, `external:os`) and exactly these 3 edges: `agg|calls|module:main.py|package:app` weight 3, `agg|imports|module:main.py|package:app` weight 1, `agg|imports|package:app|external:os` weight 1.
   - view of `package:app` → 1 node, 0 edges.
   - view of `module:app/a.py` → 2 nodes (`class:app/a.py#C`, `function:app/a.py#f`), 1 edge `agg|calls|function:app/a.py#f|class:app/a.py#C` weight 1.
   - view of an unknown id throws `PvError`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R GraphLevelView` → all pass.

- **Type:** CODE

#### P1-FS-001 — Module skeleton and glob matching
**Files:** `engine/modules/fs/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/fs/include/pv/fs/fs.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fs/src/glob.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fs/tests/glob_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R6
**Why:** excludes and `.gitignore` rules are glob patterns.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME fs DEPS pv_core)`
2. `fs.hpp` — declare everything of this module now:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>
#include <regex>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace pv::fs {

std::string glob_to_regex(const std::string& glob);
bool glob_match(const std::string& glob, const std::string& path);

class GlobSet {
public:
    explicit GlobSet(const std::vector<std::string>& globs);
    bool matches(const std::string& path) const;
private:
    std::vector<std::regex> regexes_;
};

std::vector<std::string> default_excludes();
bool looks_binary(const std::string& first_bytes);

class GitIgnore {
public:
    void add_file(const std::string& dir_rel, const std::string& content);
    bool ignored(const std::string& rel_path, bool is_dir) const;
private:
    struct Rule { std::regex self; std::regex inside; bool negate = false; bool dir_only = false; };
    std::vector<Rule> rules_;
};

struct DiscoverOptions {
    std::vector<std::string> extensions;      // lower-case with dot, e.g. ".py"; empty = all files
    std::vector<std::string> exclude_globs;   // extra user excludes (relative paths)
    std::uintmax_t max_file_bytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024;
    bool use_gitignore = true;
};
struct DiscoveredFile {
    std::string rel_path;   // normalized, relative to root
    std::string abs_path;   // normalized absolute path
    std::uintmax_t size = 0;
};
struct DiscoverResult {
    std::vector<DiscoveredFile> files;   // sorted by rel_path
    std::vector<std::string> skipped;    // "<rel_path> (too large)" or "<rel_path> (binary)", sorted
};
DiscoverResult discover_files(const std::string& root, const DiscoverOptions& options);

}  // namespace pv::fs
```
3. In `glob.cpp` implement `glob_to_regex`, `glob_match`, and `GlobSet`:
   - Walk the glob left to right: `**/` → `(?:.*/)?` ; `**` → `.*` ; `*` → `[^/]*` ; `?` → `[^/]` ; any of `. + ( ) ^ $ | [ ] { } \` → backslash + that char; anything else → itself. Wrap as `^…$`.
   - `glob_match` = `std::regex_match(path, std::regex(glob_to_regex(glob)))`.
   - `GlobSet` compiles each glob once; `matches` returns true if any regex matches.
4. Tests suite `FsGlob`: `glob_match("*.py","a.py")` true; `glob_match("*.py","x/a.py")` false; `glob_match("**/*.py","x/y/a.py")` true; `glob_match("**/*.py","a.py")` true; `glob_match("node_modules/**","node_modules/a/b.js")` true; `glob_match("**/node_modules/**","web/node_modules/")` true; `glob_match("a?c.txt","abc.txt")` true; `glob_match("a.py","aXpy")` false (dot is literal).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R FsGlob` → all pass.

#### P1-FS-003 — .gitignore rules
**Files:** `engine/modules/fs/src/gitignore.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fs/tests/gitignore_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R3
**Why:** respect what the project itself ignores.
**Steps:**
1. `GitIgnore::add_file(dir_rel, content)`: for each line (split on `\n`, trim, drop `\r`): skip empty lines and lines starting with `#`. `negate` = line starts with `!` (remove it). `dir_only` = line ends with `/` (remove it). If the line starts with `/`, remove that `/` and mark anchored; also anchored if the (remaining) line contains a `/`. Prefix = `dir_rel.empty() ? "" : dir_rel + "/"`. Glob `g` = anchored ? prefix + line : prefix + "**/" + line. Store rule with `self = regex(glob_to_regex(g))`, `inside = regex(glob_to_regex(g + "/**"))`.
2. `ignored(rel_path, is_dir)`: `result = false`; for each rule in order: `match = std::regex_match(rel_path, rule.inside) || ((!rule.dir_only || is_dir) && std::regex_match(rel_path, rule.self))`; if `match`, `result = !rule.negate`. Return `result`.
3. Tests suite `FsGitIgnore`: after `add_file("", "# c\n*.log\nbuild/\n/secret.txt\n!keep.log\n")`: `ignored("a.log",false)` true; `ignored("x/b.log",false)` true; `ignored("keep.log",false)` false; `ignored("build",true)` true; `ignored("build",false)` false; `ignored("src/build/x.py",false)` true; `ignored("secret.txt",false)` true; `ignored("sub/secret.txt",false)` false. After also `add_file("sub", "*.tmp")`: `ignored("sub/a.tmp",false)` true; `ignored("a.tmp",false)` false.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R FsGitIgnore` → all pass.

#### P1-FS-004 — Temporary folder helper for tests
**Files:** `engine/modules/fs/tests/temp_tree.hpp` (create)
**Refs:** R14
**Why:** discovery tests build small folder trees on disk and delete them afterwards.
**Steps:**
1. Create exactly:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <atomic>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <string>

namespace pv::fs::testing {

class TempTree {
public:
    TempTree() {
        static std::atomic<int> counter{0};
        root_ = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() /
                ("pv_fs_test_" + std::to_string(counter++) + "_" + std::to_string(std::rand()));
        std::filesystem::create_directories(root_);
    }
    ~TempTree() {
        std::error_code ec;
        std::filesystem::remove_all(root_, ec);
    }
    TempTree(const TempTree&) = delete;
    TempTree& operator=(const TempTree&) = delete;

    void write(const std::string& rel, const std::string& content) {
        auto p = root_ / rel;
        std::filesystem::create_directories(p.parent_path());
        std::ofstream out(p, std::ios::binary);
        out << content;
    }
    std::string root() const { return root_.generic_string(); }

private:
    std::filesystem::path root_;
};

}  // namespace pv::fs::testing
```
**Verify:** compiled by the next task.

#### P1-FS-005 — Discover files (basic walk)

For each regular file: `abs = core::normalize_path(entry.path().generic_string())`; `rel = core::path_relative_to(root_n, abs).value()`; `ext = core::path_extension(rel)`; if `options.extensions` is not empty and does not contain `ext` → skip. Else add `DiscoveredFile{rel, abs, entry.file_size()}`.
   5. Sort `files` by `rel_path`.

#### P1-FS-007 — Size limit and binary skip
**Files:** `engine/modules/fs/src/discover.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/fs/tests/discover_test.cpp` (edit)

**Why:** huge or binary files would slow parsing and crash nothing useful.

### MODULE P1-RPC — JSON-RPC framing, method table and stdio server
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE

#### P1-RPC-001 — Message framing
**Files:** `engine/modules/rpc/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/include/pv/rpc/framing.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/src/framing.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/tests/framing_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** read and write `Content-Length` framed messages.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME rpc DEPS pv_core)`
2. `framing.hpp` (namespace `pv::rpc`):
```cpp
std::optional<std::string> read_message(std::istream& in);
void write_message(std::ostream& out, const std::string& body);
```
3. `read_message`: read header lines with `std::getline` (strip a trailing `\r`). If the stream hits EOF before reading any character → return `std::nullopt`. Stop at the first empty line. A header whose name equals `content-length` ignoring case gives the length (parse the text after `:` trimmed, with `std::stoul`). If EOF happens inside the headers, or there is no Content-Length → throw `core::PvError(core::err::ParseError, "bad message header")`. Then read exactly that many bytes with `in.read`; if fewer bytes arrive → throw `PvError(ParseError, "truncated message body")`.
4. `write_message`: write `"Content-Length: " + std::to_string(body.size()) + "\r\n\r\n" + body` and `flush()`.
5. Tests suite `RpcFraming`: write then read back `{"a":1}` through a `std::stringstream`; two messages in a row are read in order; empty stream → `nullopt`; header `content-length: 3` (lower case) works; missing length throws; body shorter than length throws; an extra header `Content-Type: x` is ignored.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R RpcFraming` → all pass.

#### P1-RPC-002 — Notifier interface
**Files:** `engine/modules/rpc/include/pv/rpc/notifier.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/src/notifier.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/tests/notifier_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** modules send notifications without knowing how they are transported.
**Steps:**
1. `notifier.hpp`:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>
#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

namespace pv::rpc {
using Json = nlohmann::json;

class Notifier {
public:
    virtual ~Notifier() = default;
    virtual void notify(const std::string& method, const Json& params) = 0;
};

class NullNotifier : public Notifier {
public:
    void notify(const std::string& method, const Json& params) override;
};

class RecordingNotifier : public Notifier {
public:
    void notify(const std::string& method, const Json& params) override;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, Json>> items() const;  // copy, thread-safe
private:
    mutable std::mutex mutex_;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, Json>> items_;
};
}  // namespace pv::rpc
```
2. Implement: `NullNotifier::notify` does nothing (mark parameters unused with `(void)`); `RecordingNotifier` appends under the mutex; `items()` returns a copy under the mutex.
3. Tests suite `RpcNotifier`: record two notifications from two threads (`std::thread`) → `items().size() == 2`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R RpcNotifier` → pass.

#### P1-RPC-006 — Request dispatcher
**Files:** `engine/modules/rpc/include/pv/rpc/dispatch.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/src/dispatch.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/tests/dispatch_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9, R15
**Why:** turn one JSON-RPC request into one response, catching every error.
**Steps:**
1. Declare `Json handle_request(const MethodTable& table, const Json& request);` and `Json make_error_response(const Json& id, int code, const std::string& message);`
2. `make_error_response` → `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":id,"error":{"code":code,"message":message}}`.
3. `handle_request`:
   1. If `request` is not an object → return error response with `id = null`, code `err::InvalidRequest`, message `"invalid request"`.
   2. `is_notification = !request.contains("id")`; `id = is_notification ? Json(nullptr) : request["id"]`.
   3. If `request.value("jsonrpc", "") != "2.0"` or `method` is missing or not a string → error `InvalidRequest` (return `Json()` i.e. null instead if it is a notification).
   4. `params = request.contains("params") && !request["params"].is_null() ? request["params"] : Json::object()`.
   5. Call `table.call(method, params)` inside `try`: catch `core::PvError` → code/what; catch `nlohmann::json::exception` → `err::InvalidParams` + what; catch `std::exception` → `err::Internal` + what. For notifications return `Json()` (null) in all cases.
   6. Success: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":id,"result":result}`.
4. Tests suite `RpcDispatch`: echo method success; unknown method → code -32601; handler throwing `PvError(err::NodeNotFound,"x")` → code -32002 message "x"; handler doing `params.at("missing")` → code -32602; missing `jsonrpc` → -32600; request without `id` → returns null JSON even on success; a string id `"abc"` is echoed back.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R RpcDispatch` → all pass.

#### P1-RPC-007 — Stdio server loop
**Files:** `engine/modules/rpc/include/pv/rpc/server.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/src/server.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/tests/server_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** the engine's main loop: read requests, write responses and notifications.
**Steps:**
1. `server.hpp`:
```cpp
class StdioServer : public Notifier {
public:
    StdioServer(std::istream& in, std::ostream& out);
    void notify(const std::string& method, const Json& params) override;  // thread-safe
    int run(const MethodTable& table);   // returns 0 on EOF or stop, 1 on a framing error
    void request_stop();                 // thread-safe; loop ends after the current message
private:
    void send(const Json& message);
    std::istream& in_;
    std::ostream& out_;
    std::mutex write_mutex_;
    std::atomic<bool> stop_{false};
};
```
2. `run`: loop: `read_message` (catch `PvError` → send an error response with id null and code `ParseError`, return 1); `nullopt` → return 0; parse JSON with `Json::parse` (on exception send `make_error_response(nullptr, err::ParseError, "parse error")` and continue); `resp = handle_request(table, req)`; if not null → `send(resp)`; if `stop_` → return 0.
3. `send`: lock `write_mutex_`, `write_message(out_, message.dump())`. `notify`: `send({{"jsonrpc","2.0"},{"method",method},{"params",params}})`.
4. Tests suite `RpcServer`: build an input `std::stringstream` with 2 framed requests (`a.echo` ids 1 and 2) → after `run` returns 0 the output stream contains 2 framed responses with ids 1 and 2 in order (parse them back with `read_message`); a body that is not JSON produces a `-32700` response and the loop continues; a handler that calls `server.request_stop()` makes `run` return after its response; `notify` writes a framed notification without an `id`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R RpcServer` → all pass.

Title `# rpc module`; sections `## Framing` (exact byte format), `## Dispatch` (error mapping table: PvError → its code; json exception → -32602; other → -32603), `## Notifications` (thread-safe; from any thread), `## Adding a method` (in your module's `src/register.cpp`: `reg.methods.add("ns.name", [&reg](const Json& p) { … });`).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " engine/modules/rpc/README.md` → `4`.

#### P1-RPC-009 — Connections and fan-out notifier (new architecture)
**Files:** `engine/modules/rpc/include/pv/rpc/fanout.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/src/fanout.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/include/pv/rpc/connection.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/src/connection.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/tests/connection_test.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/rpc/README.md` (edit)
**Refs:** R8, R9
**Why:** the engine must serve several local clients (desktop over a pipe, VS Code over TCP 7700) with one method table and send notifications to all of them.
**Steps:**
1. `fanout.hpp`: `class FanoutNotifier : public Notifier { public: int add(Notifier* sink); void remove(int id); std::size_t size() const; void notify(const std::string& method, const Json& params) override; };` — thread-safe (one `std::mutex`); `notify` copies the sink list under the lock, then calls each sink outside it; a sink that throws is removed.
2. `connection.hpp`: `struct ByteStream { virtual ~ByteStream() = default; virtual std::size_t read_some(char* buf, std::size_t n) = 0; /* 0 = closed */ virtual void write_all(const char* data, std::size_t n) = 0; virtual void close() = 0; };` and `class Connection : public Notifier { public: using Gate = std::function<std::optional<Json>(const Json& request)>; Connection(std::unique_ptr<ByteStream> stream, std::mutex& dispatch_mutex, Gate gate = {}); int run(const MethodTable& table); void notify(const std::string& method, const Json& params) override; void close(); };`.
3. `connection.cpp`: wrap the `ByteStream` in a small `std::streambuf` so `read_message` / `write_message` from `framing.hpp` are reused unchanged; `run` reads messages until the stream closes; for each request: if `gate` returns a JSON error object, answer with it; otherwise lock `dispatch_mutex` and call the same dispatcher the stdio server uses; writes are serialized with an internal mutex (responses and notifications may come from different threads).
4. Tests (suite `RpcConnection`): an in-memory `ByteStream` pair; a request gets its response; a gate that rejects `graph.node` produces the error; `FanoutNotifier` with two recording sinks delivers to both; after `remove` only one receives.
5. README: section `## Connections and fan-out` describing both classes.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R RpcConnection` → pass.

#### P1-PARSE-001 — Module skeleton and raw extraction structs
**Files:** `engine/modules/parse/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/include/pv/parse/raw.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/tests/raw_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R8
**Why:** every language adapter produces the same raw data.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME parse DEPS pv_core pv_tp_tree_sitter TEST_DEPS pv_tp_ts_python)`
2. `raw.hpp`:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include "pv/core/types.hpp"

namespace pv::parse {

struct RawDefinition {
    std::string kind;              // "class" or "function"
    std::string name;              // e.g. "start"
    std::string qualname;          // unique in-file qualname, e.g. "App.start" or "helper~2"
    std::string parent_qualname;   // "" = module level
    bool parent_is_class = false;  // true -> this function is a method
    core::Span span;
    int complexity = 1;
    std::string signature;         // first line of the definition, trimmed, max 200 chars
    std::string docstring;         // "" if none, max 1000 chars
};

struct RawImport {
    std::string module;            // as written: "os.path", ".utils", "..", "..pkg"
    std::string name;              // from-import symbol; "" for plain import; "*" for wildcard
    std::string alias;             // "" if none
    int line = 0;
    std::string scope_qualname;    // "" = module level
};

struct RawCall {
    std::string name;              // called identifier, e.g. "get_user"
    std::string object;            // text before the last ".", e.g. "self" or "db.session"; "" for plain calls
    int line = 0;
    std::string caller_qualname;   // enclosing definition qualname; "" = module level
};

struct RawInherit {
    std::string class_qualname;
    std::string base;              // as written: "Base" or "models.Model"
    int line = 0;
};

struct FileExtraction {
    std::string file_path;         // relative, normalized
    std::string language;          // adapter id
    int loc = 0;                   // number of lines of the file
    bool has_syntax_errors = false;
    bool has_main_guard = false;   // entry-point marker (Python: if __name__ == "__main__")
    std::string module_docstring;
    std::vector<RawDefinition> definitions;
    std::vector<RawImport> imports;
    std::vector<RawCall> calls;
    std::vector<RawInherit> inherits;
};

}  // namespace pv::parse
```
3. Test suite `ParseRaw`: a default `RawDefinition` has `complexity == 1` and `parent_is_class == false`; a default `FileExtraction` has empty vectors.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R ParseRaw` → pass.

**Files:** `engine/modules/parse/include/pv/parse/project_index.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/src/project_index.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/tests/project_index_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7

```cpp
struct ProjectIndex {
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string> module_to_file;                 // "app.utils" -> "app/utils.py"
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> file_to_modules;   // file -> its module names
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string>> file_symbols; // file -> (qualname -> node id)
    std::unordered_set<std::string> top_levels;                                  // first segments of module names

    void add_module_name(const std::string& module_name, const std::string& file_path);
    void add_symbol(const std::string& file_path, const std::string& qualname, const std::string& node_id);
    std::optional<std::string> file_for_module(const std::string& module_name) const;
    std::optional<std::string> symbol_id(const std::string& file_path, const std::string& qualname) const;
    bool has_top_level(const std::string& segment) const;
};
```
2. `add_module_name`: if the name is empty do nothing; if not yet in `module_to_file`, insert (first mapping wins); always append the name to `file_to_modules[file_path]` if not already present; insert the text before the first `.` (or the whole name) into `top_levels`.
3. `add_symbol` sets `file_symbols[file][qualname] = node_id`. The getters return `nullopt` when missing.
4. Tests suite `ParseIndex`: add `"app.utils"`→`"app/utils.py"` then `"app.utils"`→`"other.py"` → `file_for_module("app.utils") == "app/utils.py"`; `has_top_level("app")` true; `symbol_id("app/utils.py","normalize")` after `add_symbol` returns the id; unknown lookups return nullopt.

#### P1-PARSE-003 — Language adapter interface and registry
**Files:** `engine/modules/parse/include/pv/parse/adapter.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/include/pv/parse/registry.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/src/registry.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/parse/tests/registry_test.cpp` (create)

```cpp
#pragma once
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include "pv/parse/project_index.hpp"
#include "pv/parse/raw.hpp"

namespace pv::parse {

struct ImportTarget {
    std::string node_id;        // resolved project node (module, class, function…) or ""
    std::string external_name;  // top-level external package name (e.g. "numpy") or ""
};                              // both empty = could not resolve

class LanguageAdapter {
public:
    virtual ~LanguageAdapter() = default;
    virtual std::string id() const = 0;                         // "python"
    virtual std::vector<std::string> extensions() const = 0;    // lower-case, e.g. {".py", ".pyi"}
    virtual FileExtraction extract(const std::string& rel_path, const std::string& source) const = 0;
    virtual std::vector<std::string> module_names(const std::string& rel_path) const = 0; // preferred name first
    virtual ImportTarget resolve_import(const RawImport& imp, const std::string& importer_file,
                                        const ProjectIndex& index) const = 0;
    virtual std::string self_keyword() const = 0;               // "self" for Python, "this" for JS/Java
};

}  // namespace pv::parse
```
2. `registry.hpp`:
```cpp
class AdapterRegistry {
public:
    void add(std::unique_ptr<LanguageAdapter> adapter);  // duplicate id or claimed extension -> PvError(err::Conflict)
    const LanguageAdapter* for_extension(const std::string& extension) const; // case-insensitive; nullptr if none
    const LanguageAdapter* by_id(const std::string& id) const;
    std::vector<const LanguageAdapter*> all() const;      // sorted by id
    std::vector<std::string> all_extensions() const;      // sorted, lower-case
private:
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<LanguageAdapter>> adapters_;
    std::map<std::string, const LanguageAdapter*> by_extension_;
};
```

```cpp
public:
    explicit TsTree(TSTree* tree);

};

    TsParser(const TsParser&) = delete;
    TsParser& operator=(const TsParser&) = delete;

private:
    TSParser* parser_ = nullptr;
};

core::Span node_span(TSNode node);                                // lines +1 (1-based), columns as-is
std::string node_type(TSNode node);                               // ts_node_type
TSNode child_by_field(TSNode node, const char* field);           // ts_node_child_by_field_name(node, field, strlen(field))
```

#### P1-PY-003 — Module names from paths
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/module_names.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/module_names_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** Python imports use dotted module names; we derive them from file paths.
**Steps:**
1. Implement `module_names_for(rel_path)`:
   1. `dir = core::path_parent(rel_path)`, `stem = core::path_stem(rel_path)`.
   2. `parts = dir.empty() ? {} : core::split(dir, '/')`; if `stem != "__init__"` push `stem`.
   3. If `parts` is empty return `{}`.
   4. `full = core::join(parts, ".")`. If `parts.size() > 1` and `parts[0]` is `"src"` or `"lib"`: return `{join(parts without first, "."), full}` (preferred name first). Otherwise return `{full}`.
2. Tests suite `LangPyModuleNames`: `"app/models.py"` → `{"app.models"}`; `"src/app/main.py"` → `{"app.main","src.app.main"}`; `"app/__init__.py"` → `{"app"}`; `"main.py"` → `{"main"}`; `"__init__.py"` → `{}`; `"src/__init__.py"` → `{"src"}`; `"lib/x.pyi"` → `{"x","lib.x"}`; `"a/b.ipynb"` → `{"a.b"}`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangPyModuleNames` → all pass.

#### P1-PY-004 — Relative import resolution
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/relative.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/relative_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** `from .models import User` must become `app.models`.
**Steps:**
1. Implement `resolve_relative_module(importer_file, module_text)`:
   1. `dots` = number of leading `.` characters; `rest` = the text after them.
   2. `names = module_names_for(importer_file)`; `base = names.empty() ? "" : names[0]`.
   3. `package = (core::path_stem(importer_file) == "__init__") ? base : (text of base before its last "." , or "" if base has no ".")`.
   4. `parts = package.empty() ? {} : core::split(package, '.')`.
   5. `ups = dots - 1`. If `ups > 0` and `ups >= parts.size()` → return `""` (beyond the top-level package). Else remove the last `ups` items of `parts`.
   6. If `rest` is not empty push `rest`. Return `core::join(parts, ".")`.
2. Tests suite `LangPyRelative`: `("app/services.py", ".models") == "app.models"`; `("app/services.py", ".") == "app"`; `("app/api/routes.py", "..services") == "app.services"`; `("app/api/routes.py", "...x") == ""`; `("app/services.py", "..x") == ""`; `("app/api/__init__.py", ".routes") == "app.api.routes"`; `("main.py", ".utils") == "utils"`; `("src/app/services.py", ".models") == "app.models"`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangPyRelative` → all pass.

2. `strip_string_literal(literal)`: remove leading prefix letters among `rRuUbBfF`; then if it starts with `"""` or `'''` remove 3 characters from both ends (if long enough); else if it starts with `"` or `'` remove 1 from both ends; return `core::trim` of the result.

#### P1-PY-006 — Cyclomatic complexity
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/complexity.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/complexity_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** complexity feeds hotspots and risk.
**Steps:**
1. Implement exactly:
```cpp
int compute_complexity(TSNode definition) {
    static const std::unordered_set<std::string> kDecision = {
        "if_statement", "elif_clause", "for_statement", "while_statement", "except_clause",
        "conditional_expression", "boolean_operator", "for_in_clause", "if_clause", "case_clause"};
    TSNode body = parse::child_by_field(definition, "body");
    if (ts_node_is_null(body)) return 1;
    int count = 1;
    std::vector<TSNode> stack{body};
    while (!stack.empty()) {
        TSNode n = stack.back();
        stack.pop_back();
        const std::string t = parse::node_type(n);
        if (t == "function_definition" || t == "class_definition") continue;  // nested defs count separately
        if (kDecision.count(t)) ++count;
        for (TSNode c : parse::named_children(n)) stack.push_back(c);
    }
    return count;
}
```
2. Tests suite `LangPyComplexity` (parse a snippet, take the first `function_definition`): `"def f():\n    return 1\n"` → 1; `"def f(x):\n    if x:\n        return 1\n    elif x > 2:\n        return 2\n    return 3\n"` → 3; `"def f(a, b):\n    return a and b or a\n"` → 3; `"def f(xs):\n    for x in xs:\n        while x:\n            x -= 1\n"` → 3; `"def f():\n    def g(x):\n        if x:\n            pass\n    return g\n"` → 1.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangPyComplexity` → all pass.

#### P1-PY-007 — Main guard detection

#### P1-PY-008 — Walker: definitions
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/walker.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_python/src/walker.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/walker_defs_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** one tree walk collects all facts with the correct enclosing scope.
**Steps:**
1. `src/walker.hpp` (private header):
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>
#include <tree_sitter/api.h>
#include "pv/parse/raw.hpp"

namespace pv::lang_python {
class PythonWalker {
public:
    PythonWalker(const std::string& source, parse::FileExtraction& out);
    void walk(TSNode root);
private:
    void visit(TSNode node);
    void on_definition(TSNode node, bool is_class);
    void on_import(TSNode node);
    void on_import_from(TSNode node);
    void on_call(TSNode node);
    void on_bases(TSNode class_node, const std::string& class_qualname);
    std::string current_qualname() const;
    bool current_is_class() const;
    std::string unique_qualname(const std::string& base);
    const std::string& source_;
    parse::FileExtraction& out_;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, bool>> scope_;  // (qualname, is_class), innermost last
    std::unordered_map<std::string, int> seen_;
};
}  // namespace pv::lang_python
```
2. `walker.cpp` — implement in this task: constructor, `walk` (= `visit(root)`), `current_qualname` (`scope_` empty → `""`, else last qualname), `current_is_class`, `unique_qualname` (`n = ++seen_[base]`; `n == 1 ? base : base + "~" + std::to_string(n)`), `visit`, `on_definition`. The other `on_*` methods get empty bodies for now.
```cpp
void PythonWalker::visit(TSNode node) {
    const std::string type = parse::node_type(node);
    if (type == "class_definition") { on_definition(node, true); return; }
    if (type == "function_definition") { on_definition(node, false); return; }
    if (type == "import_statement") { on_import(node); return; }
    if (type == "import_from_statement") { on_import_from(node); return; }
    if (type == "call") { on_call(node); }  // no return: calls nested in the arguments are visited below
    for (TSNode child : parse::named_children(node)) visit(child);
}

void PythonWalker::on_definition(TSNode node, bool is_class) {
    TSNode name_node = parse::child_by_field(node, "name");
    if (ts_node_is_null(name_node)) return;
    const std::string name = parse::node_text(name_node, source_);
    const std::string parent = current_qualname();
    parse::RawDefinition def;
    def.kind = is_class ? "class" : "function";
    def.name = name;
    def.qualname = unique_qualname(parent.empty() ? name : parent + "." + name);
    def.parent_qualname = parent;
    def.parent_is_class = current_is_class();
    def.span = parse::node_span(node);
    def.complexity = is_class ? 1 : compute_complexity(node);
    def.signature = first_line(parse::node_text(node, source_), 200);
    TSNode body = parse::child_by_field(node, "body");
    def.docstring = ts_node_is_null(body) ? "" : extract_docstring(body, source_);
    out_.definitions.push_back(def);
    if (is_class) on_bases(node, def.qualname);
    TSNode params = parse::child_by_field(node, "parameters");
    if (!ts_node_is_null(params)) visit(params);   // default values run in the outer scope
    scope_.push_back({def.qualname, is_class});
    if (!ts_node_is_null(body)) visit(body);
    scope_.pop_back();
}
```
3. Tests suite `LangPyWalkerDefs`: parse the content of fixture `app/models.py` (read with `core::read_file_text(std::string(PV_TEST_FIXTURES) + "/pyproj_small/app/models.py")`), run the walker into a `FileExtraction`; expect 5 definitions in this order: `Base` (class, span 4–6, parent ""), `Base.save` (function, parent "Base", `parent_is_class` true, span 5–6), `User` (class, 9–17), `User.__init__` (10–12), `User.display` (function, 14–17, complexity 2). Also: source `"def h():\n    pass\ndef h():\n    pass\n"` → qualnames `h`, `h~2`; nested `"def a():\n    def b():\n        pass\n"` → `a`, `a.b` with `b.parent_is_class == false`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangPyWalkerDefs` → all pass.

#### P1-PY-009 — Walker: imports
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/walker.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/walker_imports_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** imports connect modules.
**Steps:**
1. `on_import(node)` (`import a.b as c, d`): for each named child: if type `dotted_name` → `RawImport{module = text}`; if type `aliased_import` → `module = text(child_by_field(child,"name"))`, `alias = text(child_by_field(child,"alias"))`; other types → skip. Set `line = node_span(node).start_line`, `scope_qualname = current_qualname()`, push to `out_.imports`.
2. `on_import_from(node)` (`from X import a, b as c` / `from X import *`): `module_node = child_by_field(node,"module_name")`; `module = text(module_node)` with all spaces removed. For each named child whose `ts_node_start_byte` differs from `module_node`'s: type `dotted_name` → `name = text`; `aliased_import` → `name` and `alias` from its fields; `wildcard_import` → `name = "*"`; else skip. Each becomes one `RawImport{module, name, alias, line, scope}`.
3. Tests suite `LangPyWalkerImports`: fixture `app/services.py` → imports exactly `[(".models","User","",2), (".utils","normalize","",3), (".utils","is_valid","",3), (".","utils","",4)]` (module, name, alias, line); fixture `app/api/routes.py` → `[("app.services","UserService","",2), ("app.utils","","u",3)]`; snippet `"from os import *\n"` → `[("os","*","",1)]`; snippet `"def f():\n    import json\n"` → scope `"f"`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangPyWalkerImports` → all pass.

#### P1-PY-010 — Walker: calls
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/walker.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/walker_calls_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** calls are the main dependency edges between functions.
**Steps:**
1. `on_call(node)`: `fn = child_by_field(node,"function")`; `RawCall call; call.line = node_span(node).start_line; call.caller_qualname = current_qualname();` If `node_type(fn) == "identifier"` → `call.name = text(fn)`. Else if `"attribute"` → `call.name = text(child_by_field(fn,"attribute"))`, `call.object = text(child_by_field(fn,"object"))` cut to 200 characters. Any other type → return without adding. Push to `out_.calls`.

#### P1-PY-013 — Import resolution: plain imports
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/resolve.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_python/src/python_adapter.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/resolve_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** turn `import app.utils as u` into a link to the real module node.
**Steps:**
1. In `resolve.cpp` implement `resolve_python_import` for plain imports (`imp.name` empty) and wildcard (`imp.name == "*"`); from-imports with a name return `{}` for now (next task):
   1. If `imp.module` starts with `.` → `base = resolve_relative_module(importer_file, imp.module)`; if `base` is empty return `{}`. Else `base = imp.module`.
   2. `first = base` up to the first `.`.
   3. Helper `module_node(name)`: if `index.file_for_module(name)` → `core::make_node_id(core::NodeKind::Module, file, "")`.
   4. Try `candidate = base`, then remove the last `.segment` repeatedly: return the first `module_node(candidate)` found as `{node_id, ""}`.
   5. Not found: if `imp.module` starts with `.` or `index.has_top_level(first)` → return `{}` (internal but unresolved); else return `{"", first}` (external package).

#### P1-PY-014 — Import resolution: from-imports
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_python/src/resolve.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/resolve_test.cpp` (edit)

Add tests (suite `LangPyResolve`, same index): importer `app/services.py`: `{module:".models", name:"User"}` → `class:app/models.py#User`; `{module:".", name:"utils"}` → `module:app/utils.py`; `{module:".utils", name:"unknown_fn"}` → `module:app/utils.py`; `{module:"app.nothing", name:"x"}` → `{}`; `{module:"numpy", name:"array"}` → external `numpy`; importer `app/api/routes.py`: `{module:"...x", name:"y"}` → `{}`; `{module:"app.services", name:"UserService"}` with no symbol in index → `module:app/services.py`.

#### P1-BUILDR-002 — Parallel extraction
**Files:** `engine/modules/builder/src/extract_all.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/tests/fake_adapter.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/tests/extract_all_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** parse files on several threads; one bad file never stops the import.
**Steps:**
1. `extract_all(adapters, files, on_progress, threads, errors)`:
   1. `n = files.size()`; result vector of `n` empty `FileExtraction`s. If `threads <= 0` use `std::clamp(std::thread::hardware_concurrency(), 1u, 8u)`; never more threads than files.
   2. Shared `std::atomic<size_t> next{0}`, `std::atomic<int> done{0}`, `std::mutex m`.
   3. Each worker loops `i = next++` while `i < n`: `adapter = adapters.for_extension(core::path_extension(files[i].rel_path))`; if null → skip (count as done). Else `try { text = core::read_file_text(files[i].abs_path); result[i] = adapter->extract(files[i].rel_path, text); } catch (const std::exception& e) { result[i].file_path = rel; result[i].language = adapter->id(); lock m; errors.push_back(rel + ": " + e.what()); }`. Then `d = ++done`; lock `m` and call `on_progress(d, n)` if it is set.
   4. Join all threads; sort `errors`; return `result`.
2. `tests/fake_adapter.hpp`: class `FakeAdapter : parse::LanguageAdapter` with id `"fake"`, extensions `{".fk"}`, `extract` returns a `FileExtraction{file_path=rel, language="fake", loc=core::count_lines(source)}` and throws `std::runtime_error("boom")` if the source contains `"BOOM"`; `module_names(rel)` returns `{core::path_stem(rel)}`; `resolve_import` returns `{module node id of index.file_for_module(imp.module)}` if found, else `{"", imp.module}`; `self_keyword()` returns `"self"`.
3. Tests suite `BuilderExtractAll` (use a temp folder with `std::filesystem`): 20 files `f<i>.fk` with `"a\nb\n"`, one containing `BOOM` → 21 results; 1 error that starts with its rel path; progress callback called 21 times, last call `(21,21)`; every result for a good file has `loc == 2`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R BuilderExtractAll` → all pass.

#### P1-BUILDR-003 — Definition nodes
**Files:** `engine/modules/builder/src/definitions.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/tests/definitions_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Needs:** P1-PY-015 (this and all later builder tests use the real Python adapter)
**Why:** classes, functions and methods become nodes under their module.
**Steps:**
1. `add_definition_nodes(g, fx, adapter)`:
   1. `module_id = core::make_node_id(Module, fx.file_path, "")`; if the module node exists, set its `qualified_name = adapter.module_names(fx.file_path)` first element (or `""`), `span = {1,0,fx.loc,0}`, `language = fx.language`.
   2. Map `kind_of[qualname] = definition_kind(def)` for all definitions.
   3. For each definition: `kind = kind_of[def.qualname]`; `id = make_node_id(kind, fx.file_path, def.qualname)`; `parent_id = def.parent_qualname.empty() ? module_id : make_node_id(kind_of[def.parent_qualname], fx.file_path, def.parent_qualname)` (if the parent qualname is not in the map, use `module_id`); `name = def.name`; `qualified_name = module_qn.empty() ? def.qualname : module_qn + "." + def.qualname`; `file_path`, `language`, `span = def.span`, `level = core::level_of(kind)`, `metrics.complexity = def.complexity`, `metrics.loc = span.end_line - span.start_line + 1`. `g.add_node(node)`.
2. Tests suite `BuilderDefinitions`: structure nodes for `app/models.py` + `PythonAdapter().extract` of the fixture file → nodes `class:app/models.py#User` (parent module, qualified `app.models.User`, loc 9), `method:app/models.py#User.display` (parent `class:app/models.py#User`, complexity 2, level 4); module node `span.end_line == 17` and `qualified_name == "app.models"`.

#### P1-BUILDR-005 — Link imports
**Files:** `engine/modules/builder/src/link_imports.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/tests/link_imports_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** create `imports` edges, external nodes and name bindings.
**Steps:**
1. `link_imports(g, fx, adapter, index)`:
   1. `module_id` of the file. `FileBindings bindings`.
   2. For each import: `target = adapter.resolve_import(imp, fx.file_path, index)`; `local = !imp.alias.empty() ? imp.alias : (!imp.name.empty() && imp.name != "*" ? imp.name : imp.module)`.
   3. If `target.node_id` is not empty, the node exists and it is not `module_id`: `g.add_edge(Edge{make_edge_id(Imports, module_id, target), Imports, module_id, target.node_id, 1, true})`; if `imp.name != "*"` set `bindings[local] = target.node_id`.
   4. Else if `target.external_name` is not empty: `ext = make_node_id(External, "", name)`; if missing add node {kind External, name, qualified_name = name, parent `project:`, level 1}; add the imports edge `module_id → ext`; `bindings[local] = ext`.
   5. Return `bindings`.
2. Tests suite `BuilderLinkImports`: build structure + definitions + index for all 8 fixture files (use the Python adapter; helper function in the test file), then run `link_imports` for `app/services.py` → 4 imports edges from `module:app/services.py` to `class:app/models.py#User`, `function:app/utils.py#normalize`, `function:app/utils.py#is_valid`, `module:app/utils.py`; bindings `utils → module:app/utils.py`, `User → class:app/models.py#User`. For `main.py` → node `external:sys` exists (parent `project:`), binding `sys → external:sys`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R BuilderLinkImports` → all pass.

#### P1-BUILDR-006 — Link calls
**Files:** `engine/modules/builder/src/link_calls.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/tests/link_calls_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** `calls` edges are the most useful dependency information.
**Steps:**
1. `link_calls(g, fx, adapter, index, bindings)`. Helpers: `sym(qn)` = `index.symbol_id(fx.file_path, qn)` or `""`; `kinds` = qualname → `definition_kind`.
2. For each call:
   1. `caller = call.caller_qualname.empty() ? module_id : sym(call.caller_qualname)`; skip if empty.
   2. **Plain call** (`object` empty): `scope = caller_qualname`; loop: `cand = scope.empty() ? name : scope + "." + name`; `target = sym(cand)`; stop if found or `scope` is empty; else drop the last `.segment` of `scope` (or set `""`). If still not found and `bindings` has `name` → that id.
   3. **Self call** (`object == adapter.self_keyword()` or `object == "cls"`): walk `scope` from `caller_qualname` upward; at the first scope whose `kinds[scope] == Class`, `target = sym(scope + "." + name)` and stop.
   4. **Other object**: `holder = bindings[object]` if present; else if the first segment of `object` (before `.`) is bound to an id starting with `external:`, `holder` = that id. Then: `external:` holder → `target = holder`; `module:` holder → `target = index.symbol_id(<file after "module:">, name)`; `class:` holder → file = that node's `file_path`, class qualname = text after `#` → `target = index.symbol_id(file, class_qn + "." + name)`.
   5. **Fallback for plain calls** (object empty) still unresolved: for each distinct binding value that starts with `module:` (sorted), try `index.symbol_id(<file after "module:">, name)`; the first match wins. (This links C/C++ calls to functions of included headers, and similar cases.)
   6. Skip if `target` is empty, equals `caller`, or the node does not exist. Else `g.add_edge(calls edge caller → target, weight 1)`.
3. Tests suite `BuilderLinkCalls` (full fixture as in P1-BUILDR-005, after imports): edges from `method:app/services.py#UserService.get_user` go to exactly `function:app/utils.py#is_valid`, `class:app/models.py#User`, `function:app/utils.py#normalize`, `method:app/services.py#UserService.format_user`; `method:…#UserService.format_user` → `function:app/utils.py#normalize`; `module:main.py` → `external:sys` and `function:main.py#main`; `function:app/api/routes.py#get_user_route` → `class:app/services.py#UserService` and `function:app/utils.py#is_valid`; total calls edges in the graph = 10.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R BuilderLinkCalls` → all pass.

Add `inherits` edge `cls → target` when both exist and differ.

#### P1-BUILDR-012 — Extraction cache hook (new architecture)
**Files:** `engine/modules/builder/include/pv/builder/extraction_cache.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/src/extraction_cache.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/builder/src/extract_all.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/builder/tests/extraction_cache_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** the local cache (P4-ECACHE) keeps extractions of unchanged files so reopening a project does not parse them again; the builder only offers the hook.
**Steps:**
1. `extraction_cache.hpp`: `class ExtractionCache { public: virtual ~ExtractionCache() = default; virtual std::optional<parse::FileExtraction> lookup(const std::string& abs_path, const std::string& language, const std::string& content_hash) = 0; virtual void store(const std::string& abs_path, const std::string& language, const std::string& content_hash, const parse::FileExtraction& fx) = 0; };` plus `void set_extraction_cache(ExtractionCache* cache);` (nullptr = off) and `ExtractionCache* extraction_cache();` and `std::string content_hash(const std::string& bytes);` (64-bit FNV-1a as 16 hex chars).
2. `extract_all.cpp`: when a cache is set, read the file bytes once, compute the hash, try `lookup`; on a hit use it (and skip the parser); on a miss parse as today and `store` the result. Behaviour without a cache is unchanged.
3. Tests (suite `BuilderExtractionCache`): a fake cache counting lookups/stores; the second `extract_all` over the same files has only hits and returns equal extractions.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R Builder` → all pass.

### MODULE P1-SESS — Projects, background loading and registry
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/session/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-BUILDR · P1-RPC
- **Goal:** manage open projects (load in the background, report progress, guard the graph with a lock), define the `Registry` that every module registers into, and expose the `engine.*`, `lang.list` and `project.*` RPC methods.

#### P1-SESS-001 — Project class
**Files:** `engine/modules/session/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/session/include/pv/session/project.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/session/src/project.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/session/tests/project_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** one object per open project holding state, progress and the graph.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME session DEPS pv_builder pv_rpc TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `project.hpp`:
```cpp
#pragma once
#include <mutex>
#include <shared_mutex>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include "pv/graph/graph.hpp"

namespace pv::session {

enum class ProjectState { Idle, Scanning, Parsing, Linking, Ready, Error };
std::string to_string(ProjectState state);   // "idle","scanning","parsing","linking","ready","error"

class Project {
public:
    Project(std::string id, std::string root_path);
    const std::string& id() const;
    const std::string& root_path() const;
    ProjectState state() const;
    void set_state(ProjectState state);
    int files_total() const;
    int files_done() const;
    void set_progress(int done, int total);
    std::string error_message() const;
    void set_error(const std::string& message);   // also sets state Error
    void set_build_info(std::vector<std::string> main_guard_files, std::vector<std::string> syntax_error_files,
                        std::vector<std::string> parse_errors);
    std::vector<std::string> main_guard_files() const;
    std::vector<std::string> syntax_error_files() const;
    std::vector<std::string> parse_errors() const;
    void require_ready() const;   // throws PvError(err::NotReady, "project not ready: " + id)

    template <class F> auto read(F&& fn) const { std::shared_lock lock(graph_mutex_); return fn(graph_); }
    template <class F> auto write(F&& fn) { std::unique_lock lock(graph_mutex_); return fn(graph_); }
    void replace_graph(graph::Graph graph);   // unique lock, move in

private:
    std::string id_;
    std::string root_path_;
    mutable std::mutex state_mutex_;
    ProjectState state_ = ProjectState::Idle;
    int files_done_ = 0;
    int files_total_ = 0;
    std::string error_;
    std::vector<std::string> main_guard_files_;
    std::vector<std::string> syntax_error_files_;
    std::vector<std::string> parse_errors_;
    mutable std::shared_mutex graph_mutex_;
    graph::Graph graph_;
};

}  // namespace pv::session
```
3. Implement in `project.cpp`; every getter/setter of state, progress, error and build info locks `state_mutex_`.
4. Tests suite `SessionProject`: new project is `Idle`; `require_ready()` throws `NotReady`; after `set_state(Ready)` it does not throw; `set_error("x")` → state `Error`, message `"x"`; `replace_graph` then `read([](const graph::Graph& g){ return g.node_count(); })` returns the new count; `to_string(ProjectState::Linking) == "linking"`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R SessionProject` → all pass.

#### P1-SESS-002 — Project manager: open, get, close
**Files:** `engine/modules/session/include/pv/session/project_manager.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/session/src/project_manager.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/session/tests/project_manager_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8, R9
**Why:** create projects, load them in the background and look them up by id.
**Steps:**
1. `project_manager.hpp`:
```cpp
struct OpenOptions { std::vector<std::string> exclude_globs; };

class ProjectManager {
public:
    ProjectManager(const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters, rpc::Notifier& notifier);
    ~ProjectManager();   // joins all loader threads
    ProjectManager(const ProjectManager&) = delete;
    ProjectManager& operator=(const ProjectManager&) = delete;
    std::string open(const std::string& root_path, const OpenOptions& options);
    std::string adopt(const std::string& label, graph::Graph graph);  // registers an already-built graph as a Ready project (used by Phase 2 shared snapshots)
    std::shared_ptr<Project> get(const std::string& id) const;        // PvError(err::ProjectNotFound, "project not found: " + id)
    std::shared_ptr<Project> get_ready(const std::string& id) const;  // get + require_ready
    void close(const std::string& id);                                // unknown id -> ProjectNotFound
    std::vector<std::string> ids() const;                              // sorted
    bool wait_until_settled(const std::string& id, int timeout_ms) const; // true if Ready, false if Error or timeout
    void load_now(const std::shared_ptr<Project>& project, const OpenOptions& options);
private:
    void notify_progress(const Project& project);
    const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters_;
    rpc::Notifier& notifier_;
    mutable std::mutex mutex_;
    std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<Project>> projects_;
    std::vector<std::thread> threads_;
    int counter_ = 0;
};
```
2. `open`: normalize the path; if a project with that root is already open, return its id. Else `id = "p" + std::to_string(++counter_)`, create the project, store it, start `threads_.emplace_back([this, project, options] { load_now(project, options); })`, return id.
3. `load_now` (runs the whole pipeline, catches everything):
```cpp
try {
    project->set_state(ProjectState::Scanning);
    notify_progress(*project);
    fs::DiscoverOptions dopt;
    dopt.extensions = adapters_.all_extensions();
    dopt.exclude_globs = options.exclude_globs;
    fs::DiscoverResult found = fs::discover_files(project->root_path(), dopt);
    project->set_progress(0, static_cast<int>(found.files.size()));
    project->set_state(ProjectState::Parsing);
    notify_progress(*project);
    builder::BuildResult result = builder::build_project(
        adapters_, project->root_path(), found.files,
        [&](int done, int total) {
            project->set_progress(done, total);
            if (done % 50 == 0 || done == total) notify_progress(*project);
        },
        [&](const std::string& phase) {
            if (phase == "linking") { project->set_state(ProjectState::Linking); notify_progress(*project); }
        });
    project->set_build_info(result.main_guard_files, result.syntax_error_files, result.errors);
    project->replace_graph(std::move(result.graph));
    project->set_state(ProjectState::Ready);
    notify_progress(*project);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
    project->set_error(e.what());
    notify_progress(*project);
}
```
4. `notify_progress` sends `project.progress` with `{"project_id","state","files_total","files_done"}`. `wait_until_settled` polls every 10 ms.
5. `adopt(label, graph)`: `id = "p" + std::to_string(++counter_)`; create a `Project(id, "snapshot:" + label)`; `replace_graph(std::move(graph))`; set progress `(n, n)` with `n` = number of Module nodes; state `Ready`; store it; return id. No thread is started. (Such projects have no files on disk; source requests fail with an I/O error, which the UI handles.)
5. Tests suite `SessionManager` (Python adapter + `rpc::RecordingNotifier`): `open(<fixture pyproj_small>)` returns `"p1"`; opening the same path again returns `"p1"`; `wait_until_settled("p1", 10000)` is true; the graph has 25 nodes; notifications include states `scanning`, `parsing`, `linking`, `ready` in that order (the last one is `ready`); opening a missing folder → settles with `Error` and a message containing `folder not found`; `get("nope")` throws `ProjectNotFound`; `close("p1")` then `ids()` is empty; `adopt("demo", <a graph with 2 nodes>)` returns a new id whose project is `Ready`, has `root_path() == "snapshot:demo"` and 2 nodes.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R SessionManager` → all pass.

```cpp
#pragma once
#include <memory>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include "pv/session/registry.hpp"

namespace pv::session {
class TestEnv {
public:
    explicit TestEnv(std::unique_ptr<parse::LanguageAdapter> adapter) {
        adapters.add(std::move(adapter));
        projects = std::make_unique<ProjectManager>(adapters, notifier);
        reg = std::make_unique<Registry>(Registry{methods, cli, *projects, adapters, notifier, [] {}});
    }
    std::string open_and_wait(const std::string& root) {
        std::string id = projects->open(root, {});
        if (!projects->wait_until_settled(id, 20000)) throw std::runtime_error("project did not load: " + root);
        return id;
    }
    rpc::Json call(const std::string& method, const rpc::Json& params) { return methods.call(method, params); }
    rpc::MethodTable methods;
    rpc::CliTable cli;
    parse::AdapterRegistry adapters;
    rpc::RecordingNotifier notifier;
    std::unique_ptr<ProjectManager> projects;
    std::unique_ptr<Registry> reg;
};
inline std::string pyproj_small_path() {
    return std::string(PV_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR) + "/modules/lang_python/tests/fixtures/pyproj_small";
}
}  // namespace pv::session
```

### MODULE P1-EAPP — pv-engine executable
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/app/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-SESS · P1-PY
- **Goal:** the `pv-engine` program: wires all modules together, runs the stdio JSON-RPC server, and supports CLI sub-commands.

#### P1-EAPP-001 — main.cpp and app CMake
**Files:** `engine/app/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/app/main.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8, R9
**Why:** the executable the desktop app starts.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly:
```cmake
pv_generate_registry(${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/registry_gen.cpp)
add_executable(pv-engine main.cpp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/registry_gen.cpp)
get_property(pv_module_targets GLOBAL PROPERTY PV_MODULE_TARGETS)
target_link_libraries(pv-engine PRIVATE ${pv_module_targets})
```
2. `main.cpp` exactly:
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <io.h>
#endif
#include "pv/core/log.hpp"
#include "pv/core/version.hpp"
#include "pv/parse/registry.hpp"
#include "pv/rpc/cli_table.hpp"
#include "pv/rpc/method_table.hpp"
#include "pv/rpc/server.hpp"
#include "pv/session/project_manager.hpp"
#include "pv/session/registry.hpp"

namespace pv::app {
void register_all_modules(pv::session::Registry& reg);
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    _setmode(_fileno(stdin), _O_BINARY);
    _setmode(_fileno(stdout), _O_BINARY);
#endif
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    pv::rpc::StdioServer server(std::cin, std::cout);
    pv::rpc::MethodTable methods;
    pv::rpc::CliTable cli;
    pv::parse::AdapterRegistry adapters;
    pv::session::ProjectManager projects(adapters, server);
    pv::session::Registry reg{methods, cli, projects, adapters, server, [&server] { server.request_stop(); }};
    pv::app::register_all_modules(reg);

    if (argc >= 2) {
        const std::string command = argv[1];
        if (command == "--version") {
            std::cout << pv::core::kEngineVersion << "\n";
            return 0;
        }
        if (cli.has(command)) {
            return cli.run(command, std::vector<std::string>(argv + 2, argv + argc));
        }
        std::cerr << "unknown command: " << command << "\n";
        return 2;
    }
    pv::core::log_info(std::string("pv-engine ") + pv::core::kEngineVersion + " ready");
    return server.run(methods);
}
```
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --preset dev && cmake --build --preset dev && ./build/app/Debug/pv-engine.exe --version` (Linux/macOS: `./build/app/pv-engine --version`) → prints `0.1.0`.

2. Functions: `send(proc, obj)` writes `Content-Length` framing + JSON bytes to `proc.stdin` and flushes; `read(proc)` reads header lines until an empty line, parses the length, reads the body, returns the JSON object; `request(proc, id, method, params)` sends and then reads messages until one has the same `id` (ignore notifications, but count them).

Print `SMOKE OK` and exit 0; on any failure print the reason and exit 1.

### MODULE P1-IMPACT — "What breaks if I change this?"
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/impact/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-SESS · P1-PY
- **Goal:** reverse-dependency analysis with distances, ancestor chains (for highlighting at any level) and a risk score (`impact.analyze`).

#### P1-IMPACT-001 — Types and reverse BFS
**Files:** `engine/modules/impact/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/impact/include/pv/impact/impact.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/impact/src/impact.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/impact/tests/impact_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R9
**Why:** find every node that depends on the changed node, directly or indirectly.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME impact DEPS pv_session TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `impact.hpp` (namespace `pv::impact`):
```cpp
struct AffectedNode {
    std::string node_id;
    int distance = 0;
    core::EdgeKind via = core::EdgeKind::Calls;
    std::string from_id;                    // the node it depends on
    std::vector<std::string> ancestor_ids;  // project root first, node itself last
};
struct Risk { int score = 0; std::string level; std::vector<std::string> factors; };
struct ImpactResult { std::string root_id; std::vector<AffectedNode> affected; Risk risk; };

ImpactResult analyze_impact(const graph::Graph& g, const std::string& node_id, int max_depth);
Risk compute_risk(const graph::Graph& g, const std::vector<AffectedNode>& affected);
nlohmann::json to_json(const ImpactResult& result);
```
3. `analyze_impact` (leave `risk` default in this task):
```text
g.node(node_id)                                  // throws NodeNotFound
max_depth = clamp(max_depth, 1, 10)
inside   = {node_id} ∪ descendants(node_id)
visited  = inside
frontier = sorted(inside)
for d = 1 .. max_depth:
    next = []
    for cur in frontier:
        for e in in_edges(cur) sorted by e.id:
            s = e.source_id
            if s in visited: continue
            visited.add(s)
            affected.push({s, d, e.kind, cur, g.ancestors(s)})
            next.push(s)
    if next is empty: break
    frontier = sorted(next)
sort affected by (distance, node_id)
```
4. Tests suite `ImpactBfs` using the graph module's sample graph (`#include "../../graph/tests/sample_graph.hpp"` — reading another module's test helper is allowed): impact of `method:app/a.py#C.m` → 2 affected, both distance 1: `function:app/a.py#f` (via calls, from `method:app/a.py#C.m`) and `function:main.py#main`; impact of `module:app/a.py` → exactly `function:main.py#main` (distance 1, via calls) and `module:main.py` (distance 1, via imports); `ancestor_ids` of `function:main.py#main` = `{"project:","module:main.py","function:main.py#main"}`; unknown node throws.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R ImpactBfs` → all pass.

#### P1-IMPACT-002 — Risk score
**Files:** `engine/modules/impact/src/impact.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/impact/tests/risk_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** one number and level tell the user how dangerous a change is.
**Steps:**
1. `compute_risk(g, affected)`:
   - `d1` = count with distance 1; `dn` = count with distance ≥ 2.
   - `groups` = number of distinct "package groups": for each affected node, walk its `ancestor_ids` from the end toward the root and take the first id whose node kind is Package; if none, use `"project:"`.
   - `score = min(100, d1*8 + dn*3 + max(0, groups-1)*10)`.
   - `level`: score < 20 → `"low"`; < 45 → `"medium"`; < 70 → `"high"`; else `"critical"`.
   - `factors` = exactly 3 strings: `"<d1> direct dependents"`, `"<dn> indirect dependents"`, `"spans <groups> packages"`.
   - With no affected nodes: score 0, level `"low"`, factors `"0 direct dependents"`, `"0 indirect dependents"`, `"spans 0 packages"`.
2. Call `compute_risk` at the end of `analyze_impact` and store it in `result.risk`.
3. Tests suite `ImpactRisk` (sample graph): impact of `method:app/a.py#C.m` → score 26, level `medium`, factors `{"2 direct dependents","0 indirect dependents","spans 2 packages"}`; impact of `module:app/a.py` → score 16, level `low`; impact of `function:main.py#main` (nobody depends on it) → score 0, `low`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R ImpactRisk` → all pass.

#### P1-CTX-001 — Context pack builder
**Files:** `engine/modules/context/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/context/include/pv/context/context.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/context/src/context.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/context/tests/context_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R11
**Why:** give the AI exactly the facts it needs, with node ids it may cite.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME context DEPS pv_session TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `context.hpp` (namespace `pv::context`): `nlohmann::json build_context_pack(const graph::Graph& g, const std::string& root_path, const std::string& node_id, int max_chars);`
3. Build this JSON (all lists sorted by `id`; `ref(n)` = `{"id","kind","name"}`; `ref_file(n)` = `ref(n)` + `"file_path"`):
   - `node`: the full Node JSON.
   - `source`: for Module, Class, Function, Method nodes `session::source_text_for(root_path, node)` (catch `PvError` → `""`); for other kinds `""`. If longer than `max_chars`, keep the first `max_chars` characters and set `source_truncated` true, else false.
   - `parent`: `ref(parent)` or JSON `null` for the project node.
   - `children`: `ref` of up to 50 children.
   - `callers`: `ref_file` of sources of **calls** in-edges, max 20.
   - `callees`: `ref_file` of targets of **calls** out-edges, max 20.
   - `imports`: for Module nodes `ref` of targets of **imports** out-edges (max 30); for other kinds `[]`.
   - `related_node_ids`: sorted unique ids of node, parent, children, callers, callees, imports.
   - `approx_tokens`: `(dump of the object built so far).size() / 4`, added last.
4. Tests suite `ContextPack` (TestEnv + fixture, build inside `read`): pack for `method:app/services.py#UserService.get_user` → `callers` empty; `callees` ids exactly `class:app/models.py#User`, `function:app/utils.py#is_valid`, `function:app/utils.py#normalize`, `method:app/services.py#UserService.format_user`; `parent.id == "class:app/services.py#UserService"`; `source` starts with `"    def get_user(self, user_id):"`; `approx_tokens > 0`. Pack for `module:app/services.py` → `imports` has 4 ids; `children` = `[class:app/services.py#UserService]`. Pack with `max_chars = 10` for `module:app/models.py` → `source.size() == 10` and `source_truncated == true`. Pack for `project:` → `parent` is null and `source == ""`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R ContextPack` → all pass.

#### P1-CTX-002 — context.for_node RPC method

### MODULE P1-CRPC — Phase 1 RPC contracts (JSON Schemas)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** CONTRACTS
- **Owns:** `contracts/rpc/engine/**` · `contracts/rpc/lang/**` · `contracts/rpc/project/**` · `contracts/rpc/graph/**` · `contracts/rpc/impact/**` · `contracts/rpc/context/**` · `contracts/rpc/search/**` · `contracts/rpc/analysis/**`
- **Starts after:** P0-SIGN
- **Goal:** write the params/result schema and one example for every Phase 1 method **before** the code, so engine and desktop agree (R9).

**Rules for every task in this module:** follow `contracts/README.md`. File names: `contracts/rpc/<namespace>/<method>.params.schema.json`, `…/<method>.result.schema.json`, examples `contracts/rpc/<namespace>/examples/<method>.params.1.json` and `…/<method>.result.1.json` (`<method>` is the part after the dot, e.g. `level_view`). Every object has `"additionalProperties": false` and lists all its properties in `required` unless the task marks them optional (`?`). `Node` = `{"$ref":"../../common/node.schema.json"}`, `Edge` = `{"$ref":"../../common/edge.schema.json"}`, `Span` = `{"$ref":"../../common/span.schema.json"}`, enums via `../../common/enums.schema.json#/$defs/<name>`. `project_id` and `node_id` are strings with `minLength: 1`. After each task run `cd contracts && pnpm validate` → `failed=0`.

### MODULE P1-PROMPT — Prompt templates v1
- **Type:** DOCS
- **Lane:** CONTRACTS
- **Owns:** `contracts/prompts/v1/**`
