- **Goal:** the exact text sent to the LLM for explanations and connection tests (R11).

#### P1-PROMPT-001 — Prompt format README
**Files:** `contracts/prompts/v1/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R11
**Why:** every consumer (desktop now, Python AI later) parses templates the same way.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# Prompt templates v1`; sections: `## File format` (first line `SYSTEM:`; system text; a line containing only `---`; a line `USER:`; user text), `## Variables` (`{{name}}` placeholders; every placeholder must be provided; unknown placeholders are an error), `## Citations` (the model must cite nodes as `[[node:<id>]]`; invalid ids are removed by the app), `## Templates` (table: `explain_node.md` — variables kind, name, file_path, project_notes, context_json; `test_connection.md` — no variables).
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " contracts/prompts/v1/README.md` → `4`.

#### P1-PROMPT-002 — explain_node template
**Files:** `contracts/prompts/v1/explain_node.md` (create)
**Refs:** R11
**Why:** the "Explain this" feature.
**Steps:**
1. Create with exactly:
```text
SYSTEM:
You explain source code to a developer who did not write it.
Rules:
- Use plain, simple language. Short sentences. No unexplained jargon.
- Use ONLY the facts in the FACTS section. If something is not in the facts, say "I can't tell from the code shown".
- Whenever you mention a code element whose id appears in the facts, write its name followed by a citation in the form [[node:<id>]]. Copy ids exactly. Never invent an id.
- Do not repeat the source code back.
Answer format (Markdown):
**Summary:** one sentence.
### What it does
3 to 6 bullet points.
### How it connects
Who uses it and what it uses, with citations. Write "No connections found" if there are none.
### Watch out for
1 to 3 bullet points about risks or surprising behaviour, or "Nothing notable".
Keep the whole answer under 250 words.
---
USER:
Explain the {{kind}} named "{{name}}" (file: {{file_path}}).

Notes from the project owner (may be empty): {{project_notes}}

FACTS (JSON built by the analysis engine):
{{context_json}}
```
**Verify:** the file contains exactly one line `---` (`grep -c "^---$" contracts/prompts/v1/explain_node.md` → `1`) and the 5 placeholders.

```text
USER:

```

```ts
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { defineConfig, externalizeDepsPlugin } from 'electron-vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';

export default defineConfig({
  main: {
    plugins: [externalizeDepsPlugin()],
    build: { rollupOptions: { input: { index: resolve(__dirname, 'src/main/index.ts') } } },
  },
  preload: {
    plugins: [externalizeDepsPlugin()],
    build: { rollupOptions: { input: { index: resolve(__dirname, 'src/preload/index.ts') } } },
  },
  renderer: {
    root: resolve(__dirname, 'src/renderer'),
    plugins: [react()],
    build: { rollupOptions: { input: { index: resolve(__dirname, 'src/renderer/index.html') } } },
  },
});
```

### MODULE P1-DENG — Engine process client (main process)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP
- **Owns:** `desktop/src/main/engine/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-DDEPS
- **Goal:** start `pv-engine`, talk JSON-RPC over its stdio, deliver notifications, and restart it if it crashes (REL-01).

#### P1-DENG-001 — Message framing
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/engine/framing.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/engine/framing.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** the same `Content-Length` framing as the engine.
**Steps:**
1. `framing.ts`:
```ts
export function encodeMessage(body: string): Buffer {
  const payload = Buffer.from(body, 'utf8');
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(`Content-Length: ${payload.length}\r\n\r\n`, 'ascii'), payload]);
}

export class FrameDecoder {
  private buffer: Buffer = Buffer.alloc(0);

  push(chunk: Buffer): string[] {
    this.buffer = Buffer.concat([this.buffer, chunk]);
    const messages: string[] = [];
    for (;;) {
      const headerEnd = this.buffer.indexOf('\r\n\r\n');
      if (headerEnd < 0) break;
      const header = this.buffer.subarray(0, headerEnd).toString('ascii');
      const match = /content-length:\s*(\d+)/i.exec(header);
      if (!match) throw new Error('bad message header');
      const length = Number(match[1]);
      const start = headerEnd + 4;
      if (this.buffer.length < start + length) break;
      messages.push(this.buffer.subarray(start, start + length).toString('utf8'));
      this.buffer = this.buffer.subarray(start + length);
    }
    return messages;
  }
}
```
2. Tests: encode then decode round trip; two messages in one chunk → 2 results; one message split across 3 chunks → result only after the last chunk; non-ASCII text (`"é"`) round trips (length counts bytes); a header without Content-Length throws.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/engine/framing.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DENG-002 — JSON-RPC types and errors

**Why:** typed messages and an error class that keeps the engine error code.

Export: `interface RpcRequest { jsonrpc: '2.0'; id: number; method: string; params: unknown }`, `interface RpcResponse { jsonrpc: '2.0'; id: number | string | null; result?: unknown; error?: { code: number; message: string } }`, `interface RpcNotification { jsonrpc: '2.0'; method: string; params: unknown }`, `class RpcError extends Error { constructor(public code: number, message: string) { super(message); this.name = 'RpcError'; } }`, and `function isResponse(msg: unknown): msg is RpcResponse` (object with `id` key and either `result` or `error`) and `function isNotification(msg: unknown): msg is RpcNotification` (object with string `method` and no `id`).
2. Tests for both type guards and that `new RpcError(-32002,'x')` has `code -32002` and `message 'x'`.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/engine/json-rpc.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DENG-003 — Engine client
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-client.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-client.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** send requests, match responses by id, deliver notifications.
**Steps:**
1. Implement:
```ts
export interface EngineTransport {
  write(data: Buffer): void;
  onData(cb: (chunk: Buffer) => void): void;
}
export class EngineClient {
  constructor(transport: EngineTransport, options?: { timeoutMs?: number });   // default timeout 60000 ms
  request<T = unknown>(method: string, params?: unknown, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<T>;
  onNotification(cb: (method: string, params: unknown) => void): () => void;
  failAll(reason: string): void;   // rejects every pending request with Error(reason)
}
```
2. Behaviour: ids start at 1 and increase; `request` writes `encodeMessage(JSON.stringify({jsonrpc:'2.0', id, method, params: params ?? {}}))`; a timer rejects with `Error('engine request timed out: <method>')` and removes the entry; incoming data goes through one `FrameDecoder`; each message is `JSON.parse`d; responses resolve (`result`) or reject (`new RpcError(error.code, error.message)`); notifications call every listener; unknown ids are ignored; invalid JSON is ignored.

Tests with a fake transport (captures writes; has a `feed(obj)` helper that encodes and calls the data callback): request resolves with result; error response rejects with `RpcError` code; notification reaches 2 listeners and unsubscribe works; timeout (use `vi.useFakeTimers()` and `timeoutMs: 100`) rejects; `failAll('engine stopped')` rejects pending.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/engine/engine-client.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DENG-005 — Engine child process
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-process.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-process.test.ts` (create)

**Why:** start the engine executable with piped stdio.

```ts
export interface EngineProcessHandle {
  transport: EngineTransport;
  onExit(cb: (code: number | null) => void): void;
  kill(): void;
}
export type Spawner = (command: string, args: string[]) => EngineProcessHandle;

```

#### P1-DENG-006 — Engine service with auto-restart
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-service.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-service.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9, R10
**Why:** one object the rest of the app uses; it survives engine crashes.
**Steps:**
1. Implement:
```ts
export type EngineStatus = 'stopped' | 'starting' | 'ready' | 'crashed' | 'restarting';
export class EngineService {
  constructor(enginePath: string, spawner: Spawner, now?: () => number);
  get status(): EngineStatus;
  get path(): string;   // the engine executable path given to the constructor
  start(): Promise<void>;
  request<T = unknown>(method: string, params?: unknown): Promise<T>;
  onNotification(cb: (method: string, params: unknown) => void): () => void;
  onStatus(cb: (status: EngineStatus) => void): () => void;
  stop(): Promise<void>;
}
```
2. `start`: status `starting`; `handle = spawner(enginePath, [])`; `client = new EngineClient(handle.transport)`; forward client notifications to this service's listeners; `await client.request('engine.ping')`; status `ready`. On exit while not stopping: `client.failAll('engine stopped')`; status `crashed`; keep the timestamps of the last restarts; if fewer than 3 restarts happened within the last 60 000 ms (use `now()`), set `restarting` and call `start()` again; otherwise stay `crashed`.
3. `request`: if status is not `ready` reject with `Error('engine not running')`; else delegate to the client.
4. `stop`: mark stopping; try `request('engine.shutdown')` (ignore errors); after up to 2000 ms kill the process; status `stopped`.
5. Tests with a fake spawner (returns handles whose transport answers `engine.ping` automatically and whose exit can be triggered): start → `ready`; crash → statuses `crashed`, `restarting`, `ready` in order; 4 crashes within 60 s → final status `crashed`; `request` while stopped rejects; notifications from the engine reach listeners even after a restart.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/engine/engine-service.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DENG-008 — Engine connection over a named pipe (new architecture)
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/engine/pipe-transport.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/engine/pipe-transport.test.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-process.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-service.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/main/engine/engine-service.test.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/main/engine/README.md` (edit)
**Refs:** R9, R10
**Why:** the new architecture connects the UI to the engine over a named pipe / Unix socket, and the same engine serves VS Code on TCP 7700.
**Needs:** P4-EIPC
**Steps:**
1. `pipe-transport.ts`: `pipePath(pid = process.pid): string` → Windows `\\.\pipe\pv-engine-<user>-<pid>`, else `<os.tmpdir()>/pv-engine-<user>-<pid>.sock` (`<user>` = `os.userInfo().username` with non `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` replaced by `_`); `connectPipe(path, timeoutMs = 5000): Promise<net.Socket>` retries every 100 ms until the engine listens.
2. `engine-process.ts`: when setting `engine.transport` is not `'stdio'` (default `'pipe'`), spawn `pv-engine serve --pipe <pipePath()> --tcp 7700 --parent-pid <process.pid>`; the returned process object exposes `input`/`output` streams that are the socket instead of stdin/stdout (stderr stays the log).
3. `engine-service.ts`: if the pipe connection fails or the engine exits within 5 s with `unknown command: serve`, log a warning and restart once with stdio (old behaviour). Restart-on-crash keeps working for both transports. Expose `transport: 'pipe' | 'stdio'` in the status.
4. Tests: `pipePath` on both platforms; fallback to stdio when `connectPipe` rejects (fake process factory).
5. README: "Transports" section.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/engine` → all pass.

1. Create exactly:
```ts
export type Envelope<T> =
  | { ok: true; value: T }
  | { ok: false; error: { code: string | number; message: string } };

export interface PvBridge {
  rpc(method: string, params?: unknown): Promise<Envelope<unknown>>;
  invoke(channel: string, payload?: unknown): Promise<Envelope<unknown>>;
  onNotification(cb: (method: string, params: unknown) => void): () => void;
  on(channel: string, cb: (payload: unknown) => void): () => void;
}

export const CHANNEL_RPC = 'pv:rpc';
export const CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION = 'pv:notification';
export const CHANNEL_ENGINE_STATUS = 'pv:engine.status';
```

```ts
export interface IpcLike {
  invoke(channel: string, ...args: unknown[]): Promise<unknown>;
  on(channel: string, listener: (event: unknown, ...args: unknown[]) => void): void;
  removeListener(channel: string, listener: (event: unknown, ...args: unknown[]) => void): void;
}
export function createBridge(ipc: IpcLike): PvBridge;
```
2. Behaviour: `rpc(method, params)` → `ipc.invoke(CHANNEL_RPC, { method, params })`; `invoke(channel, payload)` → if the channel does not start with `pv:` resolve `{ ok:false, error:{ code:'bad_channel', message:'channel must start with pv:' } }`, else `ipc.invoke(channel, payload)`; `onNotification(cb)` → listener on `CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION` calling `cb(msg.method, msg.params)`, returns a function that removes it; `on(channel, cb)` → throws `Error('channel must start with pv:')` for other channels; else a listener calling `cb(payload)`, returns a remover.

#### P1-DMAIN-005 — Automatic handler loader
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/core/handler-loader.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/core/handler-loader.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R3, R10
**Why:** any `handlers/*.ts` file registers itself; nobody edits a central list.
**Steps:**
1. Implement:
```ts
import type { MainContext } from './context';
export interface HandlerModule { default?: (ctx: MainContext) => void }
const discovered = import.meta.glob<HandlerModule>(['../handlers/*.ts', '!../handlers/*.test.ts'], { eager: true });
export function loadHandlers(ctx: MainContext, modules: Record<string, HandlerModule> = discovered): string[] {
  const paths = Object.keys(modules).sort();
  for (const path of paths) {
    const register = modules[path].default;
    if (typeof register !== 'function') throw new Error(`handler module has no default export: ${path}`);
    register(ctx);
  }
  return paths;
}
```
2. Tests: pass a fake modules map with 2 modules → both called in sorted order, returned paths sorted; a module without default → throws.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/core/handler-loader.test.ts` → all pass.

**Steps:**
1. Export `openInEditor(file: string, line: number, deps: { spawnCode: (args: string[]) => Promise<boolean>; openPath: (p: string) => Promise<string> }): Promise<'vscode' | 'default'>`: try `spawnCode(['-g', `${file}:${line}`])`; if it resolves true return `'vscode'`; otherwise `await openPath(file)` and return `'default'`.
2. Real deps: `spawnCode` spawns `code` (on Windows `code.cmd`) with `shell: false`, resolves true on exit code 0, false on error/non-zero; `openPath` = `shell.openPath`.
3. Default export registers `pv:editor.open` `{file_path, line}` (absolute path; line ≥ 1) → `{ opened_with }`.
4. Tests for `openInEditor` with fake deps: VS Code available → `'vscode'`; not available → `'default'` and `openPath` called.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/handlers/editor.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DMAIN-010 — Application entry
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/index.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** wire everything together at startup.
**Steps:**
1. Implement:
   1. `if (!app.requestSingleInstanceLock()) { app.quit(); }` and on `second-instance` focus the window.
   2. `app.whenReady().then(...)`: `userData = app.getPath('userData')`; `log = createLogger(join(userData,'logs','main.log'))`; `settings = new SettingsStore(join(userData,'settings.json'))`; `secrets = new SecretStore(join(userData,'secrets.json'), { isAvailable: () => safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable(), encrypt: (s) => safeStorage.encryptString(s), decrypt: (b) => safeStorage.decryptString(b) })`.
   3. `enginePath = locateEngine({ env: process.env, isPackaged: app.isPackaged, resourcesPath: process.resourcesPath, appPath: app.getAppPath(), platform: process.platform, exists: existsSync })`; `engine = new EngineService(enginePath ?? '', spawnEngine)`.
   4. `let win: BrowserWindow | null = null`; `ctx = createMainContext({ ipc: ipcMain, engine, settings, secrets, log, getWindow: () => win })`; `loadHandlers(ctx)`.
   5. `engine.onNotification((method, params) => ctx.send(CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION, { method, params }))`; `engine.onStatus((status) => ctx.send(CHANNEL_ENGINE_STATUS, { status }))`.
   6. `win = createMainWindow()`.
   7. If `enginePath` → `engine.start().catch((e) => log('error','engine start failed', String(e)))`; else `log('error','pv-engine not found; build the engine first')`.
   8. `app.on('activate', ...)` recreates the window on macOS.
   9. `app.on('window-all-closed', () => { if (process.platform !== 'darwin') app.quit(); })`; `app.on('before-quit', () => { void engine.stop(); })` (keep `engine` in a module-level variable for this).
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json` → no errors.

#### P1-DSHELL-002 — Feature registry
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/registry.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/registry.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** the single extension mechanism of the UI.
**Steps:**
1. Export these types exactly:
```ts
import type { ComponentType } from 'react';
export interface NodeRef {
  id: string; kind: string; name: string; qualified_name: string; file_path: string;
  span: { start_line: number; start_col: number; end_line: number; end_col: number };
}
export type PanelArea = 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | 'bottom';
export interface PanelDef { id: string; title: string; area: PanelArea; order: number; component: ComponentType }
export interface CommandDef { id: string; title: string; shortcut?: string; run: () => void | Promise<void> }
export interface NodeActionDef { id: string; title: string; order: number; when?: (node: NodeRef) => boolean; run: (node: NodeRef) => void | Promise<void> }
export interface SettingsSectionDef { id: string; title: string; order: number; component: ComponentType }
export interface StatusItemDef { id: string; order: number; component: ComponentType }
export interface ScreenDef { id: string; component: ComponentType }
export interface ToolbarItemDef { id: string; order: number; side: 'left' | 'right'; component: ComponentType }
export interface WelcomeActionDef { id: string; title: string; description: string; order: number; run: () => void | Promise<void> }
export interface GlobalDef { id: string; component: ComponentType }
export interface AppRegistry {
  addPanel(def: PanelDef): void; addCommand(def: CommandDef): void; addNodeAction(def: NodeActionDef): void;
  addSettingsSection(def: SettingsSectionDef): void; addStatusItem(def: StatusItemDef): void; addScreen(def: ScreenDef): void;
  addToolbarItem(def: ToolbarItemDef): void; addWelcomeAction(def: WelcomeActionDef): void; addGlobal(def: GlobalDef): void;
}
export interface RegistryReader {
  panels(area: PanelArea): PanelDef[]; commands(): CommandDef[]; nodeActions(node: NodeRef): NodeActionDef[];
  settingsSections(): SettingsSectionDef[]; statusItems(): StatusItemDef[]; screen(id: string): ScreenDef | undefined;
  toolbarItems(side: 'left' | 'right'): ToolbarItemDef[]; welcomeActions(): WelcomeActionDef[]; globals(): GlobalDef[];
}
export function createRegistry(): AppRegistry & RegistryReader;
export const appRegistry: AppRegistry & RegistryReader;
```
2. Rules: adding a second item with the same `id` in the same category throws `Error('duplicate <category> id: <id>')`. Lists are sorted by `order`, then `id` (items without `order` sort by `id`). `nodeActions(node)` returns only actions whose `when` is missing or returns true.
3. Tests: sorting, duplicate error, `when` filtering, `screen('x')` undefined.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/core/registry.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DSHELL-014 — Workspaces (dashboards) in the registry and store
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/registry.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/registry.test.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/store.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/store.test.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/workspaces.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/core/workspaces.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** one screen with every panel is too much for a newcomer; a dashboard shows only what one job needs (founder request, 2026-09-26).
**Steps:**
1. `WorkspaceDef { id; title; icon; description; order; panels?: Partial<Record<PanelArea, string[]>>; start?: Partial<Record<PanelArea, string>> }` — an area missing from `panels` shows all its panels; an empty list hides the area. `addWorkspace` / `workspaces()` on the registry.
2. Store: `workspace: string` (default `'explore'`, remembered in `localStorage` key `pv.layout.workspace`), `setWorkspace(id)` (also applies `start` to `activePanel`).

### MODULE P1-DAI — AI service in the main process (direct mode)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP

- **Starts after:** P1-DMAIN · P1-PROMPT
- **Goal:** call an LLM with the user's own key (Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as local Ollama) using engine-built context, and return a grounded explanation with validated citations (R11).

#### P1-DAI-001 — Types and prompt templates
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/ai/types.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/ai/prompt.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/ai/prompt.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R11
**Why:** one request/response shape for all providers; one template parser.
**Steps:**
1. `types.ts`:
```ts
export interface AiMessage { role: 'user' | 'assistant'; content: string }
export interface AiRequest { system: string; messages: AiMessage[]; maxTokens: number; temperature?: number }
export interface AiResponse { text: string; model: string; inputTokens?: number; outputTokens?: number }
export interface AiProvider { id: string; complete(req: AiRequest): Promise<AiResponse> }
export interface ProviderConfig { model: string; baseUrl: string; apiKey: string }
export interface AiProviderFactory {
  id: string; label: string; needsApiKey: boolean; defaultModel: string; defaultBaseUrl: string;
  create(config: ProviderConfig, fetchImpl?: typeof fetch): AiProvider;
}
export class AiError extends Error {
  constructor(public code: 'no_api_key' | 'auth' | 'rate_limit' | 'network' | 'provider_error' | 'bad_template', message: string) {
    super(message); this.name = 'AiError';
  }
}
```
2. `prompt.ts`: `parseTemplate(text: string): { system: string; user: string }` — split at the first line that is exactly `---` (handle `\r\n`); remove a first line `SYSTEM:` from the first part and `USER:` from the second; trim both; missing separator → `AiError('bad_template', …)`. `renderTemplate(text: string, vars: Record<string, string>): string` — replace every `{{name}}`; a placeholder without a value → `AiError('bad_template', 'missing variable: name')`.
3. Tests: parse the exact P1-PROMPT-003 text; render replaces 2 variables; missing variable throws.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/ai/prompt.test.ts` → all pass.

2. Tests: valid + invalid mix; ids containing `#`, `/`, `.` and `:` (e.g. `method:app/a.py#C.m`) are extracted whole; duplicates appear once in `cited`.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/ai/citations.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DAI-004 — Anthropic provider
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/ai-providers/anthropic/index.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/ai-providers/anthropic/index.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R11, R5
**Why:** default provider.
**Steps:**
1. Export `provider: AiProviderFactory` with `id 'anthropic'`, `label 'Anthropic (Claude)'`, `needsApiKey true`, `defaultModel 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'`, `defaultBaseUrl 'https://api.anthropic.com'`.
2. `create(config, fetchImpl = fetch)` returns a provider whose `complete(req)`:
   - `POST ${config.baseUrl}/v1/messages` with headers `content-type: application/json`, `x-api-key: <key>`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`; body `{ model, max_tokens: req.maxTokens, system: req.system, messages: req.messages, temperature: req.temperature ?? 0.2 }`.
   - Network failure (fetch throws) → `AiError('network', 'Could not reach the AI provider')`.
   - HTTP 401/403 → `AiError('auth','The API key was rejected')`; 429 → `AiError('rate_limit','Too many requests; try again shortly')`; other non-2xx → `AiError('provider_error', 'AI provider error <status>')`.
   - Success: `text` = concatenation of `content[].text` for items with `type === 'text'`; `model` = `data.model`; tokens from `data.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`.
3. Tests with a fake `fetchImpl`: request URL, headers and body; success parsing; 401 → `auth`; thrown fetch → `network`.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/ai-providers/anthropic/index.test.ts` → all pass.

Same error mapping as Anthropic. Success: `text = data.choices[0].message.content`, `model = data.model`, tokens from `usage.prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`. Empty model → `AiError('provider_error','Set a model name in Settings → AI')` before calling.

**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/ai-providers/openai/index.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DAI-007 — AI service: explain a node
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/ai/ai-service.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/ai/ai-service.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9, R11
**Why:** the full "Explain this" pipeline.
**Steps:**
1. Implement:
```ts
import explainTemplate from '../../../../contracts/prompts/v1/explain_node.md?raw';
import testTemplate from '../../../../contracts/prompts/v1/test_connection.md?raw';
export interface ExplainResult { node_id: string; markdown: string; cited_nodes: { id: string; name: string }[]; model: string }
export class AiService {
  constructor(deps: {
    engine: { request<T>(method: string, params?: unknown): Promise<T> };
    settings: { get<T>(k: string, f: T): T };
    secrets: { get(n: string): string | null };
    providers?: AiProviderFactory[];   // default listProviders()
    fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
  });
  explainNode(projectId: string, nodeId: string): Promise<ExplainResult>;
  testConnection(): Promise<{ ok: true; model: string; latency_ms: number }>;
}
```
2. `explainNode`: `pack = await engine.request('context.for_node', {project_id, node_id, max_chars: 12000})`; `status = await engine.request('project.status', {project_id})`; `notes = settings.get('project.notes.' + status.root_path, '')`; build `valid` map (id → name) from `pack.node`, `pack.parent` (if not null), `children`, `callers`, `callees`, `imports`; `vars = { kind: pack.node.kind, name: pack.node.name, file_path: pack.node.file_path || '(no file)', project_notes: notes || '(none)', context_json: JSON.stringify(pack, null, 1) }`; `{factory, config} = readAiConfig(...)`; `resp = await factory.create(config, fetchImpl).complete({ system: renderTemplate(t.system, vars), messages: [{ role:'user', content: renderTemplate(t.user, vars) }], maxTokens: 900 })`; `{text, cited} = cleanCitations(resp.text, valid)`; return `{ node_id, markdown: text, cited_nodes: cited, model: resp.model }`.
3. `testConnection`: render `test_connection.md`, `maxTokens: 5`, measure time with `Date.now()`; return `{ ok: true, model, latency_ms }` (errors propagate).
4. **Backend extension point (used from Phase 4):** at module level `const backends = import.meta.glob<{ backend?: { id: string; explainNode(input: { pack: unknown; notes: string; valid: Map<string, string> }): Promise<{ markdown: string; cited_nodes: { id: string; name: string }[]; model: string }> } }>(['../ai-backends/*/index.ts'], { eager: true });`. In `explainNode`, after building `pack`, `notes` and `valid`: `mode = settings.get('ai.mode', 'direct')`; if `mode !== 'direct'` and a discovered backend has `id === mode`, return `{ node_id, ...(await backend.explainNode({ pack, notes, valid })) }` instead of calling the provider. (No backend exists in Phase 1, so direct mode is always used.)
5. Tests with fake engine (returns a small pack + status), fake settings/secrets and a fake provider factory: explanation text with one valid and one invalid citation → invalid removed, `cited_nodes` has the valid one; the rendered user message contains the node name and `context_json`; missing key → `AiError` `no_api_key`; with setting `ai.mode = 'cloud'` and no backends, direct mode is still used.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/ai/ai-service.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-DVIEW-001 — View model
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/model.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/model.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R10
**Why:** one visual description shared by 2D and 3D.
**Steps:**
1. Export:
```ts
export interface ViewNode {
  id: string; label: string; kind: string; level: number; color: string; borderColor: string;
  size: number; shape: string; badge: string; pulse: boolean; opacity: number; hasChildren: boolean; data: GraphNode;
}
export interface ViewEdge { id: string; source: string; target: string; kind: string; weight: number; color: string; width: number; animated: boolean; opacity: number }
export interface ViewGraph { parentId: string; nodes: ViewNode[]; edges: ViewEdge[] }
export function kindColor(kind: string): string;
export function kindShape(kind: string): string;
export function nodeSize(loc: number): number;
export function edgeColor(kind: string): string;
export function edgeWidth(weight: number): number;
export function buildViewGraph(view: LevelView, overlays: Record<string, Overlay>): ViewGraph;
```
2. Values: colors — project `#8b5cf6`, package `#3b82f6`, module `#06b6d4`, class `#f59e0b`, function `#10b981`, method `#34d399`, variable `#a3a3a3`, statement `#737373`, external `#94a3b8`, anything else `#9ca3af`. Shapes — project/package `round-rectangle`, module `rectangle`, class `diamond`, external `hexagon`, others `ellipse`. `nodeSize(loc) = 30 + Math.min(50, Math.round(10 * Math.log10(Math.max(1, loc))))`. Edge colors — imports `#64748b`, calls `#22c55e`, inherits `#f97316`, references `#a855f7`. `edgeWidth(w) = 1 + Math.min(6, Math.log2(Math.max(1, w)))`. `hasChildren` = kind is one of project, package, module, class, function, method.
3. `buildViewGraph`: `merged = mergeOverlays(overlays)`; each node gets base values (`borderColor = color`, `badge ''`, `pulse false`, `opacity 1`) then the fields of `merged.nodes[id]` override; if `merged.dimOthers` and the node has no overlay style, `opacity = 0.25`. Same for edges with `merged.edges`. `label = node.name`.
4. Tests: sizes (loc 1 → 30, 100 → 50, 10^9 → 80); overlay color wins; dimOthers dims unstyled nodes only.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/view/model.test.ts` → all pass.

**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/renderer-types.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/renderers.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/renderers.test.ts` (create)

```ts
  updateStyles(graph: ViewGraph): void;   // same ids; update visual fields only; no layout

}
export interface RendererEntry { mode: '2d' | '3d'; create: () => GraphRenderer }
```
2. `renderers.ts`: `const discovered = import.meta.glob<{ renderer?: RendererEntry }>('../renderers/*/index.ts', { eager: true })`; `listRenderers(modules = discovered): RendererEntry[]`; `getRenderer(mode, modules = discovered)`.

#### P1-DVIEW-003 — Level view loader hook
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/use-level-view.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/use-level-view.test.tsx` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** fetch the current level whenever project, parent or graph version change.
**Steps:**
1. `useLevelView(): { view: LevelView | null; loading: boolean; error: string | null; reload(): void }` — reads `projectId`, `currentParentId`, `graphVersion` from `useAppStore`; when `projectId` is null returns `view null`. #### P1-DVIEW-008 — Renderer choice and engine layouts (new architecture)
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/renderer-types.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/renderers.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/renderers.test.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/model.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/use-level-view.ts` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/use-level-view.test.tsx` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/view/Canvas.tsx` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/canvas/GraphViewSettings.tsx` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/canvas/register.tsx` (edit) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/canvas/register.test.tsx` (edit)
**Refs:** R9, R10
**Why:** the new architecture draws 2D with React Flow + D3 and 3D with React Three Fiber, laid out by the engine; the classic renderers stay selectable.
**Steps:**
1. `RendererEntry` gets optional `id?: string` (default: folder name), `label?: string`, `preferred?: boolean`, `layout?: 'renderer' | 'engine'` (default `'renderer'`). `ViewGraph` gets optional `positions?: Record<string, { x: number; y: number; z?: number }>` and `edgePoints?: Record<string, { x: number; y: number }[]>`.
2. `renderers.ts`: `listRenderers(mode?)` returns entries with their ids; `getRenderer(mode, modules?, choice?)` → the entry whose id equals `choice`, else the first `preferred`, else the first.
3. `use-level-view.ts`: when the active renderer has `layout: 'engine'`, call `rpc('layout.compute', {project_id, parent_id, mode})` after the level view and put the result into `positions` / `edgePoints`; on error keep going without positions (the renderer then uses its own fallback layout).
4. `Canvas.tsx`: read settings `view.renderer2d` / `view.renderer3d` (via `invoke('pv:settings.get', …)`) and re-create the renderer when they change.
5. `GraphViewSettings.tsx` + `register.tsx`: settings section "Graph view" (order 15) with one select per mode listing `label ?? id`.
6. Tests: choice / preferred / first order; the hook calls `layout.compute` only for engine-layout renderers; the settings section is registered.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/view src/renderer/src/features/canvas` → all pass.

### MODULE P1-D2D — 2D renderer (Cytoscape)

- **Lane:** DESKTOP

#### P1-D2D-001 — Element conversion
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-elements.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-elements.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** a pure, testable mapping from ViewGraph to Cytoscape elements.
**Steps:**
1. `toElements(g: ViewGraph): ElementDefinition[]` (type from `cytoscape`): nodes first with `data: { id, label, displayLabel: badge ? `${label} [${badge}]` : label, color, borderColor, size, shape, opacity, kind }` and `classes: pulse ? 'pulse' : ''`; then edges with `data: { id, source, target, color, width, opacity, kind }` and `classes: animated ? 'animated' : ''`. Skip edges whose source or target is not among the nodes.
2. Tests: counts, displayLabel with a badge, dangling edge skipped.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-elements.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-D2D-002 — Stylesheet
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-style.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-style.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** visual rules driven by element data.
**Steps:**
1. `buildStylesheet(): StylesheetStyle[]` (use the `cytoscape` stylesheet type available in the installed typings; if the name differs, use `any[]` is NOT allowed — use `cytoscape.StylesheetJson` or the type the typings export and note it) with selectors:
   - `node`: `background-color: data(color)`, `border-color: data(borderColor)`, `border-width: 2`, `width: data(size)`, `height: data(size)`, `shape: data(shape)`, `label: data(displayLabel)`, `color: #e5e7eb`, `font-size: 11`, `text-valign: bottom`, `text-margin-y: 4`, `opacity: data(opacity)`, `text-outline-color: #0f1320`, `text-outline-width: 2`.
   - `node:selected`: `border-width: 4`, `border-color: #fbbf24`.
   - `node.pulse`: `border-width: 5`, `border-style: double`.
   - `edge`: `curve-style: bezier`, `target-arrow-shape: triangle`, `line-color: data(color)`, `target-arrow-color: data(color)`, `width: data(width)`, `opacity: data(opacity)`, `arrow-scale: 0.8`.
   - `edge.animated`: `line-style: dashed`, `line-dash-pattern: [6, 4]`.
2. Test: the returned array has these 5 selectors in this order.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-style.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P1-D2D-003 — Cytoscape renderer
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-renderer.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-renderer.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** the 2D implementation of `GraphRenderer`.
**Steps:**
1. `class CyRenderer implements GraphRenderer` with constructor `(options: { headless?: boolean } = {})`. At module level register dagre once: `cytoscape.use(dagre)` guarded by a module-level boolean.
2. `mount(container)`: `this.cy = cytoscape({ container: options.headless ? undefined : container, headless: options.headless, style: buildStylesheet(), elements: [], wheelSensitivity: 0.2, minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 3 })`; attach events: `tap` on `node` → `nodeClick`; `dbltap` on `node` → `nodeDoubleClick`; `cxttap` on `node` → `nodeContext`; `mouseover` on `node` → `nodeHover` with id; `mouseout` on `node` → `nodeHover` with null; `tap` where `evt.target === cy` → `backgroundClick`. Payload x/y = `evt.renderedPosition` plus the container's `getBoundingClientRect()` left/top (0 in headless).
3. `setGraph(g)`: `cy.elements().remove(); cy.add(toElements(g));` then layout: nodes ≤ 300 → `{ name: 'dagre', rankDir: 'LR', nodeSep: 30, rankSep: 80, animate: false }`; ≤ 1000 → `{ name: 'cose', animate: false }`; else `{ name: 'grid' }`; run it, then `fit(undefined, 40)`.
4. `updateStyles(g)`: inside `cy.batch`, for each view node/edge that exists, update its data fields and set its classes as in `toElements` (no layout).
5. `select(id)`: unselect all; select that node if it exists. `fit()`: `cy.fit(undefined, 40)`. `on(event, cb)`: store listeners; return remover. `destroy()`: `cy.destroy()`; clear listeners.
6. Animated edges: while any edge has class `animated`, run a `requestAnimationFrame` loop increasing `line-dash-offset` by 1 each frame on `.animated` edges; stop when none (and on `destroy`).
7. Tests (headless): `setGraph` with 3 nodes, 2 edges → `cy.nodes().length === 3`; `updateStyles` changes `data('color')` without changing positions; `select` marks the node selected; listeners receive `nodeClick` when you call `cy.$id('a').emit('tap')`.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/cy-renderer.test.ts` → all pass.

**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/index.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/index.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** makes the 2D renderer discoverable.
**Steps:**
1. `export const renderer: RendererEntry = { mode: '2d', create: () => new CyRenderer() };`
2. Test: `getRenderer('2d')` from `../../view/renderers` returns an entry with mode `2d`.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/renderers/cy2d/index.test.ts` → pass.

### MODULE P1-DIMPACT — "What breaks if I change this?" UI
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP
- **Owns:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/impact/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-DVIEW
- **Goal:** run impact analysis on a node, color the affected parts at every level, and list them with a risk level (US-06).

#### P1-DIMPACT-001 — Impact overlay builder
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/impact/impact-overlay.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/impact/impact-overlay.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** convert the engine result into an overlay that works at any zoom level.
**Steps:**
1. `buildImpactOverlay(result: ImpactResult, rootAncestors: string[]): Overlay` with `priority 50`, `dimOthers true`:
   - For every id in `rootAncestors` except `project:` → `{ borderColor: '#fbbf24' }`; for the root itself add `badge: 'changed'`.
   - For each affected node A: color = distance 1 `#ef4444`, 2 `#f97316`, ≥3 `#eab308`. For every id in `A.ancestor_ids` except `project:`: if the id has no color yet or its stored distance is larger, set `{ color }` (keep the smallest distance). For A itself also set `badge: 'd' + distance`.
   - No edge styles.
2. Tests: nested ancestors get the smallest-distance color; the root has the badge; `project:` never styled.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/features/impact/impact-overlay.test.ts` → all pass.

**Refs:** R10
**Why:** run, keep and clear the current impact analysis.
**Steps:**
1. Zustand store `useImpactStore` with `rootNode: NodeRef | null`, `result: ImpactResult | null`, `loading`, `error`; actions `run(node: NodeRef)` (`result = await analyzeImpact(pid, node.id)`; `ancestors = await getAncestors(pid, node.id)`; `setOverlay('impact', buildImpactOverlay(result, ancestors.map(n => n.id)))`; `showPanel('bottom','impact')`) and `clear()` (`setOverlay('impact', null)`, reset). Errors → `notify.error('Impact analysis failed', message)`.
2. Tests with mocks: run sets overlay and result; clear removes overlay.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/features/impact/impact-store.test.ts` → all pass.

### MODULE P1-MVP — 🏁 MVP CHECKPOINT
- **Type:** DOCS
- **Lane:** DOCS
- **Owns:** `docs/signoff/mvp-checkpoint.md` · `docs/signoff/mvp-demo.md`
- **Starts after:** P1-EAPP · P1-GAPI · P1-IMPACT · P1-CTX · P1-D2D · P1-DNAV · P1-DINSP · P1-DIMPACT · P1-DEXPL · P1-DSET · P1-DIMPORT · P1-DAI
- **Goal:** prove the MVP works end-to-end on real projects, measure it, and decide to continue. **At this point the MVP exists:** Python only, open a folder, clickable 2D map, drill down/up, inspector with code, Explain, What breaks?, all local.

#### P1-MVP-001 — MVP checklist and demo script
**Files:** `docs/signoff/mvp-checkpoint.md` (create)
**Refs:** R1
**Why:** a repeatable way to check the MVP.
**Steps:**
1. Title `# MVP checkpoint`; sections:
   - `## Build`: commands — engine: `cd engine && cmake --preset dev && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev`; desktop: `cd desktop && pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm dev`.
   - `## Demo script` (numbered): 1. Start the app. 2. Settings → AI → add a key (or Ollama URL + model) → Test connection. 3. Open folder `engine/modules/lang_python/tests/fixtures/pyproj_small`. 4. See 4 nodes at the top level. 5. Double-click `app` → 5 nodes. 6. Select `services.py` → inspector shows code. 7. Right-click `UserService` (inside `services.py`) → Explain this → explanation with clickable references. 8. Right-click `is_valid` (inside `utils.py`) → What breaks? → 3 affected, risk shown, map highlighted. 9. Breadcrumb back to the project. 10. Repeat steps 3–8 on a real open-source Python project (e.g. clone `https://github.com/pallets/flask`).
   - `## Acceptance` table US-01 … US-06 with columns Criterion (from `docs/requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`) · Result (pass/fail) · Notes.
   - `## Measurements` table: PERF-01, PERF-02, PERF-03, PERF-04, PERF-06 with Target · Measured.
   - `## Decision` with checkboxes: `- [ ] Continue Phase 1 post-MVP` · `- [ ] Fix blockers first (list them)`.
**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " docs/signoff/mvp-checkpoint.md` → `5`.

#### P1-MVP-002 — Run the checkpoint (human task)
**Files:** `docs/signoff/mvp-checkpoint.md` (edit)
**Refs:** R1
**Why:** real evidence that the MVP works.
**Steps:**
1. Follow the demo script on both projects. Fill Acceptance and Measurements tables honestly.
2. Every failure becomes a bug note (R2.6) and a fix task in the owning module.
3. Tick a decision checkbox; both founders sign under it with the date.
**Verify:** all 6 acceptance rows are filled; a decision is ticked.

#### P1-MVP-003 — Record a 60–90 second demo video (human task)
**Files:** `docs/signoff/mvp-demo.md` (create)
**Refs:** R1
**Why:** for early users, the landing page and later the YC application.
**Steps:**

2. Upload (unlisted YouTube or Loom). Create `mvp-demo.md` with the link, the date, and 3 bullet points of what it shows.
**Verify:** the link opens the video.

## Phase 1 — after the MVP checkpoint

### MODULE P1-SRCH — Search engine module
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/search/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-MVP
- **Goal:** `search.query` and `search.suggest` (US-07).

#### P1-SRCH-001 — Match scoring
**Files:** `engine/modules/search/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/search/include/pv/search/search.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/search/src/search.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/search/tests/score_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** rank how well a node name matches the typed text.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME search DEPS pv_session TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `search.hpp` (namespace `pv::search`):
```cpp
struct SearchHit { std::string node_id, name, kind, file_path, qualified_name; int score = 0; int level = 0; };
int score_match(const std::string& text, const core::Node& node);
std::vector<SearchHit> search_nodes(const graph::Graph& g, const std::string& text,
                                    const std::vector<core::NodeKind>& kinds, int limit);
std::vector<std::string> suggest_names(const graph::Graph& g, const std::string& prefix, int limit);
```
3. `score_match` (all comparisons case-insensitive with `core::to_lower`): name equals text → 100; name starts with text → 80; name contains text → 60; qualified_name contains text → 40; `core::is_subsequence_ci(text, name)` → 20; else 0. `search_nodes` and `suggest_names` get temporary bodies that throw `Unsupported`.
4. Tests suite `SearchScore`: each rule with a hand-made node (`name "UserService"`: `"userservice"` → 100, `"user"` → 80, `"serv"` → 60, `"usv"` → 20, `"zzz"` → 0; qualified-name rule with name `"x"` and qualified name `"app.models.x"`, text `"models"` → 40).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R SearchScore` → all pass.

#### P1-SRCH-002 — search_nodes
**Files:** `engine/modules/search/src/search.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/search/tests/search_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** the ordered result list.
**Steps:**
1. Implement: iterate `g.all_nodes()`, skip the Project node, skip kinds not in `kinds` (when not empty), compute `score_match`, keep score > 0; sort by score desc, then level asc, then name asc, then id asc; cut to `limit`.
2. Tests suite `SearchNodes` (TestEnv + fixture): text `"user"` → results[0] `class:app/models.py#User` (100), [1] `class:app/services.py#UserService` (80), [2] `method:app/services.py#UserService.get_user` (60), [3] `function:app/api/routes.py#get_user_route` (60); with kinds `{Function}` → first is `get_user_route`; limit 1 → 1 result.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R SearchNodes` → all pass.

#### P1-SRCH-003 — Name suggestions
**Files:** `engine/modules/search/src/search.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/search/tests/suggest_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** contextual suggestions while typing.
**Steps:**
1. `suggest_names`: unique names (not project) that start with `prefix` case-insensitively; sort by length asc then alphabetically; cut to `limit`.
2. Tests suite `SearchSuggest` (fixture): prefix `"get"` → `{"get_user","get_user_route"}`; prefix `"no"` → `{"normalize"}`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R SearchSuggest` → all pass.

#### P1-SRCH-004 — Search RPC methods
**Files:** `engine/modules/search/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/search/tests/search_rpc_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** expose search to the desktop app.
**Steps:**
1. `pv_register_search` adds `search.query` (`text` required; `kinds` via `optional_string_list` + `node_kind_from_string`, unknown → `InvalidParams`; `limit = clamp_int(optional_int(p,"limit",50),1,200)`) → `{"results":[{"node_id","name","kind","file_path","qualified_name","score"}]}` and `search.suggest` (`prefix` required; `limit = clamp_int(optional_int(p,"limit",10),1,50)`) → `{"suggestions":[…]}`.

#### P1-ANLYS-002 — Hotspots
**Files:** `engine/modules/analysis/src/hotspots.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/analysis/tests/hotspots_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** find the risky parts of the code.
**Steps:**
1. Candidates: Function, Method and Module nodes. For each metric m in (complexity, fan_in, fan_out, loc): `max_m` over candidates; normalized `v/max_m` (0 when `max_m` is 0). `score = round(100 * (0.30*c + 0.25*fi + 0.25*fo + 0.20*l))`.
2. Reasons: for each metric, `p75` = value at index `floor(0.75 * (n - 1))` of the sorted (ascending) values; if the node's value ≥ p75 and > 0 add: `"High complexity (<v>)"`, `"Many callers (<v>)"`, `"Many dependencies (<v>)"`, `"Large (<v> lines)"`.
3. Output `{"hotspots":[{"node_id","kind","name","file_path","score","reasons","metrics"}]}` sorted by score desc then id, cut to `limit`.
4. Tests suite `AnalysisHotspots` (fixture): result length ≤ limit; scores sorted desc and within 0–100; the candidate with the highest complexity has a reason starting with `"High complexity"`; `limit 1` → 1 item.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R AnalysisHotspots` → all pass.

#### P1-ANLYS-003 — Entry points
**Files:** `engine/modules/analysis/src/entry_points.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/analysis/tests/entry_points_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** where execution starts.
**Steps:**
1. Reasons: a module whose `file_path` is in `main_guard_files` → `"has __main__ guard"`; a module whose file name is one of `__main__.py main.py app.py manage.py wsgi.py asgi.py run.py cli.py` → `"conventional entry file name"`; a Function whose parent is a Module and whose name is `main` → `"function named main"`. Merge reasons per node (in that order); output sorted by node_id: `{"entry_points":[{"node_id","reasons"}]}`.
2. Tests suite `AnalysisEntryPoints` (fixture): exactly `function:main.py#main` (`["function named main"]`) and `module:main.py` (`["has __main__ guard","conventional entry file name"]`).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R AnalysisEntryPoints` → all pass.

#### P1-ANLYS-004 — Architectural boundaries
**Files:** `engine/modules/analysis/src/boundaries.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/analysis/tests/boundaries_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** show coupling between packages.
**Steps:**
1. For each Package node P (sorted by id): let `inside(x)` = `g.is_descendant(x, P.id)`. Over all edges (count edges, not weights): `internal` = both ends inside; `outgoing` = source inside, target outside; `incoming` = source outside, target inside. `instability = outgoing / (incoming + outgoing)` or `0.0` when both are 0. Output `{"packages":[{"node_id","name","internal_edges","outgoing_edges","incoming_edges","instability"}]}`.
2. Tests suite `AnalysisBoundaries` (fixture): `package:app` → internal 14, outgoing 0, incoming 2, instability 0.0; `package:app/api` → internal 0, outgoing 4, incoming 0, instability 1.0.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R AnalysisBoundaries` → all pass.

### MODULE P1-D3D — 3D renderer and view mode
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP
- **Owns:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/**` · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/viewmode/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-MVP
- **Goal:** the same level view in 3D, switchable at any time (US-10, 2D/3D twinning).

#### P1-D3D-001 — Graph data conversion
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/fg-data.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/fg-data.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** pure mapping from ViewGraph to 3d-force-graph data.
**Steps:**
1. `toGraphData(g: ViewGraph): { nodes: FgNode[]; links: FgLink[] }` with `FgNode = { id, name, color, val, opacity, badge }` (`val = size / 10`) and `FgLink = { id, source, target, color, width, animated }`; dangling links skipped.
2. Tests: counts, `val`, dangling skipped.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/fg-data.test.ts` → pass.

#### P1-D3D-002 — 3D renderer
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/fg-renderer.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** the 3D implementation of `GraphRenderer`.
**Steps:**
1. `class Fg3dRenderer implements GraphRenderer`. `mount(container)`: create the graph with `ForceGraph3D()(container)` from `3d-force-graph` (if the installed version's README says to use `new ForceGraph3D(container)`, use that), set `backgroundColor('#0f1320')`, `nodeLabel((n) => n.name + (n.badge ? ' [' + n.badge + ']' : ''))`, `nodeColor((n) => n.color)`, `nodeVal((n) => n.val)`, `nodeOpacity(0.9)`, `linkColor((l) => l.color)`, `linkWidth((l) => l.width)`, `linkDirectionalArrowLength(3)`, `linkDirectionalParticles((l) => (l.animated ? 4 : 0))`.
2. Events: `onNodeClick(node, event)` → `nodeClick`; a second click on the same node within 300 ms → `nodeDoubleClick`; `onNodeRightClick` → `nodeContext`; `onNodeHover(node)` → `nodeHover` (id or null); `onBackgroundClick` → `backgroundClick`. x/y = `event.clientX/clientY`.
3. `setGraph(g)` → `graphData(toGraphData(g))`; `updateStyles(g)` → copy the style fields onto the existing node/link objects by id, then re-apply `nodeColor`/`linkColor` accessors to refresh; `select(id)` → selected node color `#fbbf24` (restore the previous color on change); `fit()` → `zoomToFit(400)`; `destroy()` → `_destructor()` if present, then empty the container.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json` → no errors. (WebGL cannot run in unit tests; the manual check is in P1-D3D-004.)

#### P1-D3D-003 — 3D renderer entry
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/index.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/index.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** make it discoverable.
**Steps:**
1. `export const renderer: RendererEntry = { mode: '3d', create: () => new Fg3dRenderer() };` — import `Fg3dRenderer` lazily inside `create` is not needed; a normal import is fine because WebGL is only touched in `mount`.
2. Test: `getRenderer('3d')` returns mode `3d` (do not call `mount`).
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/renderers/fg3d/index.test.ts` → pass.

#### P1-D3D-004 — View mode toggle
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/viewmode/ViewModeToggle.tsx` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/viewmode/register.tsx` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/viewmode/viewmode.test.tsx` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** switch 2D ↔ 3D.
**Steps:**
1. `ViewModeToggle`: two-button segmented control "2D" / "3D" (`aria-pressed`), calls `setViewMode`.
2. `register(app)`: `addToolbarItem({ id: 'view-mode', order: 50, side: 'right', component: ViewModeToggle })`; `addCommand({ id: 'view.toggle3d', title: 'Toggle 2D / 3D', shortcut: 'Ctrl+Shift+3', run: toggle })`.
3. Test: clicking 3D sets `viewMode '3d'`.
4. Manual check: `pnpm dev`, open the fixture, toggle 3D → nodes appear in 3D; double-click drills down; toggle back keeps the level.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/features/viewmode/viewmode.test.tsx` → pass; manual check done.

- **Type:** CODE

#### P1-REL-001 — App icon (human task)
**Files:** `desktop/build/icon.png` (create) · `desktop/build/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R1
**Why:** installers need an icon.
**Steps:**
1. Design a 1024×1024 PNG icon (simple: a node graph inside a rounded square) with any free tool; save as `desktop/build/icon.png`.
2. `README.md`: "icon.png must be 1024×1024 PNG; electron-builder generates platform icons from it."
**Verify:** the file is a 1024×1024 PNG.

#### P1-REL-002 — electron-builder configuration
**Files:** `desktop/electron-builder.yml` (create)
**Refs:** R4, R8
**Why:** produce installers that include `pv-engine`.
**Steps:**
1. Create exactly:
```yaml
appId: com.projectvisualizer.app
productName: Project Visualizer
directories:
  output: release
  buildResources: build
files:
  - out/**
  - package.json
asar: true
win:
  target: nsis
  extraResources:
    - from: ../engine/build/app/Release/pv-engine.exe
      to: engine/pv-engine.exe
nsis:
  oneClick: false
  allowToChangeInstallationDirectory: true
mac:
  target: dmg
  category: public.app-category.developer-tools
  extraResources:
    - from: ../engine/build-release/app/pv-engine
      to: engine/pv-engine
linux:
  target: AppImage
  category: Development
  extraResources:
    - from: ../engine/build-release/app/pv-engine
      to: engine/pv-engine
publish:
```

### MODULE P2-DEPS — Dependency navigation engine
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/deps/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-SIGN
- **Goal:** neighbors (forward/reverse, multi-level), paths between nodes, and cycles (strongly connected components) at any abstraction level.

#### P2-DEPS-001 — Neighbors
**Files:** `engine/modules/deps/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/include/pv/deps/deps.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/src/neighbors.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/tests/neighbors_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R9
**Why:** "what does this use / who uses this, N steps away".
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME deps DEPS pv_session TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `deps.hpp` (namespace `pv::deps`) — declare the whole module:
```cpp
struct NeighborItem { std::string node_id; int distance = 0; std::string direction; std::vector<std::string> ancestor_ids; };
struct NeighborsResult { std::string root_id; std::vector<NeighborItem> items; std::vector<core::Edge> edges; };
struct PathResult { bool found = false; std::vector<std::string> node_ids; std::vector<std::string> edge_ids; };

NeighborsResult neighbors(const graph::Graph& g, const std::string& node_id, const std::string& direction,
                          int depth, const std::vector<core::EdgeKind>& kinds);
PathResult find_path(const graph::Graph& g, const std::string& from_id, const std::string& to_id,
                     const std::vector<core::EdgeKind>& kinds, int max_depth);
std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> find_cycles(const graph::Graph& g, int level, int limit);
nlohmann::json to_json(const NeighborsResult& r);
nlohmann::json to_json(const PathResult& r);
```
3. Implement `neighbors` (other functions: temporary `Unsupported` bodies):
   - `g.node(node_id)` (throws if missing); `depth` clamp 1–5; `direction` must be `in`, `out` or `both` (else `PvError(err::InvalidParams, "bad direction")`).
   - Start set `S = {node_id} ∪ descendants(node_id)`.
   - For each requested direction d (`out` first, then `in` when `both`): `visited = S`; `frontier = sorted(S)`; for `k = 1..depth`: for each `cur` in frontier, for each edge of `cur` (out-edges for `out`, in-edges for `in`) sorted by id whose kind is in `kinds` (or any if empty): remember the edge (unique by id); `other` = target (out) or source (in); if not visited → add to visited, push item `{other, k, d, g.ancestors(other)}` and to `next`. Stop early when `next` is empty; `frontier = sorted(next)`.
   - Sort items by (distance, direction, node_id); edges by id.
4. Tests suite `DepsNeighbors` (graph sample from `../../graph/tests/sample_graph.hpp`): `function:main.py#main` `out` depth 1 → items `function:app/a.py#f`, `method:app/a.py#C.m` (distance 1), 2 edges; `out` depth 2 → same items, 3 edges; `in` depth 1 → no items; `module:app/a.py` `in` depth 1 → items `function:main.py#main` and `module:main.py`; kinds `{Imports}` for `module:app/a.py` `in` → only `module:main.py`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R DepsNeighbors` → all pass.

#### P2-DEPS-002 — Path between nodes
**Files:** `engine/modules/deps/src/path.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/tests/path_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** explain how one part reaches another.
**Steps:**
1. `find_path`: both nodes must exist; `max_depth` clamp 1–12. Start set `S = {from_id} ∪ descendants(from_id)`. BFS over out-edges (kind filter) in sorted order, remembering `parent[node] = (previous node, edge id)`. A node **matches** when it is not in `S` and (`node == to_id` or `g.is_descendant(node, to_id)`). On the first match, rebuild the path back to the start-set node: `node_ids` from start to match, `edge_ids` in the same order; `found = true`. No match within `max_depth` → `found = false`, empty lists.
2. Tests suite `DepsPath` (sample graph): `module:main.py` → `package:app` gives `node_ids {"function:main.py#main","function:app/a.py#f"}`, `edge_ids {"calls|function:main.py#main|function:app/a.py#f"}`; `package:app` → `module:main.py` → not found; unknown id → throws.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R DepsPath` → all pass.

#### P2-DEPS-003 — Cycles
**Files:** `engine/modules/deps/src/cycles.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/tests/cycles_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** circular dependencies are a classic architecture smell.
**Steps:**
1. `find_cycles(g, level, limit)`: level clamp 1–4, limit clamp 1–100.
   - Group map `grp(x)`: `a = g.ancestor_at_level(x, level)`; use it only if `a` exists and `g.node(a).level == level`.
   - Adjacency: for each edge of kind imports/calls/inherits with both groups defined and different: add `grp(source) → grp(target)` (unique).
   - Find strongly connected components with Tarjan's algorithm (iterative or recursive; nodes visited in sorted id order; neighbors in sorted order).
   - Keep components with ≥ 2 members; sort each component's ids; sort components by size desc, then first id; cut to `limit`.
2. Tests suite `DepsCycles`: build a graph in the test with modules `m:a.py`, `m:b.py`, `m:c.py`, `m:d.py` (use proper ids `module:a.py` …), a function in each, calls a→b, b→c, c→a (function to function), d→a → level 2 → exactly one cycle `{"module:a.py","module:b.py","module:c.py"}`; level 4 (functions) → the same cycle among the functions; a graph without cycles → empty.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R DepsCycles` → all pass.

#### P2-DEPS-004 — JSON and RPC methods
**Files:** `engine/modules/deps/src/json.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/deps/tests/deps_rpc_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** expose `deps.*`.
**Steps:**
1. `to_json(NeighborsResult)` → `{"root_id","items":[{"node_id","distance","direction","ancestor_ids"}],"edges":[…]}`; `to_json(PathResult)` → `{"found","node_ids","edge_ids"}`.
2. `pv_register_deps`: `deps.neighbors` (`direction` default `both`, `depth` default 1, `kinds` parsed like `graph.edges`), `deps.focus` (= neighbors with `both` and `depth = radius`, default 1), `deps.path` (`from_id`, `to_id` required, `max_depth` default 8), `deps.cycles` (`level` default 2, `limit` default 20) → `{"cycles":[{"node_ids":[…]}]}`.
3. Tests suite `DepsRpc` (TestEnv + `pyproj_small`): `deps.neighbors` of `function:app/utils.py#is_valid` with `in` → 3 items; `deps.path` from `module:main.py` to `package:app` → found; `deps.cycles` level 2 → `{"cycles":[]}`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R DepsRpc` → all pass.

**Steps:**

**Verify:** `grep -c "^## " engine/modules/deps/README.md` → `4`.

- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE

#### P2-LOCATE-001 — Locate functions
**Files:** `engine/modules/locate/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/locate/include/pv/locate/locate.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/locate/src/locate.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/locate/tests/locate_test.cpp` (create)

### MODULE P2-LGEN — Generic query-based language framework
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/lang_generic/**`
- **Starts after:** P1-SIGN
- **Goal:** extract definitions, imports, calls and inheritance for **any** tree-sitter language from four query strings with standard capture names, plus path-based helpers. Every new language reuses this.

**Standard capture names (the contract for every language's queries):**

| Query | Captures |
|---|---|
| definitions | the whole node as `@definition.class`, `@definition.interface`, `@definition.function` or `@definition.method`; its name node as `@name` |
| imports | `@import.module` (required, quotes/brackets stripped), optional `@import.name`, `@import.alias`, `@import.default` (default-import local name → name `default`), `@import.namespace` (namespace alias → name empty), `@import.wildcard` (sets name `*`), `@import.require_fn` (the match is kept only if its text equals the spec's `require_function`) |
| calls | `@call.name` (required), optional `@call.object` |
| inherits | `@inherit.class` (the class's **name** node), `@inherit.base` |

#### P2-LGEN-001 — Query spec and definitions extraction
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_generic/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_generic/include/pv/lang_generic/query_extractor.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_generic/src/query_extractor.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_generic/tests/definitions_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7, R8
**Why:** nesting and qualnames from containment, for any language.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME lang_generic DEPS pv_parse TEST_DEPS pv_tp_ts_python)`
2. `query_extractor.hpp` (namespace `pv::lang_generic`):
```cpp
struct QuerySpec {
    std::string language_id;
    const TSLanguage* language = nullptr;
    std::string definitions_query;
    std::string imports_query;     // may be empty
    std::string calls_query;       // may be empty
    std::string inherits_query;    // may be empty
    std::vector<std::string> decision_node_types;   // for complexity
    std::string require_function;  // e.g. "require"; empty = no require filtering
};
parse::FileExtraction extract_with_queries(const QuerySpec& spec, const std::string& rel_path, const std::string& source);
std::string strip_quotes(const std::string& text);   // removes surrounding "", '', ``, or <>
```
3. Implement `strip_quotes` and the **definitions part** of `extract_with_queries` (imports/calls/inherits come next tasks):
   1. `fx.file_path`, `fx.language = spec.language_id`, `fx.loc = count_lines`, parse with `TsParser(spec.language)`, `has_syntax_errors`.
   2. Run the definitions query (compile it with `parse::TsQuery` — compile each query once per call is acceptable). For each match: the definition node = the capture whose name starts with `definition.`; kind word = the part after the dot; name = text of `@name`.
   3. Collect `(start_byte, end_byte, kind word, name, node)`; sort by start asc, then end desc. Walk with a stack of open definitions (pop while the top's `end_byte <= current.start_byte`); parent = top of stack (or none).
   4. For each: `qualname = unique(parent ? parent.qualname + "." + name : name)` (same `~N` rule as Python); `kind` = `"class"` for class/interface, `"function"` for function/method; `parent_is_class` = parent exists and its kind is `"class"`; `span = node_span(node)`; `signature = first line (≤200 chars)`; `complexity` = 1 + number of descendant nodes whose type is in `decision_node_types`, not descending into nodes that are themselves definitions (compare start bytes with the definition list).
   5. Keep a private list of (start_byte, end_byte, qualname) and a map from the **name node** start byte to qualname (used by later tasks).
4. Tests suite `LangGenericDefs` using the **Python** grammar and this query: `(class_definition name: (identifier) @name) @definition.class (function_definition name: (identifier) @name) @definition.function`; source = fixture `app/models.py` (read via `PV_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR`) → qualnames `Base`, `Base.save`, `User`, `User.__init__`, `User.display`; `User.display` has complexity 2 with decision types `{"if_statement"}`; `strip_quotes("'./a'") == "./a"`, `strip_quotes("<stdio.h>") == "stdio.h"`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangGenericDefs` → all pass.

#### P2-LGEN-002 — Imports, calls and inheritance extraction
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_generic/src/query_extractor.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/lang_generic/tests/refs_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** complete the generic extraction.
**Steps:**
1. Helper `enclosing(byte)`: the qualname of the innermost definition whose byte range contains `byte`, or `""`.
2. Imports (if the query is not empty): per match: skip if `@import.require_fn` exists and its text ≠ `spec.require_function`; `module = strip_quotes(text(@import.module))`; `name` = text of `@import.name` if present; if `@import.default` → `alias = text`, `name = "default"`; if `@import.namespace` → `alias = text`, `name = ""`; if `@import.alias` → `alias = text`; if `@import.wildcard` → `name = "*"`; `line` = start line of the module capture; `scope_qualname = enclosing(start byte of the match's first capture)`.
3. Calls: per match: `name = text(@call.name)`; `object = text(@call.object)` (cut 200) if present; `line`; `caller_qualname = enclosing(start byte of @call.name)`.
4. Inherits: per match: `class_qualname` = qualname mapped from the `@inherit.class` node's start byte (skip if unknown); `base = text(@inherit.base)`; `line`.
5. Keep document order (matches arrive in order).
6. Tests suite `LangGenericRefs` (Python grammar, fixture `app/services.py`): imports query `(import_from_statement module_name: (_) @import.module name: (dotted_name) @import.name)` → 4 imports (`.models`/`User`, `.utils`/`normalize`, `.utils`/`is_valid`, `.`/`utils`); calls query `(call function: (identifier) @call.name) (call function: (attribute object: (_) @call.object attribute: (identifier) @call.name))` → 7 calls, the first `is_valid` with caller `UserService.get_user`; inherits on `app/models.py` with `(class_definition name: (identifier) @inherit.class superclasses: (argument_list (identifier) @inherit.base))` → one `(User, Base)`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangGenericRefs` → all pass.

#### P2-LGEN-003 — Path-based module helpers
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_generic/include/pv/lang_generic/path_modules.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_generic/src/path_modules.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_generic/tests/path_modules_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** JS/TS/C/C++ refer to files by path; Go by directory; these helpers are shared.
**Steps:**
1. Declare and implement (namespace `pv::lang_generic`):
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> path_module_names(const std::string& rel_path);   // "src/a/b.ts" -> {"src/a/b"}; "src/a/index.js" -> {"src/a/index","src/a"}
std::string resolve_relative_path(const std::string& importer_file, const std::string& spec,
                                  const std::vector<std::string>& strip_extensions); // "./x.js" from "src/a/m.js" -> "src/a/x"
std::string longest_suffix_module(const parse::ProjectIndex& index, const std::string& import_path); // module name m with import_path == m or ends with "/" + m; longest; "" if none
std::string external_package_name(const std::string& spec);  // "@scope/pkg/sub" -> "@scope/pkg"; "lodash/fp" -> "lodash"; "node:fs" -> "node:fs"
```
2. `resolve_relative_path`: `base = normalize_path(path_join(path_parent(importer), spec))`; if `base`'s extension (lower-case) is in `strip_extensions`, remove it; return `base`.
3. Tests suite `LangGenericPaths`: each example; `longest_suffix_module` with modules `internal/store` and `store` for import `github.com/acme/shop/internal/store` → `internal/store`.

#### P2-LJS-002 — Queries
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_javascript/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_javascript/include/pv/lang_javascript/queries.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_javascript/src/queries.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_javascript/tests/queries_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** the language knowledge, as data.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME lang_javascript DEPS pv_lang_generic pv_tp_ts_javascript pv_tp_ts_typescript pv_tp_ts_tsx pv_session)`
2. `queries.hpp` declares `extern const char* kJsDefinitions; kJsImports; kJsCalls; kJsInherits; kTsDefinitions; kTsInherits;` (TS reuses the JS imports and calls queries) and the three `extern "C"` language functions.
3. `queries.cpp` defines them as raw strings:
```text
kJsDefinitions:
(function_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @definition.function
(generator_function_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @definition.function
(class_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @definition.class
(method_definition name: (property_identifier) @name) @definition.method
(variable_declarator name: (identifier) @name value: [(arrow_function) (function_expression)]) @definition.function

kJsImports:
(import_statement (import_clause (identifier) @import.default) source: (string) @import.module)
(import_statement (import_clause (namespace_import (identifier) @import.namespace)) source: (string) @import.module)
(import_statement (import_clause (named_imports (import_specifier name: (identifier) @import.name alias: (identifier)? @import.alias))) source: (string) @import.module)
(variable_declarator name: (identifier) @import.alias value: (call_expression function: (identifier) @import.require_fn arguments: (arguments . (string) @import.module)))
(expression_statement (call_expression function: (identifier) @import.require_fn arguments: (arguments . (string) @import.module)))

kJsCalls:
(call_expression function: (identifier) @call.name)
(call_expression function: (member_expression object: (_) @call.object property: (property_identifier) @call.name))
(new_expression constructor: (identifier) @call.name)

kJsInherits:
(class_declaration name: (identifier) @inherit.class (class_heritage (identifier) @inherit.base))
(class_declaration name: (identifier) @inherit.class (class_heritage (member_expression) @inherit.base))

kTsDefinitions:
(function_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @definition.function
(generator_function_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @definition.function
(class_declaration name: (type_identifier) @name) @definition.class
(abstract_class_declaration name: (type_identifier) @name) @definition.class
(interface_declaration name: (type_identifier) @name) @definition.interface
(method_definition name: (property_identifier) @name) @definition.method
(variable_declarator name: (identifier) @name value: [(arrow_function) (function_expression)]) @definition.function

kTsInherits:
(class_declaration name: (type_identifier) @inherit.class (class_heritage (extends_clause value: (identifier) @inherit.base)))
(class_declaration name: (type_identifier) @inherit.class (class_heritage (implements_clause (type_identifier) @inherit.base)))
```
4. Test suite `LangJsQueries`: each query compiles with `parse::TsQuery` against its grammar (JS queries with JS; TS definitions/inherits and the JS imports/calls queries with both TS and TSX). **If a query does not compile, the exception gives the byte offset: open the grammar's `src/node-types.json` (in the CMake build `_deps` folder) to find the correct node or field name, fix only the query text, and mention the change in your answer.**
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangJsQueries` → all pass.

#### P2-LJS-003 — Module names and import resolution
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_javascript/include/pv/lang_javascript/resolve.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_javascript/src/resolve.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_javascript/tests/resolve_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** `./utils`, `../api/client`, `@/x`, `lodash`.
**Steps:**

Declare (namespace `pv::lang_javascript`): `inline const std::vector<std::string> kJsExtensions = {".js",".jsx",".mjs",".cjs",".ts",".tsx",".mts",".cts"};` and `parse::ImportTarget resolve_js_import(const parse::RawImport& imp, const std::string& importer_file, const parse::ProjectIndex& index);`
2. Rules for `spec = imp.module`:
   - Relative (`./`, `../`, `.` or `..`): `base = lang_generic::resolve_relative_path(importer, spec, kJsExtensions)`.
   - Alias `@/x` or `~/x`: try `"src/" + x` then `x` (strip known extensions).

   - Otherwise (bare): return `{"", lang_generic::external_package_name(spec)}`.
   - For a computed `base`: `file = index.file_for_module(base)`; missing → `{}`. If `imp.name` is not empty, not `default` and not `*`, and `index.symbol_id(file, imp.name)` exists → return it; else return the module node id of `file`.

Tests suite `LangJsResolve` with a hand-built index (module names from `lang_generic::path_module_names`): `./format.js` from `src/utils/x.js` with name `formatName` → function id; `./utils` (dir with `index.js`) → module `src/utils/index.js`; `../api/client` from `src/index.js`… → `{}` when missing; `lodash/fp` → external `lodash`; `@/utils/format` → resolved through `src/`.

#### P2-LJAVA-002 — Module names and resolution
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_java/src/resolve.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_java/tests/resolve_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** Java files map to dotted class names under source roots.
**Steps:**
1. `java_module_names(rel)`: remove `.java`; if the path contains `/java/` (e.g. `src/main/java/`), keep the part after the **last** `/java/`; else if it starts with `src/`, drop `src/`; replace `/` with `.` → `{name}`.
2. `resolve_java_import`: wildcard (`name == "*"`) → `{}` (no binding); module `m`: if `index.file_for_module(m)` → file `f`: last segment `s` of `m`; return `symbol_id(f, s)` if present else module id; else try `m` without its last segment the same way (static imports); else if the first segment is a project top-level → `{}`; else external: first two segments when the first is one of `com org net io`, otherwise the first segment.
3. Tests suite `LangJavaResolve`: `src/main/java/com/acme/App.java` → `com.acme.App`; import `com.acme.util.Helper` → class node; `java.util.List` → external `java`; `org.springframework.web.Bind` → external `org.springframework`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangJavaResolve` → all pass.

```text
kGoDefinitions:
(function_declaration name: (identifier) @name) @definition.function
(method_declaration name: (field_identifier) @name) @definition.method

kGoReceivers:
```
