4. Queries:
```text
kCDefinitions:
(function_definition declarator: (function_declarator declarator: (identifier) @name)) @definition.function
(function_definition declarator: (pointer_declarator declarator: (function_declarator declarator: (identifier) @name))) @definition.function
(struct_specifier name: (type_identifier) @name body: (field_declaration_list)) @definition.class

kCppDefinitions:
(function_definition declarator: (function_declarator declarator: (identifier) @name)) @definition.function
(function_definition declarator: (function_declarator declarator: (field_identifier) @name)) @definition.method
(function_definition declarator: (function_declarator declarator: (qualified_identifier) @name)) @definition.function
(function_definition declarator: (pointer_declarator declarator: (function_declarator declarator: (identifier) @name))) @definition.function
(function_definition declarator: (reference_declarator (function_declarator declarator: (identifier) @name))) @definition.function
(class_specifier name: (type_identifier) @name body: (field_declaration_list)) @definition.class
(struct_specifier name: (type_identifier) @name body: (field_declaration_list)) @definition.class

kIncludes (both):
(preproc_include path: (string_literal) @import.module)
(preproc_include path: (system_lib_string) @import.module)

kCCalls:
(call_expression function: (identifier) @call.name)
(call_expression function: (field_expression argument: (_) @call.object field: (field_identifier) @call.name))

kCppCalls: kCCalls plus
(call_expression function: (qualified_identifier scope: (_) @call.object name: (identifier) @call.name))

kCppInherits:
(class_specifier name: (type_identifier) @inherit.class (base_class_clause (type_identifier) @inherit.base))
(class_specifier name: (type_identifier) @inherit.class (base_class_clause (qualified_identifier) @inherit.base))
```
5. Test suite `LangCppQueries`: all compile (fix only query text if needed, using `node-types.json`).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangCppQueries` → pass.

#### P3-LCPP-002 — Include resolution
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_cpp/src/resolve.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_cpp/tests/resolve_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** connect files through `#include`.
**Steps:**
1. `resolve_include(imp, importer, index)`: `spec = imp.module` (already without quotes/brackets). If the original capture was a system include (`<…>` — the generic extractor strips the brackets, so treat as system when `index` has no match **and** the spec has no `/` and matches a known system header list `{stdio.h stdlib.h string.h math.h vector string map set memory iostream algorithm utility cstdio cstdlib cstring functional unordered_map unordered_set thread mutex chrono}`) → external name = spec without extension. Otherwise: candidate = `normalize_path(path_join(path_parent(importer), spec))` → `file_for_module(candidate)`; else `lang_generic::longest_suffix_module(index, spec)`; found → module node id; not found → `{}`.
2. Tests suite `LangCppResolve`: `"util.h"` from `src/shape.cpp` → `module:src/util.h`; `"inc/a.h"` found by suffix; `iostream` → external `iostream`; unknown quoted header → `{}`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangCppResolve` → all pass.

#### P3-LCPP-003 — Adapters with qualified-name post-processing
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_cpp/src/adapters.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_cpp/tests/adapters_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** `int Square::area()` is a method of `Square`.
**Steps:**
1. `CFamilyAdapter` (like `JsFamilyAdapter`) with self keyword `this`. `make_c_adapter()`: id `c`, extensions `{".c"}`, C grammar/queries, decision types `if_statement for_statement while_statement do_statement case_statement conditional_expression`. `make_cpp_adapter()`: id `cpp`, extensions `{".cpp",".cc",".cxx",".h",".hpp",".hh",".hxx",".ipp"}`, C++ grammar/queries (+ `catch_clause`).
2. C++ post-processing after extraction: for each definition whose `name` contains `::`: `cls` = text between the second-to-last `::` (or start) and the last `::`; `m` = after the last `::`; new qualname `cls + "." + m` (unique); if a class definition with qualname `cls` exists in the file → `parent_qualname = cls`, `parent_is_class = true`; update `name = m` and rewrite matching `caller_qualname`s.
3. Tests suite `LangCppAdapters`: source `class A { public: int f(); }; int A::f() { return g(); }` → definition `A.f` with parent `A`; the call `g` has caller `A.f`.

#### P3-LRUST-002 — Module names and resolution
**Files:** `engine/modules/lang_rust/src/resolve.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/lang_rust/tests/resolve_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** Rust module paths (`crate::a::b`).
**Steps:**
1. `rust_module_names(rel)`: path under `src/`: `src/main.rs` or `src/lib.rs` → `crate`; `src/a/mod.rs` → `crate::a`; `src/a/b.rs` → `crate::a::b`; files outside `src/` → path without extension with `/` → `::`.
2. `resolve_rust_import(imp, importer, index)`: `path = imp.module`. If it came from `mod x;` (the import has no `::` and the importer defines it as a child) → candidate `<importer module>::x` (importer module = first of `rust_module_names(importer)`; for `mod.rs`/`main.rs`/`lib.rs` the importer module itself; for `a.rs` its own path). Else: `self::…` → importer module + rest; `super::…` → parent module + rest; `crate::…` as is; other → try `crate::` + path. Then: if `file_for_module(path)` → module node; else split the last `::` segment as a symbol: `file_for_module(prefix)` + `symbol_id(file, last)` → symbol, or the module; else external = first segment.
3. Tests suite `LangRustResolve`: `crate::store::Store` → `class:src/store.rs#Store` (with index symbols set up); `mod store` from `src/main.rs` → `module:src/store.rs`; `std::collections::HashMap` → external `std`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R LangRustResolve` → all pass.

Then run `kRustImpls`: for each `(impl.type T, impl.fn f)`: find the definition named `f` whose span start line equals the capture's line; rename to `T.f` (unique), parent `T` if a definition `T` exists in the file (`parent_is_class = true`), rewrite callers. For each `(impl.trait Tr, impl.for T)`: add `RawInherit{T, Tr, line}`.
2. Imports post-processing: for `use a::b::C` (no alias, contains `::`): `module = a::b`, `name = C`; with an alias keep the alias.
3. Tests suite `LangRustAdapter`: an `impl Store { fn new() {} }` → `Store.new` with parent `Store`; `impl Countable for Store` → inherit `(Store, Countable)`.

```rust
pub trait Countable {
    fn count(&self) -> usize;
}

pub struct Store {
    items: Vec<String>,
}

impl Store {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Store { items: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn add(&mut self, item: &str) {
        if !item.is_empty() {
            self.items.push(item.to_string());
        }
    }
}

impl Countable for Store {
    fn count(&self) -> usize {
        self.items.len()
    }
}
```

### MODULE P3-AGPY — Python runtime agent
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** AGENT
- **Owns:** `agents/python/**`
- **Starts after:** P2-SIGN
- **Goal:** a zero-dependency Python 3.12+ package (`pv-agent`) that records function calls in project files with `sys.monitoring`, HTTP requests (WSGI/ASGI), database queries (DB-API), errors and stalls, and sends batches to the desktop runtime hub (R12).

#### P3-AGPY-001 — Package skeleton and configuration
**Files:** `agents/python/pyproject.toml` (create) · `agents/python/uv.lock` (create) · `agents/python/pv_agent/__init__.py` (create) · `agents/python/pv_agent/config.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_config.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12, R14
**Why:** the package and its settings.
**Steps:**
1. `pyproject.toml`: `[project] name = "pv-agent"`, `version = "0.1.0"`, `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, `dependencies = []`, `description = "Project Visualizer runtime agent"`; `[build-system] requires = ["hatchling"]`, `build-backend = "hatchling.build"`; `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["pv_agent"]`; `[dependency-groups] dev = ["pytest>=8", "ruff>=0.6"]`. Run `uv sync` (creates `uv.lock`).
2. `config.py`: `@dataclass(frozen=True) class Config: url: str; token: str; project_root: str; service: str; sample_rate: float; stall_ms: int; max_queue: int; flush_ms: int` and `def load_config(env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> Config | None` reading `PV_RUNTIME_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:47100`), `PV_RUNTIME_TOKEN` (missing → return `None`), `PV_PROJECT_ROOT` (default `os.getcwd()`, made absolute and normalized with forward slashes), `PV_SERVICE` (default basename of `sys.argv[0]` or `python`), `PV_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default 1.0), `PV_STALL_MS` (5000), `PV_MAX_QUEUE` (20000), `PV_FLUSH_MS` (200). Invalid numbers → defaults.
3. `__init__.py`: `__version__ = "0.1.0"` (start/stop come later).
4. Tests: defaults; missing token → None; bad sample rate → 1.0.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q` → pass.

#### P3-AGPY-002 — Ids and transport
**Files:** `agents/python/pv_agent/ids.py` (create) · `agents/python/pv_agent/transport.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_transport.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** send events in the background without slowing the app.
**Steps:**
1. `ids.py`: `new_trace_id()` = 32 hex chars, `new_span_id()` = 16 hex chars (`os.urandom(...).hex()`), `new_event_id()` = `uuid.uuid4().hex`, `now_ns()` = `time.time_ns()`.
2. `transport.py`: `class Transport: def __init__(self, config, sender=None)`; `emit(event: dict)` appends to a `collections.deque(maxlen=config.max_queue)` (oldest dropped, count `dropped`); a daemon thread wakes every `flush_ms` and sends batches of ≤ 1000 events as `{"source": {"agent": "python", "version": __version__, "service": config.service, "project_root": config.project_root}, "events": [...]}`; default `sender` = `urllib.request` POST to `config.url + "/v1/events"` with headers `Content-Type: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, timeout 2 s; failures increment `failed` and drop the batch (never raise into the app); `flush()` sends everything now; `close()` stops the thread after a final flush.
3. Tests with a fake sender: 2,500 events → 3 batches; queue overflow counts dropped; sender exception does not propagate.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q tests/test_transport.py` → pass.

#### P3-AGPY-003 — Trace context and span stacks
**Files:** `agents/python/pv_agent/context.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_context.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** parent/child spans and trace ids across calls and threads.
**Steps:**
1. `class Span: __slots__ = ("trace_id","span_id","parent_span_id","name","file_path","line","start_ns","error")`. Per-thread stacks: `_stacks: dict[int, list[Span]]` (thread ident → stack) guarded by a lock only when creating a thread's list; `current_stack()`; `push(span)`, `pop()`; `current_trace_id()` = top of stack's trace or `None`; a `contextvars.ContextVar("pv_trace_id", default=None)` lets middleware force a trace id for a request (`set_request_trace(trace_id)` / `reset_request_trace(token)`); `snapshot_open_spans()` → list of `(thread_ident, span)` for the innermost span of every thread (used by the watchdog).
2. Tests: push/pop across 2 threads keep separate stacks; request trace id is used for a new root span.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q tests/test_context.py` → pass.

#### P3-AGPY-004 — Function tracer with sys.monitoring
**Files:** `agents/python/pv_agent/tracer.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_tracer.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** record calls of project functions only, with low overhead.
**Steps:**
1. `class Tracer: def __init__(self, config, emit)`; `start()`: pick a free tool id among `sys.monitoring.PROFILER_ID` (2), 3, 4 (`sys.monitoring.get_tool(i) is None`), `use_tool_id(i, "pv_agent")`, register callbacks for `PY_START`, `PY_RETURN`, `PY_UNWIND`, `set_events(i, PY_START | PY_RETURN | PY_UNWIND)`; `stop()` frees the tool id.
2. `_in_project(code)`: cache per `code.co_filename` → normalized path starts with `config.project_root + "/"` and does not contain `/site-packages/` or `/.venv/` or the agent's own folder.
3. `PY_START(code, offset)`: not in project → `return sys.monitoring.DISABLE`; root span (empty stack): sampling (`random.random() < sample_rate`, remembered per trace; unsampled → push a marker span with `trace_id=None`); push `Span(trace_id=request trace or new_trace_id(), span_id=new_span_id(), parent=top.span_id or None, name=code.co_qualname, file_path=code.co_filename, line=code.co_firstlineno, start=now_ns())`.
4. `PY_RETURN(code, offset, retval)`: not in project → `DISABLE`; pop; if sampled emit `{"v":1,"event_id":…,"trace_id","span_id","parent_span_id","kind":"call","name":module + "." + qualname,"file_path","line","start_ns","duration_ns":now-start,"status":"ok","error":None,"attrs":{},"service","pid","thread"}` (module = `code.co_filename` relative to root with `/` → `.` and without `.py`).
5. `PY_UNWIND(code, offset, exc)`: if in project: pop; emit with `status "error"` and `error {type, message, stack: "".join(traceback.format_exception(exc))[:16384]}`.
6. Tests: create a temp project folder with a module defining `a()` calling `b()`; set `project_root` to it; start the tracer with a list-collecting `emit`; import and call `a()` → 2 events with `b`'s `parent_span_id == a`'s `span_id`; a raising function produces `status "error"`; a stdlib call is not recorded; `stop()` releases the tool.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q tests/test_tracer.py` → pass.

#### P3-AGPY-005 — Stall watchdog
**Files:** `agents/python/pv_agent/watchdog.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_watchdog.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** detect where a program hangs.
**Steps:**
1. `class Watchdog(threading.Thread)` (daemon): every 1 s, for each innermost open span older than `stall_ms` and not yet reported (remember span ids), emit `{kind: "stall", name, file_path, line: <current line of that thread's innermost project frame from sys._current_frames()>, start_ns: span.start, duration_ns: now - start, status: "ok", …}`.
2. Test: `stall_ms = 200`; a thread running a project function that sleeps 1.5 s → at least one stall event with that function's file.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q tests/test_watchdog.py` → pass.

#### P3-AGPY-006 — WSGI and ASGI middleware
**Files:** `agents/python/pv_agent/web.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_web.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** one trace per HTTP request (Flask/Django = WSGI, FastAPI/Starlette = ASGI).
**Steps:**
1. `class PvWsgiMiddleware: __init__(self, app, emit)`; `__call__(environ, start_response)`: new trace id → `set_request_trace`; wrap `start_response` to capture the status code; time the call; emit `kind "http_in"`, `name = METHOD + " " + PATH_INFO`, attrs `http.method`, `http.route` (PATH_INFO), `http.status_code`; status `error` for 5xx or exceptions (re-raise); reset the trace var.
2. `class PvAsgiMiddleware` for `scope["type"] == "http"` wrapping `send` to read `http.response.start` status; other scope types pass through.
3. Tests with a tiny WSGI app (`wsgiref.util.setup_testing_defaults`) and a tiny ASGI app driven by `asyncio.run` with fake receive/send.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q tests/test_web.py` → pass.

#### P3-AGPY-007 — Database and error hooks
**Files:** `agents/python/pv_agent/dbapi.py` (create) · `agents/python/pv_agent/errors.py` (create) · `agents/python/tests/test_db_errors.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** see slow queries and crashes on the map.
**Steps:**
1. `dbapi.py`: `wrap_connection(conn, emit, project_root)` returns a proxy whose `cursor()` returns a cursor proxy; `execute`/`executemany` are timed and emit `kind "db_query"`, `name = first 60 chars of the SQL`, attrs `db.statement` (first 500 chars), `db.system` (module name of the connection class), `file_path`/`line` of the first caller frame inside `project_root` (walk `sys._getframe()`), errors re-raised with `status "error"`.
2. `errors.py`: `install(emit, project_root)` sets `sys.excepthook` and `threading.excepthook` (calling the previous hooks) to emit `kind "error"` with the stack and the innermost project frame's file/line; `uninstall()`.
3. Tests with `sqlite3` in memory; a raised exception in a thread produces an error event.
**Verify:** `cd agents/python && uv run pytest -q tests/test_db_errors.py` → pass.

#### P3-AGNODE-002 — HTTP tracing and errors
**Files:** `agents/node/src/http.ts` (create) · `agents/node/src/errors.ts` (create) · `agents/node/src/http.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** requests and crashes without code changes.
**Steps:**
1. `http.ts`: `instrumentHttp(emit)` subscribes with `diagnostics_channel.subscribe` to `http.server.request.start` (store start time on the request object with a `WeakMap`, new trace id, `AsyncLocalStorage` context) and `http.server.response.finish` (emit `http_in` with method, url path as route, status code, duration); `http.client.request.start` / `http.client.response.finish` → `http_out` with host and path. Return an unsubscribe function.
2. `errors.ts`: `installErrorHooks(emit, projectRoot)` on `process.on('uncaughtExceptionMonitor')` and `process.on('unhandledRejection')` → error event with `stack`; `file_path`/`line` = first stack frame whose path starts with `projectRoot` (parse `(path:line:col)`).

**Verify:** `cd agents/node && pnpm test` → pass.

### MODULE P3-DHUB — Desktop runtime hub (agent and OTLP receiver)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP
- **Owns:** `desktop/src/main/runtime/**` · `desktop/src/main/handlers/runtime.ts` · `desktop/src/main/handlers/runtime.test.ts`
- **Starts after:** P3-RTCORE
- **Goal:** receive events on `127.0.0.1:47100` (`/v1/events` and OTLP `/v1/traces`), authenticate with a token, and forward them to the engine for the active project.

#### P3-DHUB-001 — OTLP JSON conversion
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/runtime/otlp.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/runtime/otlp.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** accept any OpenTelemetry-instrumented application.
**Steps:**
1. `otlpToEvents(body: unknown, serviceFallback: string): RuntimeEventJson[]`: iterate `resourceSpans[].scopeSpans[].spans[]`; `service` = resource attribute `service.name` or fallback; each span → `{v:1, event_id: span.spanId + '-' + span.startTimeUnixNano, trace_id: traceId, span_id: spanId, parent_span_id: parentSpanId || null, kind, name, file_path: attr('code.filepath') ?? '', line: Number(attr('code.lineno') ?? 0), start_ns: Number(BigInt(startTimeUnixNano)), duration_ns: Number(BigInt(end) - BigInt(start)), status: status?.code === 2 ? 'error' : 'ok', error: status?.code === 2 ? {type: 'Error', message: status.message ?? '', stack: ''} : null, attrs: <string/number/boolean attributes, max 30>, service}`; `kind`: span kind 2 (SERVER) → `http_in` when an `http.method`/`http.request.method` attribute exists; 3 (CLIENT) → `http_out`, or `db_query` if `db.system` exists; otherwise `call`. Attribute values come in OTLP form `{stringValue|intValue|boolValue|doubleValue}`. `traceId`/`spanId` may be hex (OTLP JSON uses hex strings).
2. Tests with a realistic OTLP JSON sample (2 spans, one SERVER with http attributes, one internal with code attributes).
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/otlp.test.ts` → pass.

#### P3-DHUB-002 — Batch validation
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/runtime/batch.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/runtime/batch.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** never forward garbage to the engine.
**Steps:**
1. `validateBatch(body: unknown): { source: {...}; events: RuntimeEventJson[]; rejected: number }` — `events` must be an array ≤ 5000; each event must have `v === 1`, string `event_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`, `kind` in the R12 list, string `name`, integer `start_ns ≥ 0`; invalid events are counted in `rejected` and skipped; missing `source` → `{agent:'unknown', version:'', service:'', project_root:''}`.
2. Tests: good, mixed, and oversize batches.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/batch.test.ts` → pass.

#### P3-DHUB-003 — Hub HTTP server
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/runtime/hub-server.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/runtime/hub-server.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R12, R15
**Why:** the local endpoint agents send to (SEC-05).
**Steps:**
1. `class HubServer { constructor(opts: { token: () => string; onEvents(source: BatchSource, events: RuntimeEventJson[]): void; port?: number }); start(): Promise<number>; stop(): Promise<void>; stats(): { received: number; rejected: number; unauthorized: number } }` using `node:http`, bound to `127.0.0.1`, default port 47100 (if busy, try up to 47109).
2. Routes: `GET /healthz` → `{"ok":true}` (no auth); `POST /v1/events` and `POST /v1/traces`: require header `authorization: Bearer <token>` (else 401 and count); body limit 5 MB (else 413); JSON parse (else 400); `/v1/events` → `validateBatch`; `/v1/traces` → `otlpToEvents` (service fallback `otlp`); call `onEvents`; respond `{"accepted": n}`. Any other path → 404.
3. Tests with a real server on a random port using `fetch`: 401 without token; 200 with token and the callback receives events; OTLP path works; 413 for a 6 MB body.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/hub-server.test.ts` → all pass.

#### P3-DHUB-004 — Forwarder to the engine
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/runtime/forwarder.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/runtime/forwarder.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** batch events to `runtime.ingest` for the active project.
**Steps:**
1. `class Forwarder { constructor(engine: { request(m: string, p: unknown): Promise<unknown> }, setTimer = setInterval); setActiveProject(projectId: string | null, root: string | null); push(source, events); stats(): { forwarded; dropped_no_project; dropped_other_root; errors } ; stop() }`: every 200 ms send queued events in chunks of 500 with `runtime.ingest {project_id, events}`; with no active project, drop (count); if `source.project_root` is set and does not match the active root (normalize slashes, case-insensitive on Windows), drop (count `dropped_other_root`); engine errors counted, never thrown. Queue max 50,000 (drop oldest).
2. Tests with a fake engine and fake timer.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/forwarder.test.ts` → pass.

#### P3-DHUB-005 — Runtime IPC handler
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/handlers/runtime.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/handlers/runtime.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R10
**Why:** start the hub with the app; tell the renderer how to connect agents.
**Steps:**
1. `register(ctx)`: token = setting `runtime.token` (generate 32 hex if missing); `Forwarder(ctx.engine)`; `HubServer({ token: () => current token, onEvents: (s, e) => forwarder.push(s, e) })` started (errors logged); on `before-quit` stop both.
2. Channels: `pv:runtime.setActiveProject {project_id, root}` (null values allowed); `pv:runtime.hubInfo` → `{url: 'http://127.0.0.1:' + port, token, running, ...server.stats(), ...forwarder.stats()}`; `pv:runtime.regenerateToken` → new token saved and returned.
3. Tests with mocked hub/forwarder classes and a fake context.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/handlers/runtime.test.ts` → pass.

### MODULE P3-DERR — Errors UI (paste-an-error and runtime errors)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP
- **Owns:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/errors/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-ERRMAP · P3-DRT
- **Goal:** paste a stack trace and see where it happened; list runtime errors; plain-language basics from a built-in dictionary (the "plain language error translation foundation"; AI explanations come in Phase 4) (US-16).

#### P3-DERR-001 — API, dictionary and basic explanations
**Files:** `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/errors/errors-api.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/errors/dictionary.json` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/errors/explain-basic.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/errors/explain-basic.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** instant, offline, plain-language hints.
**Steps:**
1. API: `mapStack(pid, text)`, `listErrors(pid)`, `clearErrors(pid, id?)`.
2. `dictionary.json`: object keyed `"<language>:<ErrorType>"` → `{ "title": "...", "plain": "...", "causes": ["...", "..."] }`. Include at least: python — `KeyError`, `IndexError`, `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `ValueError`, `NameError`, `ImportError`, `ModuleNotFoundError`, `ZeroDivisionError`, `FileNotFoundError`, `RecursionError`, `AssertionError`; javascript — `TypeError`, `ReferenceError`, `RangeError`, `SyntaxError`; java — `java.lang.NullPointerException`, `java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, `java.lang.ClassCastException`, `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException`, `java.lang.IllegalStateException`; go — `panic`; csharp — `System.NullReferenceException`, `System.ArgumentException`, `System.InvalidOperationException`, `System.IndexOutOfRangeException`. Write each `plain` in one or two simple sentences (e.g. KeyError: "The code asked a dictionary for a key that is not in it.").
3. `explainBasic(language, type)` → entry or a generic `{title: type, plain: 'The program stopped because of an error of type ' + type + '.', causes: []}`.
4. Tests: known and unknown lookups; every dictionary entry has the 3 fields.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/features/errors/explain-basic.test.ts` → pass.

Store: `errors`, `selected`, `refresh()` (`listErrors`), `select(error)` (ancestors via `getAncestors` → overlay `error`; `revealNode(origin)`), `paste(text)` (`mapStack` → refresh → select), `clear()`; `startErrorsWatcher()` refreshes (max once per 2 s) when a `runtime.update` notification carries errors.

**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/features/errors/errors-store.test.ts` → pass.

### MODULE P3-SRTAGG — Runtime aggregation service (team runtime metrics and alerts)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** SERVER
- **Owns:** `server/services/runtime-agg/**` · `server/db/migrations/0041_rtagg_alert_rules.sql` · `infra/compose/compose.runtime-agg.yml` · `infra/observability/prometheus/targets/runtime-agg.json`
- **Starts after:** P2-SIGN
- **Goal:** the new architecture's runtime aggregation: desktops upload per-node aggregates every 5 s (R12); the service stores them in TimescaleDB, serves time series for team dashboards and fires alerts. Replaces P3-SCOLL.

#### P3-SRTAGG-001 — Package, config and time-series schema
**Files:** `server/services/runtime-agg/package.json` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/pnpm-lock.yaml` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/tsconfig.json` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/.env.example` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/src/config.ts` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/migrations/0001_metrics.sql` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/src/migrate.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R13
**Why:** skeleton and the hypertables.
**Steps:**
1. Package `@pv/runtime-agg`; deps `fastify@5 zod@3 pg@8 ioredis@5 @pv/common @pv/db @pv/authz @pv/telemetry`. Config: `PV_RTAGG_PORT` (8105), `PV_PG_URL`, `PV_TSDB_URL`, `PV_REDIS_URL`, `PV_PROJECTS_URL`, `PV_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, JWT settings, `PV_RTAGG_RETENTION_DAYS` (30), `PV_OTLP_URL?`.
2. `0001_metrics.sql` (runs on TimescaleDB, not the main PostgreSQL):
```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS node_metrics (
  time timestamptz NOT NULL,
  project_id uuid NOT NULL,
  user_id uuid NOT NULL,
  node_id text NOT NULL,
  calls integer NOT NULL,
  errors integer NOT NULL,
  error_rate real NOT NULL,
  p95_ms real NOT NULL,
  state text NOT NULL
);
SELECT create_hypertable('node_metrics', 'time', if_not_exists => TRUE);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS node_metrics_project_node_idx ON node_metrics (project_id, node_id, time DESC);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS error_counts (
  time timestamptz NOT NULL,
  project_id uuid NOT NULL,
  node_id text NOT NULL,
  type text NOT NULL,
  count integer NOT NULL
);
SELECT create_hypertable('error_counts', 'time', if_not_exists => TRUE);
```
3. `migrate.ts`: applies files in `migrations/` in name order once (table `rtagg_migrations(name text primary key)`), then `add_retention_policy` for both tables with `PV_RTAGG_RETENTION_DAYS`.
**Verify:** typecheck passes; with the compose stack running, `pnpm tsx src/migrate.ts` twice → second run applies nothing.

#### P3-SRTAGG-002 — Metrics store
**Files:** `server/services/runtime-agg/src/store.ts` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/src/upload.ts` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/src/store.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R12, R13
**Why:** write uploads; read series and top lists.
**Steps:**
1. `upload.ts`: zod schema of the R12 upload body (`nodes` ≤ 2000, `errors` ≤ 500, `window_ms` 1000–60000).
2. `interface MetricsStore { write(projectId, userId, body): Promise<number>; series(projectId, nodeId, fromMs, toMs, bucketS): Promise<{t: number; calls: number; errors: number; p95_ms: number}[]>; top(projectId, fromMs, limit, by: 'calls'|'errors'|'p95_ms'): Promise<{node_id: string; calls: number; errors: number; p95_ms: number}[]> }` + `TimescaleStore` (`time_bucket`, one multi-row INSERT per upload) + `MemoryStore`.
3. Tests on `MemoryStore`: two uploads → series has two buckets; top ordered by errors.
**Verify:** `cd server/services/runtime-agg && pnpm test` → pass.

#### P3-SRTAGG-003 — Alert engine
**Files:** `server/services/runtime-agg/src/alerts.ts` (create) · `server/db/migrations/0041_rtagg_alert_rules.sql` (create) · `server/services/runtime-agg/src/alerts.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R13
**Why:** tell the team when a part of the app starts failing or slowing down.
**Steps:**
1. Migration (main PostgreSQL): `alert_rules (id uuid PK default gen_random_uuid(), project_id uuid not null, node_id text null, metric text not null check (metric in ('error_rate','p95_ms','calls')), op text not null check (op in ('>','<')), threshold real not null, window_s integer not null default 300, created_by uuid not null, created_at timestamptz not null default now())`.
2. `AlertEngine.evaluate(projectId, nowMs)`: for each rule, compute the metric over `window_s` from the store (null `node_id` = worst node); state machine per rule ok → firing → ok; on each transition to firing publish `{type:'runtime.alert', project_id, rule_id, node_id, metric, value, threshold}` to `pv:notify:<project_id>`; cooldown 5 min per rule. Called after each write (at most once per 5 s per project).
3. Tests with the memory store and a fake publisher: firing once, cooldown respected, back to ok.
**Verify:** `cd server/services/runtime-agg && pnpm test` → pass.

### MODULE P3-DCIMP — Import from Git for a team (local analysis, shared map)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** DESKTOP
- **Owns:** `desktop/src/main/handlers/cloud-import.ts` · `desktop/src/main/handlers/cloud-import.test.ts` · `desktop/src/renderer/src/features/cloud-import/**`
- **Starts after:** P2-DCLOUD · P1-DGIT
- **Goal:** import a whole Git repository for a team in one step: clone it on this computer (P1-DGIT), analyze it with the local engine, then share the map to a team project (P2-DCLOUD). The new architecture keeps source code on the user's machine, so this replaces the cloud import (P3-SING, P3-SPW).

#### P3-DCIMP-001 — IPC handler
**Files:** `desktop/src/main/handlers/cloud-import.ts` (create) · `desktop/src/main/handlers/cloud-import.test.ts` (create)
**Refs:** R9, R10, R13
**Why:** clone, analyze and share in one job, with progress.
**Steps:**
1. Channel `pv:cloudImport.start {cloud_project_id, git_url, branch?, parent_dir?}` → returns `{job_id}` at once and runs the job: `validateGitUrl` and `cloneRepo` from `../git/git-clone` (P1-DGIT; default parent folder = the one P1-DGIT uses) → `engine.request('project.open', {root_path})` → poll `project.status` every 500 ms until `ready` (or `error`) → `engine.request('snapshot.export', {project_id})` → `CloudClient.uploadSnapshot(cloud_project_id, label, snapshot)` (label = repo folder name + date). Progress is sent with `ctx.send('pv:cloudImport.progress', {job_id, stage: 'clone'|'analyze'|'upload'|'done'|'failed', progress: 0–100, project_id?, snapshot_id?, error?})`.
2. `pv:cloudImport.status {job_id}` → the last progress object. Only one job at a time (a second start → error `busy`).
3. Tests with fakes for clone, engine and client: stages in order; a clone failure ends in `failed` with the message.
**Verify:** `cd desktop && pnpm vitest run src/main/handlers/cloud-import.test.ts` → pass.

### MODULE P3-RTE2E — Runtime end-to-end test
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** AGENT
- **Owns:** `tests/e2e-runtime/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-AGPY · P3-RTCORE · P3-HEALTH · P3-ERRMAP
- **Goal:** prove the chain Python agent → HTTP → engine mapping, health and errors works with real processes.

#### P3-RTE2E-001 — Sample app and forwarder
**Files:** `tests/e2e-runtime/sample_app/app.py` (create) · `tests/e2e-runtime/sample_app/shop/__init__.py` (create) · `tests/e2e-runtime/sample_app/shop/cart.py` (create) · `tests/e2e-runtime/forwarder.py` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** a tiny app with a normal path, an error and a slow call; a mini hub that forwards to the engine.
**Steps:**
1. `shop/__init__.py` empty. `shop/cart.py`: `def add(items, x): items.append(x); return len(items)`; `def total(items): return sum(items)`; `def broken(): return {}["missing"]`; `def slow(): import time; time.sleep(0.3); return 1`.
2. `app.py`: calls `add` 3 times, `total` once, `slow` once, then `try: broken() except KeyError: pass`, then finally calls `broken()` without catching (so the process exits with an error).
3. `forwarder.py`: starts `pv-engine` (path from argv) with stdio pipes (framing helpers like `engine/app/smoke_test.py`), opens the project `tests/e2e-runtime/sample_app`, waits for ready, runs an `http.server` on a free port accepting `POST /v1/events` (token `e2e`) and forwarding events with `runtime.ingest`; exposes helper `call(method, params)` for the test runner.
**Verify:** `python tests/e2e-runtime/sample_app/app.py` → ends with a `KeyError` traceback (expected).

#### P3-RTE2E-002 — Runner
**Files:** `tests/e2e-runtime/run_e2e.py` (create) · `tests/e2e-runtime/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R14
**Why:** one command for the whole chain.
**Steps:**
1. `run_e2e.py <engine-path>`: start the forwarder (in-process thread); run the sample app with `python -m pv_agent run tests/e2e-runtime/sample_app/app.py` and env `PV_RUNTIME_URL`, `PV_RUNTIME_TOKEN=e2e`, `PV_PROJECT_ROOT=<abs sample_app>`, `PYTHONPATH=agents/python`; wait for it to exit; sleep 1 s; then assert via the engine: `runtime.status.events_total >= 6`; `health.get` shows `function:shop/cart.py#broken` with state `error`; `errors.list` has an error whose `origin_node_id` is `function:shop/cart.py#broken`; `runtime.recent_traces` is not empty. Print `E2E RUNTIME OK`; exit non-zero on any failure (the forwarder must register the `health`/`errmap` modules — they are part of `pv-engine` already).
2. README: prerequisites (engine built, `uv` for the agent) and command.
**Verify:** `python tests/e2e-runtime/run_e2e.py engine/build/app/Debug/pv-engine.exe` → `E2E RUNTIME OK`.

# PHASE 4 — AI DEBUGGING VISUALIZATION AND IMPACT ANALYSIS

**Mission:** explain errors in plain language grounded in the twin, detect when a fix works and clear the error live, preview the impact of a change with a risk score (static + runtime evidence), answer questions about the codebase, give AI coding agents the map through MCP, and open the engine to any language through plugins. Adds the Python AI service and the AI gateway **[ARCH-DEPENDENT]**. New architecture (2026-09-26): the engine becomes a local server (named pipe + TCP 7700), gains a local cache, a native file watcher and engine-side layouts, and the desktop gets React Flow / React Three Fiber views.

### Phase 4 wave table

| Wave | Modules (parallel inside a wave) |
|---|---|
| 1 | P4-CRPC · P4-PROMPT · P4-AIDEPS · P4-PLUGIN · P4-EWATCH · P4-EIPC · P4-ECACHE · P4-DDEPS |
| 2 | P4-INCR · P4-CHANGE · P4-GROUND · P4-AIBASE · P4-LPACK · P4-ELAYOUT |
| 3 | P4-FIXSYNC · P4-MCP · P4-AIEXP · P4-AIERR · P4-AIQA · P4-AIEMB · P4-DRF2D · P4-DR3F |
| 4 | P4-SAIGW · P4-AIEVAL |
| 5 | P4-DAIM · P4-DFIX |
| 6 | P4-DERRAI · P4-DQA · P4-DCHANGE · P4-DMCP |
| 7 | P4-UDOC |
| 8 | P4-SIGN |

### MODULE P4-INCR — Incremental re-parse and live file sync
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/incremental/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-SIGN
- **Goal:** watch the project folder (polling), re-parse only changed files, rebuild links, swap the graph, and notify `graph.changed` (auto-fix detection foundation).

#### P4-INCR-001 — File states and diff
**Files:** `engine/modules/incremental/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/include/pv/incremental/incremental.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/src/states.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/tests/states_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** cheap change detection without OS-specific watchers.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME incremental DEPS pv_session TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `incremental.hpp` (namespace `pv::incremental`) — declare the module:
```cpp
struct FileState { int64_t mtime_ns = 0; std::uintmax_t size = 0; };
using StateMap = std::map<std::string, FileState>;   // rel path -> state
struct ChangeSet { std::vector<std::string> added, modified, removed; bool empty() const; };
struct GraphDiff { std::vector<std::string> added, removed, updated; };
using ExtractionMap = std::map<std::string, parse::FileExtraction>;
using ChangeListener = std::function<void(const std::string& project_id, const std::vector<std::string>& files_changed, const GraphDiff& diff)>;

StateMap scan_states(const std::string& root, const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters, const std::vector<std::string>& excludes);
ChangeSet diff_states(const StateMap& before, const StateMap& after);
graph::Graph rebuild_graph(const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters, const std::string& root, const ExtractionMap& extractions);
GraphDiff diff_graphs(const graph::Graph& before, const graph::Graph& after);

class IncrementalManager {
public:
    void start(std::shared_ptr<session::Project> project, const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters, rpc::Notifier& notifier, int interval_ms);
    void stop(const std::string& project_id);
    nlohmann::json status(const std::string& project_id) const;   // {watching, interval_ms, seeded, last_change_ms}
    std::vector<std::string> apply_changes(session::Project& project, const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters, rpc::Notifier& notifier, const ChangeSet& changes); // returns files changed; public for tests
    void seed(session::Project& project, const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters);   // full extraction into the cache
    void add_listener(ChangeListener listener);
    void stop_all();
    void reset_for_tests();
};
IncrementalManager& manager();
```
3. Implement `ChangeSet::empty`, `scan_states` (use `fs::discover_files` with the adapters' extensions and `excludes`; state from `std::filesystem::last_write_time` converted to nanoseconds since epoch and `file_size`) and `diff_states` (sorted outputs). Others: `Unsupported`.
4. Tests suite `IncrStates` (temp folder with `.py` files): modify one (write different content and bump mtime with `last_write_time`), add one, delete one → each list correct.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R IncrStates` → all pass.

#### P4-INCR-002 — Rebuild from extractions and graph diff
**Files:** `engine/modules/incremental/src/rebuild.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/tests/rebuild_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** re-linking everything is fast; only parsing is slow.
**Steps:**
1. `rebuild_graph`: rel files = keys; `builder::add_structure_nodes(g, root, files, language_of)` with `language_of(rel) = extractions.at(rel).language`; for each extraction with an adapter (`adapters.by_id(language)`) → `add_definition_nodes`; `index = builder::build_index(<values>, adapters)`; for each: `link_imports` → `link_calls` → `link_inherits`; `compute_metrics`.
2. `diff_graphs`: ids only in `after` → added; only in `before` → removed; in both but with different `span`, `metrics`, `name` or `parent_id` → updated. All sorted.
3. Tests suite `IncrRebuild` (fixture `pyproj_small`): extract all files with the Python adapter into a map; `rebuild_graph` → 25 nodes / 19 edges (same as the golden test); change `app/utils.py` extraction by removing `is_valid` → diff shows it removed and the callers' fan-out updated.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R IncrRebuild` → all pass.

#### P4-INCR-003 — Manager: seed, apply changes, notify
**Files:** `engine/modules/incremental/src/manager.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/tests/manager_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** keep the twin in sync with the code on disk.
**Steps:**
1. Per project state: `ExtractionMap cache`, `StateMap states`, `bool seeded`, `std::thread worker`, `std::atomic<bool> stop`, `int interval_ms`, `int64_t last_change_ms`, mutex.
2. `seed`: discover files, `builder::extract_all(...)` into the cache, `states = scan_states(...)`, `seeded = true`.
3. `apply_changes`: for added/modified: read + `adapter->extract` (adapter by extension) into the cache (errors → keep an empty extraction with the path and language); removed → erase; `after = rebuild_graph(...)`; copy `health` from the old graph for ids that still exist (read lock copy of the old graph first); `diff = diff_graphs(old, after)`; `project.replace_graph(after)`; update `set_build_info` from the cache (main guard and syntax error files); send `graph.changed` with `files_changed` = added + modified + removed and the diff; call listeners; return the files.
4. `start`: if already watching update the interval; else start a thread: `seed` (if needed), then loop every `interval_ms`: `after = scan_states`, `changes = diff_states(states, after)`, if not empty → `apply_changes` and `states = after`; exits when `stop`. `stop` joins. `stop_all` for shutdown.
5. Tests suite `IncrManager` (copy the fixture to a temp folder first, open it with TestEnv): `seed` then change `app/utils.py` (rename `is_valid` to `is_ok` in the file and in `routes.py`/`services.py`), call `apply_changes` directly with the change set → the graph now has `function:app/utils.py#is_ok`; a `graph.changed` notification was recorded; a node's health set before the change is preserved.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R IncrManager` → all pass.

#### P4-INCR-004 — RPC methods and README
**Files:** `engine/modules/incremental/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/tests/watch_rpc_test.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** the desktop turns live sync on and off.
**Steps:**
1. `pv_register_incremental`: `watch.start` (`interval_ms` default 1000, clamp 250–60000) → `manager().start(reg.projects.get_ready(id), reg.adapters, reg.notifier, interval)` → status; `watch.stop` → status; `watch.status` → status. (Excludes: none extra in Phase 4.)
2. Test suite `WatchRpc`: start on a temp copy of the fixture; write a new file `app/extra.py` with a function; poll `watch.status`/graph for up to 5 s → node `function:app/extra.py#<name>` exists; stop.
3. README: `## How it works` (polling, seed, re-parse changed files, full relink), `## Cost` (parsing only changed files), `## Limits` (1 s default delay; very large repos: raise the interval).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R WatchRpc` → pass.

#### P4-INCR-005 — Native watcher as the change source (new architecture)
**Files:** `engine/modules/incremental/CMakeLists.txt` (edit) · `engine/modules/incremental/include/pv/incremental/incremental.hpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/incremental/src/manager.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/incremental/src/register.cpp` (edit) · `engine/modules/incremental/tests/native_watch_test.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/incremental/README.md` (edit)
**Refs:** R8, R9
**Why:** the new architecture updates the map less than 100 ms after a save; 1 s polling is too slow.
**Needs:** P4-EWATCH
**Steps:**
1. Add `pv_fswatch` to DEPS. `IncrementalManager::start(project, interval_ms, mode)` with `mode` `auto` (default: native when `fswatch::create_watcher` succeeds, else poll), `native` (error `unsupported` when unavailable) or `poll` (old behaviour).
2. Native mode: watcher events (already debounced by `fswatch`) → the changed relative paths go straight to `apply_changes` (the hash check still ignores saves without changes); a `rescan` event runs one full `scan_states` diff. Polling still runs every 10 s as a safety net.
3. `status` adds `mode`; `watch.*` RPC accepts and returns `mode` (P4-CRPC-006).
4. Test (suite `IncrNativeWatch`): on a temp project, modify one file → `graph.changed` arrives; the test prints the measured delay and fails above 500 ms (the product target is < 100 ms; CI machines are slow).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R Incr` → all pass.

### MODULE P4-FIXSYNC — Auto-fix detection and live resolution sync
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/fixsync/**`
- **Starts after:** P4-INCR
- **Goal:** when a file with an erroring function changes, mark the error "fix pending"; confirm with successful runtime calls; remove resolved errors; detect regressions (US-18).

#### P4-FIXSYNC-001 — Fix tracker
**Files:** `engine/modules/fixsync/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/fixsync/include/pv/fixsync/fixsync.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fixsync/src/tracker.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fixsync/tests/tracker_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R12
**Why:** the state machine open → fix_pending → verified | regressed.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME fixsync DEPS pv_incremental pv_errmap TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `fixsync.hpp` (namespace `pv::fixsync`): `enum class FixState { Open, FixPending, Verified, Regressed };` `std::string to_string(FixState)` (`open`, `fix_pending`, `verified`, `regressed`); `struct FixItem { std::string error_id, node_id, file_path, key; FixState state = FixState::Open; int64_t changed_at_ms = 0; int ok_calls = 0; };` `class FixTracker { public: std::vector<FixItem> on_files_changed(const std::string& pid, const std::vector<errmap::ErrorRecord>& open_errors, const std::vector<std::string>& files, const graph::Graph& g, int64_t now_ms); std::vector<FixItem> on_runtime(const std::string& pid, const std::vector<runtime::MappedEvent>& batch, int64_t now_ms); std::vector<FixItem> list(const std::string& pid) const; void reset_for_tests(); };` `FixTracker& tracker();` `nlohmann::json to_json(const FixItem&);`
3. Rules: `on_files_changed`: for each open error whose origin node's `file_path` is in `files` (node looked up in `g`; `key` = `type|message|node`): create or update its item → `FixPending`, `changed_at_ms = now`, `ok_calls = 0`; return changed items. `on_runtime`: for events on a `FixPending` item's node: ok call → `ok_calls++`; at 3 → `Verified`; an error event with the same key → `Regressed`; return changed items.
4. Tests suite `FixTracker`: pending → verified after 3 ok calls; pending → regressed on the same error.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R FixTracker` → all pass.

#### P4-FIXSYNC-002 — Wiring, notifications and RPC
**Files:** `engine/modules/fixsync/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fixsync/tests/fixsync_rpc_test.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fixsync/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** connect the tracker to file changes, runtime and the error list.
**Steps:**
1. `pv_register_fixsync`: `incremental::manager().add_listener(...)` → `tracker().on_files_changed(pid, <errmap::store().list(pid) with source runtime or pasted>, files, graph under read lock, now)`; `runtime::hub().add_listener(...)` → `tracker().on_runtime(...)`; for each item that became `Verified` call `errmap::store().clear(pid, error_id)`; whenever items changed send `fixes.changed {project_id, items}`. Method `fixes.list`.
2. Test suite `FixsyncRpc`: simulate: add a pasted error on `is_valid`, call the incremental listener path by `apply_changes` on a modified `app/utils.py` → `fixes.list` shows `fix_pending`; ingest 3 ok events on `is_valid` → `verified` and `errors.list` no longer contains the error.
3. README: states diagram (text), rules, limits (needs runtime traffic to verify; without an agent the item stays pending).
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R FixsyncRpc` → pass.

### MODULE P4-CHANGE — Change impact preview with risk scoring
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/change/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-SIGN
- **Goal:** `change.preview`: impact of a specific change type, with a risk score combining static dependencies and runtime evidence (US-19).

#### P4-CHANGE-001 — Preview computation
**Files:** `engine/modules/change/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/change/include/pv/change/change.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/change/src/preview.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/change/tests/preview_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R7
**Why:** different changes carry different risk.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME change DEPS pv_impact pv_health TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `change.hpp` (namespace `pv::change`): `struct Change { std::string kind, node_id, new_name, new_parent_id; };` `Change change_from_json(const nlohmann::json&)` (kind validated); `double type_multiplier(const std::string& kind)` (`modify_body` 0.6, `change_signature` 1.0, `rename` 1.0, `move` 0.8, `delete` 1.3); `nlohmann::json preview(const graph::Graph& g, const Change& c, const std::map<std::string, health::HealthInfo>& health);`
3. `preview`: `r = impact::analyze_impact(g, c.node_id, 5)`; `static_score = r.risk.score`; `ran` = number of affected nodes with `health.calls > 0`; `unstable` = the root or any affected node has state warning/stalled/error; `runtime_bonus = min(20, 2*ran) + (unstable ? 10 : 0)`; `score = min(100, round(static_score * mult) + runtime_bonus)`; level thresholds as in P1-IMPACT; factors = impact's 3 factors + `"change type: <kind> (x<mult>)"` + (ran > 0 ? `"<ran> affected parts ran recently"`) + (unstable ? `"some affected parts are currently unhealthy"`). Result per P4-CRPC-002 (affected from `impact::to_json`).
4. Tests suite `ChangePreview` (fixture): rename `class:app/services.py#UserService` with no health → score 42, level medium; `modify_body` → round(42 × 0.6) = 25 → medium; `delete` → 55 → high; with health showing 2 affected nodes ran and one in error → +14 bonus.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R ChangePreview` → all pass.

### MODULE P4-MCP — MCP server for AI coding agents
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/mcp/**`
- **Starts after:** P4-GROUND
- **Goal:** `pv-engine mcp <root>` — a Model Context Protocol server (stdio) so agents like Claude Code or Cursor can ask for structure, dependencies and impact before editing (US-21).

#### P4-MCP-001 — MCP stdio transport and lifecycle
**Files:** `engine/modules/mcp/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/mcp/include/pv/mcp/mcp.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/mcp/src/server.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/mcp/tests/server_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** MCP uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio with **one JSON message per line** (no Content-Length headers).
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt` exactly: `pv_add_module(NAME mcp DEPS pv_grounding pv_deps pv_impact TEST_DEPS pv_lang_python)`
2. `mcp.hpp` (namespace `pv::mcp`): `using ToolFn = std::function<nlohmann::json(const nlohmann::json& args)>;` `struct Tool { std::string name, description; nlohmann::json input_schema; ToolFn fn; };` `class McpServer { public: McpServer(std::istream& in, std::ostream& out, std::vector<Tool> tools); int run(); nlohmann::json handle(const nlohmann::json& msg); };` `std::vector<Tool> make_tools(session::Project& project);` `int run_mcp_command(const std::vector<std::string>& args, const parse::AdapterRegistry& adapters);`
3. `handle`: `initialize` → `{"protocolVersion": <client's requested version if it is one of "2024-11-05","2025-03-26","2025-06-18", else "2025-06-18">, "capabilities": {"tools": {"listChanged": false}}, "serverInfo": {"name": "project-visualizer", "version": kEngineVersion}}`; notification `notifications/initialized` → no reply; `ping` → `{}`; `tools/list` → `{"tools": [{name, description, inputSchema}]}`; `tools/call {name, arguments}` → run the tool: success → `{"content":[{"type":"text","text": <result dumped as pretty JSON>}], "isError": false}`; tool exception → `{"content":[{"type":"text","text": <message>}], "isError": true}`; unknown method → JSON-RPC error -32601. `run`: read lines with `std::getline`; skip empty lines; parse; write each response as `dump()` + `\n` and flush; EOF → return 0.
4. Tests suite `McpServer` with a fake tool: initialize response version negotiation; tools/list lists the tool; tools/call returns text content; unknown tool → `isError` true.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R McpServer` → all pass.

#### P4-MCP-002 — Tools
**Files:** `engine/modules/mcp/src/tools.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/mcp/tests/tools_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9, R11
**Why:** the useful questions an agent asks before editing.
**Steps:**
1. `make_tools(project)` returns (each reads the graph under `project.read`):
   - `pv_overview` `{}` → `{digest}` (max 8000 chars).
   - `pv_search` `{query: string, kinds?: string[], limit?: integer}` → search hits.
   - `pv_node` `{node_id?: string, name?: string}` → by id, or the best search hit for `name` → `{node, source (max 6000 chars), children, callers, callees}` (reuse `context::build_context_pack`).
   - `pv_dependencies` `{node_id, direction?: "in"|"out"|"both", depth?: 1–3}` → `deps::neighbors` JSON.
   - `pv_impact` `{node_id, change_kind?: string}` → `impact::analyze_impact` JSON (risk included).
   - `pv_path` `{from_id, to_id}` → `deps::find_path` JSON.
   Each tool has a JSON Schema `inputSchema` (`type: object`, properties, required) and a one-sentence description written for an AI agent (e.g. `pv_impact`: "Before changing a function, class or file, call this to see everything that depends on it and a risk level.").
2. Tests suite `McpTools` (fixture loaded with a local ProjectManager + `NullNotifier`): each tool returns sensible output for `is_valid` / `UserService`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R McpTools` → all pass.

#### P4-MCP-003 — CLI command, README and agent setup guide
**Files:** `engine/modules/mcp/src/command.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/mcp/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/mcp/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** `pv-engine mcp <root>`.
**Steps:**
1. `run_mcp_command(args, adapters)`: `args[0]` = root (missing → usage to stderr, return 2); own `rpc::NullNotifier` + `session::ProjectManager`; open and wait (log progress to **stderr** only — stdout is the MCP channel); build tools; `McpServer(std::cin, std::cout, tools).run()`.
2. `pv_register_mcp`: `reg.cli.add("mcp", [&reg](const std::vector<std::string>& a) { return pv::mcp::run_mcp_command(a, reg.adapters); });`
3. README: `## What agents get` (tool list), `## Claude Code` (`claude mcp add project-visualizer -- <path-to-pv-engine> mcp <project-root>`), `## Cursor / other clients` (JSON config snippet: `{"mcpServers": {"project-visualizer": {"command": "<pv-engine>", "args": ["mcp", "<root>"]}}}`), `## Privacy` (everything runs locally).
4. Manual check: run `pv-engine mcp <fixture>` and paste `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}` + Enter → one JSON line response.
**Verify:** manual check shows the initialize result with `serverInfo.name == "project-visualizer"`.

### MODULE P4-PLUGIN — Dynamic language plugins
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/plugins/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-SIGN
- **Goal:** support **any** language without recompiling the engine: a folder with `language.json`, 4 query files and a compiled tree-sitter grammar (shared library) is loaded at startup.

#### P4-PLUGIN-001 — Manifest
**Files:** `engine/modules/plugins/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/plugins/include/pv/plugins/plugins.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/plugins/src/manifest.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/plugins/tests/manifest_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** a small, validated description of a language.
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
pv_add_module(NAME plugins DEPS pv_lang_generic pv_session ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS} TEST_DEPS pv_tp_ts_python)
if(PV_BUILD_TESTS)
  FetchContent_GetProperties(ts_python)
  add_library(pv_test_pygrammar SHARED ${ts_python_SOURCE_DIR}/src/parser.c ${ts_python_SOURCE_DIR}/src/scanner.c)
  target_include_directories(pv_test_pygrammar PRIVATE ${ts_python_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
  if(TARGET pv_plugins_tests)
    add_dependencies(pv_plugins_tests pv_test_pygrammar)
    target_compile_definitions(pv_plugins_tests PRIVATE PV_TEST_GRAMMAR_PATH="$<TARGET_FILE:pv_test_pygrammar>")
  endif()
endif()
```
2. `plugins.hpp` (namespace `pv::plugins`):
```cpp
struct Manifest {
    std::string id, library, symbol, module_naming, resolution, self_keyword, require_function, dir;
    std::vector<std::string> extensions, decision_node_types;
};
Manifest parse_manifest(const nlohmann::json& j, const std::string& dir);   // throws PvError(err::InvalidParams, reason)
class DynamicLibrary { public: explicit DynamicLibrary(const std::string& path); ~DynamicLibrary(); void* symbol(const std::string& name) const; private: void* handle_ = nullptr; };
class PluginAdapter : public parse::LanguageAdapter { /* see P4-PLUGIN-002 */ };
std::unique_ptr<parse::LanguageAdapter> load_plugin(const std::string& dir);
std::vector<std::string> plugin_roots();   // PV_LANG_PLUGINS_DIR (split by ';' on Windows, ':' elsewhere) or ~/.project-visualizer/languages
```
3. `parse_manifest` rules: `id` (lower-case letters, digits, `_`), `extensions` (non-empty, each starting with `.`), `library` (file name relative to `dir`, must exist), `symbol` (starts with `tree_sitter_`), `module_naming` ∈ `path dotted directory`, `resolution` ∈ `relative_path dotted suffix none`, optional `self_keyword` (default `this`), `require_function` (default empty), `decision_node_types` (default empty).
4. Tests suite `PluginManifest`: valid manifest; each invalid field rejected with a message naming the field.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R PluginManifest` → all pass.

#### P4-PLUGIN-002 — Dynamic loading and adapter
**Files:** `engine/modules/plugins/src/loader.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/plugins/tests/loader_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** turn a folder into a working language.
**Steps:**
1. `DynamicLibrary`: Windows `LoadLibraryW` (UTF-8 → wide) / `GetProcAddress` / `FreeLibrary`; POSIX `dlopen(RTLD_NOW)` / `dlsym` / `dlclose`; load failure → `PvError(err::Io, "cannot load library: <path>")`.
2. `PluginAdapter` holds the `DynamicLibrary` (keep it alive as long as the adapter), `Manifest`, and a `lang_generic::QuerySpec` (language pointer from calling the symbol; query texts read from `definitions.scm`, `imports.scm`, `calls.scm`, `inherits.scm` in the plugin dir — missing files → empty queries). `extract` → `extract_with_queries`; `module_names` by `module_naming` (`path` → `path_module_names`; `dotted` → path without extension with `/` → `.`; `directory` → parent folder); `resolve_import` by `resolution` (`relative_path` → like JavaScript: relative spec → `resolve_relative_path` + `file_for_module` (+ symbol when `name` set), bare → external; `dotted` → `file_for_module(module)` then symbol of the last segment, else external first segment; `suffix` → `longest_suffix_module` → `package:`/module id, else external; `none` → `{}`); `self_keyword` from the manifest.
3. `load_plugin(dir)`: read `dir/language.json`, parse, load, return the adapter.
4. Test suite `PluginLoader`: write a temp plugin folder: copy the test grammar library (`PV_TEST_GRAMMAR_PATH`) into it, `language.json` with id `pyplug`, extension `.pyx`, symbol `tree_sitter_python`, naming `dotted`, resolution `dotted`, and Python queries (`definitions.scm` with class/function definitions); `load_plugin` → `extract` of `"class A:\n    def f(self):\n        pass\n"` gives `A` and `A.f`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R PluginLoader` → pass.

#### P4-PLUGIN-003 — Startup registration, lang.list and README
**Files:** `engine/modules/plugins/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/plugins/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** plugins load automatically at engine start.
**Steps:**
1. `pv_register_plugins`: for each root in `plugin_roots()` that exists, for each sub-folder containing `language.json`: `try { reg.adapters.add(load_plugin(dir)); log_info("language plugin loaded: <id>"); } catch (const std::exception& e) { log_warn("language plugin skipped: <dir>: <what>"); }` (a plugin whose id or extension conflicts with a built-in language is skipped by the registry's Conflict error).
2. README: `## Folder layout`, `## language.json` (field table), `## Building a grammar library` (`npx tree-sitter-cli build --output <name>.dll|.so|.dylib` inside a grammar repository), `## Query captures` (link to `engine/modules/lang_generic/README.md`), `## Troubleshooting`.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev` → builds; starting `pv-engine` with `PV_LANG_PLUGINS_DIR` pointing to the test plugin prints `language plugin loaded: pyplug` on stderr.

#### P4-LPACK-002 — Ruby pack
**Files:** `engine/plugins/ruby/source.txt` (create) · `engine/plugins/ruby/language.json` (create) · `engine/plugins/ruby/definitions.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/ruby/imports.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/ruby/calls.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/ruby/inherits.scm` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** Ruby support as data.
**Steps:**
1. `source.txt`: `repo=https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-ruby`, `tag=v0.23.1`, `lib_name=ruby`.
2. `language.json`: `{"id":"ruby","extensions":[".rb"],"library":"ruby.dll","symbol":"tree_sitter_ruby","module_naming":"path","resolution":"relative_path","self_keyword":"self","require_function":"require_relative","decision_node_types":["if","unless","while","until","for","when","rescue","conditional"]}` (the build script rewrites `library` for the OS).
3. Queries:
```text
definitions.scm:
(class name: (constant) @name) @definition.class
(module name: (constant) @name) @definition.class
(method name: (identifier) @name) @definition.method
(singleton_method name: (identifier) @name) @definition.method

imports.scm:
(call method: (identifier) @import.require_fn arguments: (argument_list (string (string_content) @import.module)))

calls.scm:
(call receiver: (_) @call.object method: (identifier) @call.name)
(call !receiver method: (identifier) @call.name)

inherits.scm:
(class name: (constant) @inherit.class superclass: (superclass (constant) @inherit.base))
```
**Verify:** the build script succeeds for Ruby and `pv-engine stats` on a small Ruby folder prints a module count.

#### P4-LPACK-003 — PHP pack
**Files:** `engine/plugins/php/source.txt` (create) · `engine/plugins/php/language.json` (create) · `engine/plugins/php/definitions.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/php/imports.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/php/calls.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/php/inherits.scm` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** PHP support as data.
**Steps:**
1. `source.txt`: `repo=https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php`, `tag=v0.23.11`, `subdir=php`, `lib_name=php`.
2. `language.json`: id `php`, extensions `[".php"]`, symbol `tree_sitter_php`, naming `directory`, resolution `suffix`, self `$this` (PHP writes the object as `$this`, so calls on it only resolve with that text), decision types `["if_statement","for_statement","foreach_statement","while_statement","catch_clause","conditional_expression","case_statement"]`.
3. Queries:
```text
definitions.scm:
(class_declaration name: (name) @name) @definition.class
(interface_declaration name: (name) @name) @definition.interface
(trait_declaration name: (name) @name) @definition.class
(method_declaration name: (name) @name) @definition.method
(function_definition name: (name) @name) @definition.function

imports.scm:
(namespace_use_clause (qualified_name) @import.module)

calls.scm:
(function_call_expression function: (name) @call.name)
(member_call_expression object: (_) @call.object name: (name) @call.name)
(scoped_call_expression scope: (_) @call.object name: (name) @call.name)

inherits.scm:
(class_declaration name: (name) @inherit.class (base_clause (name) @inherit.base))
(class_declaration name: (name) @inherit.class (class_interface_clause (name) @inherit.base))
```
**Verify:** the build script succeeds for PHP.

#### P4-LPACK-004 — Kotlin pack
**Files:** `engine/plugins/kotlin/source.txt` (create) · `engine/plugins/kotlin/language.json` (create) · `engine/plugins/kotlin/definitions.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/kotlin/imports.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/kotlin/calls.scm` (create) · `engine/plugins/kotlin/inherits.scm` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** Kotlin support as data.
**Steps:**
1. `source.txt`: `repo=https://github.com/fwcd/tree-sitter-kotlin`, `tag=0.3.8`, `lib_name=kotlin`.
2. `language.json`: id `kotlin`, extensions `[".kt",".kts"]`, symbol `tree_sitter_kotlin`, naming `dotted`, resolution `dotted`, self `this`, decision types `["if_expression","when_entry","for_statement","while_statement","catch_block"]`.
3. Queries (this grammar uses few field names, so patterns are positional):
```text
definitions.scm:
(class_declaration (type_identifier) @name) @definition.class
(object_declaration (type_identifier) @name) @definition.class
(function_declaration (simple_identifier) @name) @definition.function

imports.scm:
(import_header (identifier) @import.module)

calls.scm:
(call_expression (simple_identifier) @call.name)
(call_expression (navigation_expression (_) @call.object (navigation_suffix (simple_identifier) @call.name)))

inherits.scm:
(class_declaration (type_identifier) @inherit.class (delegation_specifier (user_type (type_identifier) @inherit.base)))
(class_declaration (type_identifier) @inherit.class (delegation_specifier (constructor_invocation (user_type (type_identifier) @inherit.base))))
```
(The second pattern covers `class A : B()`, where the grammar wraps the supertype in a constructor call.)
4. If the build script reports a query error, fix only the `.scm` text using the grammar's `src/node-types.json`.
**Verify:** the build script succeeds for Kotlin.

### MODULE P4-EWATCH — Native file watcher
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/fswatch/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-SIGN
- **Goal:** operating-system file change events (ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows, inotify on Linux, FSEvents on macOS) with debouncing, so saved files reach the engine at once (new architecture: "file system watcher → change detected").

#### P4-EWATCH-001 — Interface and Windows watcher
**Files:** `engine/modules/fswatch/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/fswatch/include/pv/fswatch/fswatch.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fswatch/src/watcher_win.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fswatch/src/factory.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fswatch/tests/fswatch_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R6, R8
**Why:** one small interface; Windows first (the main dev machine).
**Steps:**
1. `CMakeLists.txt`: `pv_add_module(NAME fswatch DEPS pv_core pv_fs)` (on macOS also link `-framework CoreServices`).
2. `fswatch.hpp`: `struct Change { enum class Kind { Modified, Created, Deleted, Rescan } kind; std::string rel_path; };` `class Watcher { public: virtual ~Watcher() = default; virtual void stop() = 0; };` `std::unique_ptr<Watcher> create_watcher(const std::string& root, const std::vector<std::string>& exclude_globs, std::function<void(std::vector<Change>)> on_changes, int debounce_ms = 30);` — returns nullptr when native watching is not possible.
3. `watcher_win.cpp` (only compiled on `_WIN32`): `ReadDirectoryChangesW` on the root with `bWatchSubtree = TRUE`, filters `FILE_NOTIFY_CHANGE_FILE_NAME | DIR_NAME | LAST_WRITE | SIZE`, overlapped I/O on a worker thread, 64 KB buffer; buffer overflow (`ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR`) → one `Rescan`. Paths converted to `/` and made relative.
4. `factory.cpp`: `create_watcher` picks the platform class; applies excludes (same matcher as `fs` discovery); debounces per path (collects events for `debounce_ms` after the last one, then calls `on_changes` once with the batch).
5. Test (suite `FsWatch`): temp tree; create, modify and delete a file → the three kinds arrive within 1 s; excluded folder ignored.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R FsWatch` → pass.

#### P4-EWATCH-002 — Linux and macOS watchers
**Files:** `engine/modules/fswatch/src/watcher_linux.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fswatch/src/watcher_mac.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/fswatch/README.md` (create)
**Refs:** R8
**Why:** the same behaviour on every desktop platform.
**Steps:**
1. Linux (`__linux__`): inotify with a watch per directory (walk the tree at start; add watches for new directories); mask `IN_CLOSE_WRITE | IN_CREATE | IN_DELETE | IN_MOVED_FROM | IN_MOVED_TO | IN_DELETE_SELF`; `IN_Q_OVERFLOW` → `Rescan`; the user watch limit reached → return nullptr (the caller falls back to polling).
2. macOS (`__APPLE__`): `FSEventStreamCreate` with `kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents`, latency 0.02 s, on a dispatch queue.

### MODULE P4-EIPC — Engine local server (named pipe, Unix socket, TCP 7700)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/ipc/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-SIGN · P1-RPC · P1-EAPP
- **Goal:** `pv-engine serve`: the new architecture's IPC bridge — the desktop connects over a named pipe / Unix socket and the VS Code extension over TCP 127.0.0.1:7700, both sharing one engine, its projects and its notifications (R9).

#### P4-EIPC-001 — Listeners
**Files:** `engine/modules/ipc/CMakeLists.txt` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/include/pv/ipc/listeners.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/src/listeners_win.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/src/listeners_posix.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/tests/listeners_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8, R9
**Why:** byte streams for each transport.
**Steps:**
1. `pv_add_module(NAME ipc DEPS pv_core pv_rpc pv_session)` (Windows: link `ws2_32`).
2. `listeners.hpp`: `class Listener { public: virtual ~Listener() = default; virtual std::unique_ptr<pv::rpc::ByteStream> accept() = 0; /* nullptr after close */ virtual void close() = 0; };` `std::unique_ptr<Listener> listen_pipe(const std::string& name);` `std::unique_ptr<Listener> listen_tcp(int first_port, int tries, int& chosen_port);` (binds `127.0.0.1` only; `chosen_port = 0` when all ports are busy).
3. Windows: named pipe `\\.\pipe\<name>` with `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS`, a security descriptor that allows only the current user, a new pipe instance per accepted client; Winsock TCP. POSIX: Unix socket in the path given (file mode 0600, stale file removed first); BSD sockets TCP.
4. Tests (suite `IpcListeners`): TCP listen on port 0-range, connect with a plain client socket, bytes echo; pipe/socket round-trip.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R IpcListeners` → pass.

#### P4-EIPC-002 — Engine info file and handshake
**Files:** `engine/modules/ipc/include/pv/ipc/engine_info.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/src/engine_info.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/tests/engine_info_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R9
**Why:** local tools find the engine and prove they are the same user.
**Steps:**
1. `std::string random_token();` (32 random bytes → 64 hex, from `std::random_device`); `std::string info_path();` (`$PV_HOME` or `~/.project-visualizer` + `/engine.json`); `void write_info(const EngineInfo&)` (write to a temp file and rename; on POSIX chmod 0600; on Windows the user profile folder is already private) and `void remove_info(int pid)` (only when the file still has our pid).
2. Gate for TCP connections: until `engine.hello` with the right token succeeds, every other request gets error `-32600` "call engine.hello first"; pipe/socket connections need no token (the OS already limits them to the user) but may call `engine.hello` to set their client kind.
3. Tests (suite `IpcInfo`): write/read/remove; wrong token rejected; right token accepted.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R IpcInfo` → pass.

#### P4-EIPC-003 — serve command, clients and editor relay
**Files:** `engine/modules/ipc/include/pv/ipc/server.hpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/src/server.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/src/register.cpp` (create) · `engine/modules/ipc/tests/server_test.cpp` (create)
**Refs:** R8, R9
**Why:** one engine, many clients.
**Steps:**
1. `class LocalServer { public: LocalServer(pv::session::Registry& reg); int run(const ServeOptions& opts); void stop(); std::vector<ClientInfo> clients() const; int broadcast(const std::string& method, const Json& params, int except_client, const std::string& only_kind = ""); };` — one accept thread per listener; one thread per connection running `pv::rpc::Connection` with a shared dispatch mutex; each connection is added to the fan-out notifier (`dynamic_cast<pv::rpc::FanoutNotifier*>(&reg.notifier)`) and removed when it closes.
2. `register.cpp`: CLI command `serve` with `--pipe <name>` (default `pv-engine-<user>`), `--tcp <port>` (default 7700, `0` = off, tries 10 ports), `--parent-pid <pid>` (checked every 2 s; the engine stops when that process is gone), `--stdio` (also serve stdin/stdout). Writes `engine.json` after listening, logs `pv-engine serving pipe=<name> tcp=<port>` to stderr, removes the file on exit. Methods: `engine.hello`, `engine.info`, `editor.reveal` (broadcast notification `editor.reveal` to all other clients → `{delivered}`), `editor.open` (notification `editor.open` only to clients whose kind is `vscode` → `{delivered}`). `engine.shutdown` and `request_shutdown` stop the server.
3. Tests (suite `IpcServer`): start a server on TCP with a test registry; two clients; `project.progress`-style notification reaches both; `editor.open` reaches only the `vscode` client.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --build --preset dev && ctest --preset dev -R Ipc` → all pass.

### MODULE P4-ECACHE — Local cache (SQLite + LevelDB)
- **Type:** CODE
- **Lane:** ENGINE
- **Owns:** `engine/modules/cache/**` · `engine/third_party/sqlite/**` · `engine/third_party/leveldb/**`
- **Starts after:** P3-SIGN · P1-BUILDR
- **Goal:** the new architecture's local cache: SQLite for project metadata and the AST (extraction) index, LevelDB for graph blobs and the layout cache, so reopening a project only parses changed files. (Takes over the SQLite library from P5-METRIC.)

#### P4-ECACHE-001 — SQLite library
**Files:** `engine/third_party/sqlite/CMakeLists.txt` (create)
**Refs:** R5
**Why:** a small embedded database (also used later by P5-METRIC).
**Steps:**
1. Create:
```cmake
FetchContent_Declare(sqlite
  URL https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-3460100.zip
  DOWNLOAD_EXTRACT_TIMESTAMP TRUE)
FetchContent_GetProperties(sqlite)
if(NOT sqlite_POPULATED)
  FetchContent_Populate(sqlite)
endif()
add_library(pv_tp_sqlite STATIC ${sqlite_SOURCE_DIR}/sqlite3.c)
target_include_directories(pv_tp_sqlite PUBLIC ${sqlite_SOURCE_DIR})
target_compile_definitions(pv_tp_sqlite PRIVATE SQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION)
set_target_properties(pv_tp_sqlite PROPERTIES C_STANDARD 11 POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
if(MSVC)
  target_compile_options(pv_tp_sqlite PRIVATE /W0)
else()
  target_compile_options(pv_tp_sqlite PRIVATE -w)
  find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
  target_link_libraries(pv_tp_sqlite PUBLIC Threads::Threads ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS})
endif()
```
2. If CMake warns that `FetchContent_Populate` is deprecated, that is acceptable (the archive has no CMake project). If it errors, replace the three `GetProperties/Populate` lines with `FetchContent_MakeAvailable(sqlite)` plus `SOURCE_SUBDIR pv_no_cmake` in the declare call.
**Verify:** `cd engine && cmake --preset dev && cmake --build --preset dev --target pv_tp_sqlite` → builds.
